תָּֽשֶׁת־חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וִ֣יהִי לָ֑יְלָה בּֽוֹ־תִ֝רְמֹ֗שׂ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־יָֽעַר׃
少壯獅子吼叫，要抓取獵物，向神尋求食物。
הַ֭כְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִ֣ים לַטָּ֑רֶף וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵאֵ֣ל אָכְלָֽם׃
太陽一出，牠們就退回去，躺臥在自己的洞穴裏。
תִּזְרַ֣ח הַ֭שֶּׁמֶשׁ יֵאָסֵפ֑וּן וְאֶל־מְ֝עוֹנֹתָ֗ם יִרְבָּצֽוּן׃
人出去做工，勞碌直到晚上。
יֵצֵ֣א אָדָ֣ם לְפָעֳל֑וֹ וְֽלַעֲבֹ֖דָת֣וֹ עֲדֵי־עָֽרֶב׃
耶和華啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地滿了你所造的。
מָֽה־רַבּ֬וּ מַעֲשֶׂ֨יךָ ׀ יְֽהוָ֗ה כֻּ֭לָּם בְּחָכְמָ֣ה עָשִׂ֑יתָ מָלְאָ֥ה הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ קִנְיָנֶֽךָ׃
那裏有海，又大又廣[^14]，其中有無數爬動的活物，大大小小的動物都有。
זֶ֤ה ׀ הַיָּ֥ם גָּדוֹל֮ וּרְחַ֢ב יָ֫דָ֥יִם שָֽׁם־רֶ֭מֶשׂ וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר חַיּ֥וֹת קְ֝טַנּ֗וֹת עִם־גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃
那裏有船隻往來，有你所造的利維坦[^15]在其中嬉戲[^16]。
שָׁ֭ם אֳנִיּ֣וֹת יְהַלֵּכ֑וּן לִ֝וְיָתָ֗ן זֶֽה־יָצַ֥רְתָּ לְשַֽׂחֶק־בּֽוֹ׃
這些都仰望你按時給牠們食物。
כֻּ֭לָּם אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּר֑וּן לָתֵ֖ת אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃
你給牠們，牠們便拾起來；你張開手，牠們就飽得美物。
תִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם יִלְקֹט֑וּן תִּפְתַּ֥ח יָֽ֝דְךָ֗ יִשְׂבְּע֥וּן טֽוֹב׃
你掩面，牠們就驚惶；你收回牠們的氣息，牠們就死亡，歸回塵土[^17]。
תַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנֶיךָ֮ יִֽבָּהֵ֫ל֥וּן תֹּסֵ֣ף ר֭וּחָם יִגְוָע֑וּן וְֽאֶל־עֲפָרָ֥ם יְשׁוּֽבוּ֥ן׃[t]
你發出你的靈[^18]，牠們就被造成；你使地面煥然一新。
תְּשַׁלַּ֣ח ר֭וּחֲךָ יִבָּרֵא֑וּן וּ֝תְחַדֵּ֗שׁ פְּנֵ֣י אֲדָמָֽה׃
願耶和華的榮耀存到永遠！願耶和華因他所造的歡喜！
יְהִ֤י כְב֣וֹד יְהוָ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֑ם יִשְׂמַ֖ח יְהוָ֣ה בְּמַעֲשָֽׂיו׃
他看地，地就震動；他摸山，山就冒煙。
הַמַּבִּ֣יט לָ֭אָרֶץ וַתִּרְעָ֑ד יִגַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃
我一生要向耶和華歌唱；我還活着的時候，要向我的神歌頌。
אָשִׁ֣ירָה לַיהוָ֣ה בְּחַיָּ֑י אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה לֵאלֹהַ֣י בְּעוֹדִֽי׃
願他喜悅我的默想；我要因耶和華歡喜。
יֶעֱרַ֣ב עָלָ֣יו שִׂיחִ֑י אָ֝נֹכִ֗י אֶשְׂמַ֥ח בַּיהוָֽה׃
願罪人從地上消滅，願惡人不再存在！我的心哪，你要稱頌耶和華！你們要讚美耶和華[^19]！
יִתַּ֤מּוּ חַטָּאִ֨ים ׀ מִן־הָאָ֡רֶץ וּרְשָׁעִ֤ים ׀ ע֤וֹד אֵינָ֗ם בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: 希伯來文 *nephesh*，生命、自己。第35節同。第104篇在希伯來文中沒有標題；七十士譯本加上標題「大衛的」。這篇與第103篇一樣，以「我的心哪，你要稱頌耶和華」開始和結束。
n.2: 耶和華：神的名字，希伯來文作 YHWH。
n.3: 第104篇頌讚神是創造和維持世界的主，大致依照創世記1章創造的次序：光和天（第2至4節），地和水（第5至9節），泉水、植物和動物（第10至18節），月亮和太陽（第19至23節），海和其中的活物（第25至26節）。許多學者把它與埃及的《阿頓頌》比較，兩者有一些相似的圖像（特別參看第20至30節）。這篇時而對神說話（「你」），時而論到神（「他」）。
n.4: 希伯來文 *yeri'ah*，就是帳幕的幔子所用的詞（出埃及記26章1節）。
n.5: 指穹蒼以上的水（創世記1章7節）。
n.6: 或譯：「他以他的使者為風，以他的僕役為火焰」。希伯來文 *mal'akh* 是「使者」或「天使」，*ruach* 是「風」或「靈」。希伯來書1章7節依照七十士譯本，取後一種意思引述這節：「他以他的使者為風，以他的僕役為火焰」，用來說明天使不及神的兒子。
n.7: 希伯來文 *tehom*，就是創世記1章2節的深淵。
n.8: 或譯：「山嶺升起，山谷沉下」。
n.9: 參看約伯記38章8至11節；耶利米書5章22節。
n.10: 直譯：「為人的工作」，或「供人使用」。
n.11: 希伯來文 *lechem*，「餅」，也泛指食物，第15節同。
n.12: 希伯來文 *shephannim*，就是蹄兔，一種住在巖石間的小動物（利未記11章5節；箴言30章26節）。
n.13: 希伯來文 *mo'adim*，「所定的時候」，包括節期（參看創世記1章14節）。
n.14: 直譯：「兩手寬闊」，向四方伸展。
n.15: 一種巨大的海中生物，在別處被描繪為混亂的怪獸（74篇14節；約伯記3章8節；40章25節，和合本作41章1節；以賽亞書27章1節）。在這裏，牠只是神所造的活物之一。和合本作「鱷魚」。
n.16: 或譯：「讓你與牠嬉戲」。
n.18: 或譯：「你的氣息」。希伯來文 *ruach* 可指靈、風或氣息；第29節「牠們的氣息」也是這個字（*rucham*）。
n.19: 希伯來文 *hallelu-yah*，「你們要讚美耶和華（*Yah*）」，就是「哈利路亞」一詞的來源。*Yah* 是 YHWH 的簡稱。這是詩篇第一次出現這呼召。七十士譯本把它放在第105篇開頭。

v: 你們要稱謝耶和華[^1]，呼求他的名，在萬民中傳揚他的作為[^2]！
הוֹד֣וּ לַ֭יהוָה קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֑וֹ הוֹדִ֥יעוּ בָ֝עַמִּ֗ים עֲלִילוֹתָֽיו׃
要向他唱歌，向他歌頌，述說他一切奇妙的作為！
שִֽׁירוּ־ל֭וֹ זַמְּרוּ־ל֑וֹ שִׂ֝֗יחוּ בְּכָל־נִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃
要以他的聖名誇耀；願尋求耶和華的人心中歡喜！
הִֽ֭תְהַלְלוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשׁ֑וֹ יִ֝שְׂמַ֗ח לֵ֤ב ׀ מְבַקְשֵׁ֬י יְהוָֽה׃
要尋求耶和華和他的能力，時常尋求他的面[^3]！
דִּרְשׁ֣וּ יְהוָ֣ה וְעֻזּ֑וֹ בַּקְּשׁ֖וּ פָנָ֣יו תָּמִֽיד׃
要記念他所行的奇妙作為，他的神蹟和他口中的判語[^4]，
זִכְר֗וּ נִפְלְאוֹתָ֥יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֑ה מֹ֝פְתָ֗יו וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי־פִֽיו׃
他僕人亞伯拉罕的後裔[^5]，他所揀選的雅各子孫啊！
זֶ֭רַע אַבְרָהָ֣ם עַבְדּ֑וֹ בְּנֵ֖י יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּחִירָֽיו׃
他是耶和華我們的神，他的判斷遍行全地。
ה֭וּא יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ בְּכָל־הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ מִשְׁפָּטָֽיו׃
他永遠記念他的約[^6]，記念他所吩咐的話，直到千代，
זָכַ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ דָּבָ֥ר צִ֝וָּ֗ה לְאֶ֣לֶף דּֽוֹר׃
就是他與亞伯拉罕所立的約，他向以撒所起的誓。
אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּ֭רַת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וּשְׁב֖וּעָת֣וֹ לְיִשְׂחָֽק׃
他向雅各堅立這約作為律例，向以色列堅立它作為永遠的約，
וַיַּֽעֲמִידֶ֣הָ לְיַעֲקֹ֣ב לְחֹ֑ק לְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָֽם׃
說：「我要把迦南地賜給你，作你們產業的分[^7]。」
לֵאמֹ֗ר לְךָ֗ אֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־אֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן חֶ֝֗בֶל נַחֲלַתְכֶֽם׃
那時他們人數稀少[^8]，非常稀少，在那地寄居；
בִּֽ֭הְיוֹתָם מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט וְגָרִ֥ים בָּֽהּ׃
他們從這邦流浪到那邦，從這國去到另一個民族。
וַֽ֭יִּתְהַלְּכוּ מִגּ֣וֹי אֶל־גּ֑וֹי מִ֝מַּמְלָכָ֗ה אֶל־עַ֥ם אַחֵֽר׃
他不容許任何人欺壓他們，為了他們的緣故責備君王：
לֹֽא־הִנִּ֣יחַ אָדָ֣ם לְעָשְׁקָ֑ם וַיּ֖וֹכַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מְלָכִֽים׃
「不可碰我的受膏者[^9]，不可惡待我的先知。」
אַֽל־תִּגְּע֥וּ בִמְשִׁיחָ֑י וְ֝לִנְבִיאַי אַל־תָּרֵֽעוּ׃
他命令饑荒臨到那地，把人所倚靠的糧食完全斷絕[^10]。
וַיִּקְרָ֣א רָ֭עָב עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כָּֽל־מַטֵּה־לֶ֥חֶם שָׁבָֽר׃
他在他們以先差派了一個人，就是被賣為奴隸的約瑟。
שָׁלַ֣ח לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם אִ֑ישׁ לְ֝עֶ֗בֶד נִמְכַּ֥ר יוֹסֵֽף׃
人用腳鐐傷了他的腳[^11]，他的脖子[^12]被套上鐵鍊，
עִנּ֣וּ בַכֶּ֣בֶל *רגליו **רַגְל֑וֹ בַּ֝רְזֶ֗ל בָּ֣אָה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
直到他的話應驗的時候；耶和華的話試煉了他[^13]。
עַד־עֵ֥ת בֹּֽא־דְבָר֑וֹ אִמְרַ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה צְרָפָֽתְהוּ׃
王派人來解開他的捆綁，萬民的統治者使他得自由，
שָׁ֣לַח מֶ֭לֶךְ וַיַּתִּירֵ֑הוּ מֹשֵׁ֥ל עַ֝מִּ֗ים וַֽיְפַתְּחֵֽהוּ׃
立他作王宮的主人，掌管王一切的產業，
שָׂמ֣וֹ אָד֣וֹן לְבֵית֑וֹ וּ֝מֹשֵׁ֗ל בְּכָל־קִנְיָנֽוֹ׃
使他隨意約束王的大臣[^14]，又把智慧教導王的長老。
לֶאְסֹ֣ר שָׂרָ֣יו בְּנַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּזְקֵנָ֥יו יְחַכֵּֽם׃
以色列也來到埃及，雅各在含地[^15]寄居。
וַיָּבֹ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְ֝יַעֲקֹ֗ב גָּ֣ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־חָֽם׃
耶和華使他的子民大大繁衍，使他們比敵人更強盛。
וַיֶּ֣פֶר אֶת־עַמּ֣וֹ מְאֹ֑ד וַ֝יַּֽעֲצִמֵהוּ מִצָּרָֽיו׃
他使敵人的心轉變，恨惡他的子民，用詭計對待他的僕人。
הָפַ֣ךְ לִ֭בָּם לִשְׂנֹ֣א עַמּ֑וֹ לְ֝הִתְנַכֵּ֗ל בַּעֲבָדָֽיו׃
他差派他的僕人摩西，和他所揀選的亞倫。
שָׁ֭לַח מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדּ֑וֹ אַ֝הֲרֹ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽחַר־בּֽוֹ׃
他們在敵人中間顯出他的神蹟[^16]，在含地顯出奇事。
שָֽׂמוּ־בָ֭ם דִּבְרֵ֣י אֹתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מֹפְתִ֗ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָֽם׃
他打發黑暗，就有了黑暗；他們沒有違背他的話[^17]。
שָׁ֣לַֽח חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וַיַּחְשִׁ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־מָ֝ר֗וּ אֶת־*דברוו **דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
他使他們的水變為血，使他們的魚死了。
הָפַ֣ךְ אֶת־מֵימֵיהֶ֣ם לְדָ֑ם וַ֝יָּ֗מֶת אֶת־דְּגָתָֽם׃
他們的地滋生了青蛙，連他們君王的內室也有。
שָׁרַ֣ץ אַרְצָ֣ם צְפַרְדְּעִ֑ים בְּ֝חַדְרֵ֗י מַלְכֵיהֶֽם׃
他一說話，成群的蒼蠅就來了，蚊子[^18]佈滿他們全境。
אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א עָרֹ֑ב כִּ֝נִּ֗ים בְּכָל־גְּבוּלָֽם׃
他給他們降下冰雹代替雨水，在他們的地上降下火燄。
נָתַ֣ן גִּשְׁמֵיהֶ֣ם בָּרָ֑ד אֵ֖שׁ לֶהָב֣וֹת בְּאַרְצָֽם׃
他擊打他們的葡萄樹和無花果樹，折斷他們境內的樹木。
וַיַּ֣ךְ גַּ֭פְנָם וּתְאֵנָתָ֑ם וַ֝יְשַׁבֵּ֗ר עֵ֣ץ גְּבוּלָֽם׃
他一說話，蝗蟲就來了，還有蝻子，多得無法數算，
אָ֭מַר וַיָּבֹ֣א אַרְבֶּ֑ה וְ֝יֶ֗לֶק וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
吃光了他們地上一切的植物，吃光了他們田地的出產。
וַיֹּ֣אכַל כָּל־עֵ֣שֶׂב בְּאַרְצָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗אכַל פְּרִ֣י אַדְמָתָֽם׃
他擊殺他們地上所有的長子，就是他們壯年時頭生的[^19]。
וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּאַרְצָ֑ם רֵ֝אשִׁ֗ית לְכָל־אוֹנָֽם׃
他領以色列人帶着金銀出來，他的支派中沒有一個跌倒的。
וַֽ֭יּוֹצִיאֵם בְּכֶ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב וְאֵ֖ין בִּשְׁבָטָ֣יו כּוֹשֵֽׁל׃
他們離開的時候，埃及人都歡喜，因為埃及人懼怕他們。
שָׂמַ֣ח מִצְרַ֣יִם בְּצֵאתָ֑ם כִּֽי־נָפַ֖ל פַּחְדָּ֣ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
他鋪張雲彩作遮蓋，又使火在夜間發光。
פָּרַ֣שׂ עָנָ֣ן לְמָסָ֑ךְ וְ֝אֵ֗שׁ לְהָאִ֥יר לָֽיְלָה׃
他們一求[^20]，他就使鵪鶉飛來，又用天上的糧食[^21]使他們飽足。
שָׁאַ֣ל[t] וַיָּבֵ֣א שְׂלָ֑ו וְלֶ֥חֶם שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽם׃
他打開磐石，水就湧出，在乾旱之地像河一樣流淌。
פָּ֣תַח צ֭וּר וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מָ֑יִם הָ֝לְכ֗וּ בַּצִּיּ֥וֹת נָהָֽר׃
因為他記念他神聖的應許，就是向他僕人亞伯拉罕所說的[^22]。
כִּֽי־זָ֭כַר אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר קָדְשׁ֑וֹ אֶֽת־אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדּֽוֹ׃
他領他的子民歡喜地出來，領他所揀選的人歡呼着出來。
וַיּוֹצִ֣א עַמּ֣וֹ בְשָׂשׂ֑וֹן בְּ֝רִנָּ֗ה אֶת־בְּחִירָֽיו׃
他把列國的地賜給他們，他們就承受了萬民勞碌所得的，
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם אַרְצ֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם וַעֲמַ֖ל לְאֻמִּ֣ים יִירָֽשׁוּ׃
好讓他們遵守他的律例，謹守他的律法。你們要讚美耶和華[^23]！
בַּעֲב֤וּר ׀ יִשְׁמְר֣וּ חֻ֭קָּיו וְתוֹרֹתָ֥יו יִנְצֹ֗רוּ הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: 耶和華：神的名字，希伯來文作 YHWH。第105篇在希伯來文中沒有標題。
n.2: 第1至15節也見於歷代志上16章8至22節，就是大衛把約櫃運到耶路撒冷時所唱的感恩之歌，只有少許差別；希伯來文相同的地方，譯文也與那裏相同。這篇接着從亞伯拉罕講到進入應許之地，說明神怎樣信守他向亞伯拉罕的應許（第8至11節和第42節）。
n.3: 或譯：「他的同在」。
n.4: 直譯：「他口中的判斷」。
n.5: 歷代志上16章13節作「他僕人以色列的後裔」。
n.6: 歷代志上16章15節作「你們要永遠記念他的約」。
n.7: 直譯：「你們產業的繩索」，就是用來量地分份的繩子。
n.8: 歷代志上16章19節作「那時你們人數稀少」。
n.9: 希伯來文 *meshichai*，「我的受膏者」，來自 *mashiach*。這裏指以色列的先祖亞伯拉罕、以撒和雅各。
n.10: 直譯：「折斷一切糧食的杖」，就是人所倚靠的糧食，好像人倚靠杖一樣。接着約瑟的故事記在創世記37至50章。
n.11: 希伯來文寫作「他的雙腳」，讀作「他的腳」。
n.12: 希伯來文 *nephesh*，這裏也許是「脖子」或「喉嚨」（參看69篇2節，和合本作69篇1節），或是「他自己」。
n.13: 「他的話」可能指約瑟的話，就是他對夢的解釋（創世記40至41章），也可能指神的話。「試煉」：或譯「熬煉」，好像熬煉金屬一樣。
n.14: 直譯：「憑他的 *nephesh* 捆綁」。七十士譯本作「教導他的大臣」，讀作只差一個字母的另一個動詞。
n.15: 就是埃及（參看創世記10章6節，含是埃及的祖先）。
n.16: 直譯：「他們在他們中間放了他神蹟的話」。第28至36節的災殃依照出埃及記7至12章的記載，但次序不同，也沒有牲畜的瘟疫和生瘡的災。
n.17: 希伯來文寫作「他的眾話」，讀作「他的話」。「他們」大概指摩西和亞倫。七十士譯本作「他們違背了他的話」，沒有「沒有」一詞。
n.18: 「成群的蒼蠅」：希伯來文 *arov*，「成群」或「混雜」（參看出埃及記8章17節，和合本作8章21節）。「蚊子」：希伯來文 *kinnim*（出埃及記8章12至14節，和合本作8章16至18節）。
n.20: 直譯：「他求」，指百姓。事件記在出埃及記16章和民數記11章31至34節。
n.21: 就是嗎哪（出埃及記16章4節；參看78篇24節）。
n.23: 希伯來文 *hallelu-yah*，「你們要讚美耶和華（*Yah*）」（參看104篇35節的註釋）。

v: 你們要讚美耶和華[^1]！要稱謝耶和華[^2]，因為他是美善的，他的慈愛[^3]永遠長存！
הַֽלְלְויָ֨הּ[c] ׀ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
誰能述說耶和華大能的作為？誰能傳揚他一切可讚美的事？
מִ֗י יְ֭מַלֵּל גְּבוּר֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה יַ֝שְׁמִ֗יעַ כָּל־תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃
遵守公正、時常行公義的人多麼有福[^4]！
אַ֭שְׁרֵי שֹׁמְרֵ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֑ט עֹשֵׂ֖ה צְדָקָ֣ה בְכָל־עֵֽת׃
耶和華啊，你恩待你子民的時候，求你記念我；你施行拯救的時候，求你眷顧我[^5]，
זָכְרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה בִּרְצ֣וֹן עַמֶּ֑ךָ פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
好讓我看見你選民的福樂，分享你國民的喜樂，與你的產業一同誇耀。
לִרְא֤וֹת ׀ בְּט֘וֹבַ֤ת בְּחִירֶ֗יךָ לִ֭שְׂמֹחַ בְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת גּוֹיֶ֑ךָ לְ֝הִתְהַלֵּ֗ל עִם־נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃
我們和我們的祖先一同犯了罪[^6]；我們作了孽，行了惡。
חָטָ֥אנוּ עִם־אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃
我們的祖先在埃及不明白你的奇事，不記念你豐盛的慈愛，反而在海邊，就是在紅海[^7]那裏悖逆。
אֲב֘וֹתֵ֤ינוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם ׀ לֹא־הִשְׂכִּ֬ילוּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א זָ֭כְרוּ אֶת־רֹ֣ב חֲסָדֶ֑יךָ וַיַּמְר֖וּ עַל־יָ֣ם בְּיַם־סֽוּף׃
但他為了自己的名拯救他們，要彰顯他的大能。
וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמ֑וֹ לְ֝הוֹדִ֗יעַ אֶת־גְּבוּרָתֽוֹ׃
他斥責紅海，海就乾了；他領他們走過深水，好像走過曠野。
וַיִּגְעַ֣ר בְּיַם־ס֭וּף וֽ͏ַיֶּחֱרָ֑ב וַיּוֹלִיכֵ֥ם בַּ֝תְּהֹמ֗וֹת כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
他拯救他們脫離恨他們的人的手，救贖他們脫離仇敵的手。
וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם מִיַּ֣ד שׂוֹנֵ֑א וַ֝יִּגְאָלֵ֗ם מִיַּ֥ד אוֹיֵֽב׃
水淹沒了他們的敵人，連一個也沒有剩下。
וַיְכַסּוּ־מַ֥יִם צָרֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד מֵ֝הֶ֗ם לֹ֣א נוֹתָֽר׃
那時他們才信了他的話，歌唱讚美他[^8]。
וַיַּאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִדְבָרָ֑יו יָ֝שִׁ֗ירוּ תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃
他們很快就忘記了他的作為，不等候他的指引。
מִֽ֭הֲרוּ שָׁכְח֣וּ מַעֲשָׂ֑יו לֹֽא־חִ֝כּ֗וּ לַעֲצָתֽוֹ׃
他們在曠野大起貪慾，在荒野試探神。
וַיִּתְאַוּ֣וּ תַ֭אֲוָה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּוּ־אֵ֝֗ל בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃
他就把他們所求的賜給他們，卻使他們消瘦[^9]。
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם שֶׁאֱלָתָ֑ם וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח רָז֣וֹן בְּנַפְשָֽׁם׃
他們在營中嫉妒摩西，又嫉妒耶和華的聖者亞倫。
וַיְקַנְא֣וּ לְ֭מֹשֶׁה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה לְ֝אַהֲרֹ֗ן קְד֣וֹשׁ יְהוָֽה׃
地裂開，吞下大坍，掩蓋了亞比蘭的一夥人[^10]。
תִּפְתַּח־אֶ֭רֶץ וַתִּבְלַ֣ע דָּתָ֑ן וַ֝תְּכַ֗ס עַל־עֲדַ֥ת אֲבִירָֽם׃
有火在他們的同黨中燒起，火焰燒盡了惡人。
וַתִּבְעַר־אֵ֥שׁ בַּעֲדָתָ֑ם לֶ֝הָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט רְשָׁעִֽים׃
他們在何烈山造了牛犢，向鑄像下拜。
יַעֲשׂוּ־עֵ֥גֶל בְּחֹרֵ֑ב וַ֝יִּשְׁתַּחֲו֗וּ לְמַסֵּכָֽה׃
他們把他們的榮耀[^11]換成吃草的公牛的像。
וַיָּמִ֥ירוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדָ֑ם בְּתַבְנִ֥ית שׁ֝֗וֹר אֹכֵ֥ל עֵֽשֶׂב׃
他們忘記了拯救他們的神，就是在埃及行大事、
שָׁ֭כְחוּ אֵ֣ל מוֹשִׁיעָ֑ם עֹשֶׂ֖ה גְדֹל֣וֹת בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
在含地[^12]行奇事、在紅海行可畏之事的那一位。
נִ֭פְלָאוֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָ֑ם נ֝וֹרָא֗וֹת עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃
所以他說要消滅他們，若不是他所揀選的摩西站在破口[^13]，在他面前使他的烈怒轉消，免得他毀滅他們。
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְֽהַשְׁמִ֫ידָ֥ם לוּלֵ֡י מֹ֘שֶׁ֤ה בְחִיר֗וֹ עָמַ֣ד בַּפֶּ֣רֶץ לְפָנָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֥יב חֲ֝מָת֗וֹ מֵֽהַשְׁחִֽית׃
他們又厭棄那美好的地，不信他的應許[^14]，
וַֽ֭יִּמְאֲסוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֑ה לֹֽא־הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ לִדְבָרֽוֹ׃
在自己的帳棚裏發怨言，不聽從耶和華的聲音。
וַיֵּרָגְנ֥וּ בְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָֽה׃
所以他向他們舉手起誓[^15]，要使他們倒斃在曠野，
וַיִשָּׂ֣א יָד֣וֹ לָהֶ֑ם לְהַפִּ֥יל א֝וֹתָ֗ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
使他們的後裔倒斃在列國中，把他們分散到各地。
וּלְהַפִּ֣יל זַ֭רְעָם בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּ֝לְזָרוֹתָ֗ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
他們又與巴力‧毗珥連合，吃了祭死人的祭物[^16]。
וַ֭יִּצָּ֣מְדוּ לְבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר וַ֝יֹּאכְל֗וּ זִבְחֵ֥י מֵתִֽים׃
他們以自己的行為惹他發怒，瘟疫就在他們中間爆發。
וַ֭יַּכְעִיסוּ בְּמַ֥עַלְלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתִּפְרָץ־בָּ֝֗ם מַגֵּפָֽה׃
那時，非尼哈站出來施行審判[^17]，瘟疫就止住了。
וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד פִּֽ֭ינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּ֑ל וַ֝תֵּעָצַ֗ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃
這就算為他的義[^18]，世世代代，直到永遠。
וַתֵּחָ֣שֶׁב ל֭וֹ לִצְדָקָ֑ה לְדֹ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
他們在米利巴水那裏又惹他發怒[^19]，摩西也因他們受了害；
וַ֭יַּקְצִיפוּ עַל־מֵ֥י מְרִיבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥רַע לְ֝מֹשֶׁ֗ה בַּעֲבוּרָֽם׃
因為他們違逆了他的靈[^20]，摩西就用嘴說了冒失的話。
כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אֶת־רוּח֑וֹ וַ֝יְבַטֵּ֗א בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃
他們沒有照耶和華的吩咐，消滅那些民族，
לֹֽא־הִ֭שְׁמִידוּ אֶת־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה לָהֶֽם׃
反而與列國混雜，學習他們的行為，
וַיִּתְעָרְב֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽ֝יִּלְמְד֗וּ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃
事奉他們的偶像；這些偶像成了他們的網羅。
וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֑ם וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָהֶ֣ם לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃
他們把自己的兒女祭祀鬼魔[^21]，
וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ אֶת־בְּ֭נֵיהֶם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם לַשֵּֽׁדִים׃
流無辜人的血，就是他們兒女的血，把他們祭祀迦南的偶像；那地就被血污穢了。
וַיִּ֥שְׁפְּכ֨[t]וּ דָ֪ם נָקִ֡י דַּם־בְּנֵ֘יהֶ֤ם וּֽבְנוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר זִ֭בְּחוּ לַעֲצַבֵּ֣י כְנָ֑עַן וַתֶּחֱנַ֥ף הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ בַּדָּמִֽים׃
這樣，他們因自己的行為成為不潔淨，在所做的事上行邪淫[^22]。
וַיִּטְמְא֥וּ בְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּזְנ֗וּ בְּמַ֥עַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃
所以耶和華的怒氣向他的子民發作，他厭惡自己的產業，
וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֣ה בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וַ֝יְתָעֵ֗ב אֶת־נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃
把他們交在列國手中；恨他們的人就統治他們。
וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם בְּיַד־גּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽיִּמְשְׁל֥וּ בָ֝הֶ֗ם שֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃
他們的仇敵欺壓他們，他們就被制伏在敵人手下。
וַיִּלְחָצ֥וּם אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּכָּנְע֗וּ תַּ֣חַת יָדָֽם׃
他多次拯救他們，他們卻存心悖逆，因自己的罪孽而衰敗。
פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֗וֹת יַצִּ֫ילֵ֥ם וְ֭הֵמָּה יַמְר֣וּ בַעֲצָתָ֑ם וַ֝יָּמֹ֗כּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָֽם׃
然而，他聽見他們哀求的時候，就看顧他們的困苦，
וַ֭יַּרְא בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־רִנָּתָֽם׃
為他們記念他的約，照他豐盛的慈愛[^23]改變心意，
וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר לָהֶ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ וַ֝יִּנָּחֵ֗ם כְּרֹ֣ב *חסדו **חֲסָדָֽיו׃
使他們在所有擄掠他們的人面前蒙憐憫。
וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אוֹתָ֣ם לְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִ֝פְנֵ֗י כָּל־שׁוֹבֵיהֶֽם׃
耶和華我們的神啊，求你拯救我們，從列國中聚集我們，好讓我們稱謝你的聖名，以讚美你為榮[^24]！
הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ ׀ יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְקַבְּצֵנוּ֮ מִֽן־הַגּ֫וֹיִ֥ם לְ֭הֹדוֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ לְ֝הִשְׁתַּבֵּ֗חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
耶和華以色列的神是應當稱頌的，從永遠到永遠！願眾民都說：「阿們！」你們要讚美耶和華[^25]！
בָּ֤רֽ[t]וּךְ־יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֪י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל מִן־הָ֤עוֹלָ֨ם ׀ וְעַ֬ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם וְאָמַ֖ר כָּל־הָעָ֥ם אָמֵ֗ן הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: 希伯來文 *hallelu-yah*，「你們要讚美耶和華（*Yah*）」（參看104篇35節的註釋）。第48節同。除此以外，第106篇沒有標題。
n.2: 耶和華：神的名字，希伯來文作 YHWH。這節其餘的部分與歷代志上16章34節相同，譯文也相同（參看100篇5節；107篇1節；118篇1節；136篇1節）。
n.3: 希伯來文 *chesed*，指信實不變、守約的愛。第7和45節同，那兩處是複數，「種種慈愛的作為」。
n.4: 希伯來文 *ashrei*：有福、幸運。
n.5: 直譯：「求你探望我」。
n.6: 直譯：「我們與我們的祖先犯了罪」。這篇接着重述以色列的歷史，從出埃及到被擄，是一部悖逆的歷史，也是神施憐憫的歷史。
n.7: 希伯來文 *yam suf*，直譯：「蘆葦海」，傳統譯作「紅海」。第9和22節同。在海邊悖逆的事，參看出埃及記14章10至12節。
n.8: 參看出埃及記14章31節至15章21節。
n.9: 直譯：「使消瘦進入他們的 *nephesh*」。第14至15節的事記在民數記11章4至34節。
n.10: 大坍、亞比蘭和其他人背叛的事記在民數記16章（參看申命記11章6節）。
n.11: 就是神，以色列的榮耀（參看耶利米書2章11節；羅馬書1章23節）。猶太文士的傳統把這節列為文士出於敬畏而改動字詞的地方之一，說原文是「我的榮耀」，改為「他們的榮耀」。牛犢的事記在出埃及記32章。
n.12: 就是埃及（參看105篇23節）。
n.13: 好像士兵站在城牆的缺口上。參看出埃及記32章9至14節。
n.14: 直譯：「不信他的話」。第24至27節的事記在民數記13至14章。
n.15: 舉手是起誓的動作（參看民數記14章28至30節；以西結書20章23節）。
n.16: 直譯：「死人的祭物」，也許指獻給沒有生命的神明的祭物（參看民數記25章2節），也許指為死人獻的祭。第28至31節的事記在民數記25章1至13節。
n.17: 希伯來文 *vayefallel*，「他介入」，或「他執行審判」（參看民數記25章7至8節）。
n.18: 創世記15章6節論到亞伯拉罕也用了同樣的話。
n.19: 事件記在民數記20章2至13節。「米利巴」的意思是「爭吵」。
n.20: 就是神的靈（參看以賽亞書63章10節），或指摩西自己的心靈。
n.21: 希伯來文 *shedim*，除這裏以外只在申命記32章17節出現。
n.22: 以妻子對丈夫不忠，比喻以色列對神不忠（參看何西阿書2章；以西結書16章）。
n.23: 希伯來文寫作「他的慈愛」，讀作「他種種慈愛的作為」。
n.24: 第47至48節與歷代志上16章35至36節相近，譯文也與那裏相同；那裏第35節開頭作「要說：『拯救我們的神啊，求你拯救我們！求你聚集我們，救我們脫離列國……』」。
n.25: 歷代志上16章36節作「眾民都說：『阿們！』並且讚美耶和華」。這節的頌讚結束詩篇第四卷（第90至106篇）。第一、二和三卷也以相似的話結束（41篇14節，和合本作41篇13節；72篇18至19節；89篇53節，和合本作89篇52節），第150篇則結束整部詩篇。

v: Give thanks to the LORD,[^1] for he is good; his faithful love[^2] endures forever.
הֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, those he redeemed from the hand of the adversary,
יֹ֭אמְרוּ גְּאוּלֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גְּ֝אָלָ֗ם מִיַּד־צָֽר׃
and gathered from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the sea.[^3]
וּֽמֵאֲרָצ֗וֹת קִ֫בְּצָ֥ם מִמִּזְרָ֥ח וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֑ב מִצָּפ֥וֹן וּמִיָּֽם׃
Some wandered in the wilderness, in the desert wastes;[^4] they found no way to a city to live in.
תָּע֣וּ בַ֭מִּדְבָּר בִּישִׁימ֣וֹן דָּ֑רֶךְ עִ֥יר מ֝וֹשָׁ֗ב לֹ֣א מָצָֽאוּ׃
They were hungry and thirsty; their soul[^5] fainted within them.
רְעֵבִ֥ים גַּם־צְמֵאִ֑ים נַ֝פְשָׁ֗ם בָּהֶ֥ם תִּתְעַטָּֽף׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he rescued them from their distress.[^6]
וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֽוּקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יַצִּילֵֽם׃
He led them by a straight road, to go to a city to live in.
וַ֭יּֽ͏ַדְרִיכֵם בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ יְשָׁרָ֑ה לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת אֶל־עִ֥יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.[^7]
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
For he satisfies the thirsty soul, and fills the hungry soul with good things.
כִּי־הִ֭שְׂבִּיעַ נֶ֣פֶשׁ שֹׁקֵקָ֑ה וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָה מִלֵּא־טֽוֹב׃
Some sat in darkness and deep darkness,[^8] prisoners in misery and in iron,
יֹ֭שְׁבֵי חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת אֲסִירֵ֖י עֳנִ֣י וּבַרְזֶֽל׃
because they had rebelled against the words of God, and spurned the counsel of the Most High.[^9]
כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אִמְרֵי־אֵ֑ל וַעֲצַ֖ת עֶלְי֣וֹן נָאָֽצוּ׃
So he humbled their hearts with hard labor; they stumbled, and there was no one to help.
וַיַּכְנַ֣ע בֶּעָמָ֣ל לִבָּ֑ם כָּ֝שְׁל֗וּ וְאֵ֣ין עֹזֵֽר׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
He brought them out of darkness and deep darkness, and snapped their chains.
יֽ֭וֹצִיאֵם מֵחֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְצַלְמָ֑וֶת וּמוֹסְר֖וֹתֵיהֶ֣ם יְנַתֵּֽק׃
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
For he shatters the doors of bronze, and cuts through the bars of iron.[^10]
כִּֽי־שִׁ֭בַּר דַּלְת֣וֹת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וּבְרִיחֵ֖י בַרְזֶ֣ל גִּדֵּֽעַ׃
Some were fools because of their rebellious ways,[^11] and suffered affliction because of their iniquities.
אֱ֭וִלִים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ פִּשְׁעָ֑ם וּֽ֝מֵעֲוֺ֥נֹתֵיהֶ֗ם[t] יִתְעַנּֽוּ׃
They loathed all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
כָּל־אֹ֭כֶל תְּתַעֵ֣ב נַפְשָׁ֑ם וַ֝יַּגִּ֗יעוּ עַד־שַׁ֥עֲרֵי מָֽוֶת׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
וַיִּזְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם מִ֝מְּצֻֽקוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
He sent out his word and healed them, and rescued them from their graves.[^12]
יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּ֭בָרוֹ וְיִרְפָּאֵ֑ם וִֽ֝ימַלֵּ֗ט מִשְּׁחִיתוֹתָֽם׃ [8]׆
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ [8]׆
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving,[^13] and tell of his deeds with songs of joy.
וְ֭יִזְבְּחוּ זִבְחֵ֣י תוֹדָ֑ה וִֽיסַפְּר֖וּ מַעֲשָׂ֣יו בְּרִנָּֽה׃ [8]׆
Some went down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters.
יוֹרְדֵ֣י הַ֭יָּם בָּאֳנִיּ֑וֹת עֹשֵׂ֥י מְ֝לָאכָ֗ה בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּֽים׃ [8]׆
They saw the works of the LORD, his wonders in the deep.
הֵ֣מָּה רָ֭אוּ מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו בִּמְצוּלָֽה׃ [8]׆
For he spoke and raised a stormy wind, which lifted high the waves of the sea.
וַיֹּ֗אמֶר וַֽ֭יַּעֲמֵד ר֣וּחַ סְעָרָ֑ה וַתְּרוֹמֵ֥ם גַּלָּֽיו׃ [8]׆
They went up to the heavens; they went down to the depths; their courage[^14] melted away in their peril.
יַעֲל֣וּ שָׁ֭מַיִם יֵרְד֣וּ תְהוֹמ֑וֹת נַ֝פְשָׁ֗ם בְּרָעָ֥ה תִתְמוֹגָֽג׃
They reeled and staggered like drunkards, and all their skill[^15] was swallowed up.
יָח֣וֹגּוּ וְ֭יָנוּעוּ כַּשִּׁכּ֑וֹר וְכָל־חָ֝כְמָתָ֗ם תִּתְבַּלָּֽע׃
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he brought them out of their distress.
וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּֽ֝מִמְּצֽוּקֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹצִיאֵֽם׃
He made the storm a calm, and its waves were still.
יָקֵ֣ם סְ֭עָרָה לִדְמָמָ֑ה וַ֝יֶּחֱשׁ֗וּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם׃
They were glad when it grew quiet, and he guided them to the harbor[^16] they longed for.
וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כִֽי־יִשְׁתֹּ֑קוּ וַ֝יַּנְחֵ֗ם אֶל־מְח֥וֹז חֶפְצָֽם׃
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
יוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the council of the elders.
וִֽ֭ירֹמְמוּהוּ בִּקְהַל־עָ֑ם וּבְמוֹשַׁ֖ב זְקֵנִ֣ים יְהַלְלֽוּהוּ׃
He turns rivers into a desert, and springs of water into thirsty ground,
יָשֵׂ֣ם נְהָר֣וֹת לְמִדְבָּ֑ר וּמֹצָ֥אֵי מַ֝֗יִם לְצִמָּאֽוֹן׃
a fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of those who live there.
אֶ֣רֶץ פְּ֭רִי לִמְלֵחָ֑ה מֵ֝רָעַ֗ת יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃
He turns a desert into pools of water, and dry land into springs of water.
יָשֵׂ֣ם מִ֭דְבָּר לַֽאֲגַם־מַ֑יִם וְאֶ֥רֶץ צִ֝יָּ֗ה לְמֹצָ֥אֵי מָֽיִם׃
There he settles the hungry, and they establish a city to live in.
וַיּ֣וֹשֶׁב שָׁ֣ם רְעֵבִ֑ים וַ֝יְכוֹנְנ֗וּ עִ֣יר מוֹשָֽׁב׃
They sow fields and plant vineyards, and gather a fruitful harvest.
וַיִּזְרְע֣וּ שָׂ֭דוֹת וַיִּטְּע֣וּ כְרָמִ֑ים וַ֝יַּעֲשׂ֗וּ פְּרִ֣י תְבֽוּאָה׃
He blesses them, and they become very many, and he does not let their cattle decrease.
וַיְבָרֲכֵ֣ם וַיִּרְבּ֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וּ֝בְהֶמְתָּ֗ם לֹ֣א יַמְעִֽיט׃
When they are diminished and brought low through oppression, trouble and sorrow,[^17]
וַיִּמְעֲט֥וּ וַיָּשֹׁ֑חוּ מֵעֹ֖צֶר רָעָ֣ה וְיָגֽוֹן׃ [8]׆
he pours contempt on nobles, and makes them wander in a trackless waste;[^18]
שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ בּ֭וּז עַל־נְדִיבִ֑ים וַ֝יַּתְעֵ֗ם בְּתֹ֣הוּ לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ׃
but he lifts the needy out of affliction, and makes their families like flocks.
וַיְשַׂגֵּ֣ב אֶבְי֣וֹן מֵע֑וֹנִי וַיָּ֥שֶׂם כַּ֝צֹּ֗אן מִשְׁפָּחֽוֹת׃
The upright see it and are glad, and all injustice shuts its mouth.[^19]
יִרְא֣וּ יְשָׁרִ֣ים וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ וְכָל־עַ֝וְלָ֗ה קָ֣פְצָה פִּֽיהָ׃
Whoever is wise, let him heed these things, and consider the acts of faithful love of the LORD.
מִי־חָכָ֥ם וְיִשְׁמָר־אֵ֑לֶּה וְ֝יִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֗וּ חַֽסְדֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 107 has no title. It begins Book 5 of the Psalms (Psalms 107–150). Its first verse is the same as 106:1b (compare 100:5; 118:1; 1 Chronicles 16:34).
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verses 8, 15, 21, 31 and 43, where it is plural, "acts of faithful love".
n.3: *The sea* usually means the west. Here it may mean the south (the Red Sea), to complete the four directions.
n.4: Literally "in the wasteland of a road", or "in the wasteland, (without) a road".
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 9, 18 and 26.
n.6: This refrain comes again in verses 13, 19 and 28, and the refrain of verse 8 in verses 15, 21 and 31. They frame four pictures of people rescued by God: travelers lost in the desert (verses 4–9), prisoners (10–16), the sick (17–22) and sailors (23–32).
n.7: Literally "the sons of *adam*". Also in verses 15, 21 and 31.
n.8: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death". Also in verse 14.
n.9: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.10: Compare Isaiah 45:2.
n.11: Hebrew *evilim*, "fools", those whose folly is moral, not merely a lack of sense. Their sickness (verse 18) is the result of their sin.
n.12: Hebrew *shechitotam*, a rare word, perhaps "their pits" or "their destruction". In the Hebrew text, a mark shaped like the letter *nun* written upside down stands after each of verses 20–25 and 39, the scribal sign found also at Numbers 10:35–36. Its meaning here is uncertain.
n.13: Hebrew *todah*: a sacrifice given in thanksgiving (Leviticus 7:12).
n.14: Literally "their soul (*nephesh*)".
n.15: Literally "wisdom".
n.16: Hebrew *mechoz*, a word found only here, probably "harbor" or "city".
n.17: The thought of verses 39–41 is compressed: God humbles the proud and lifts up the needy (compare 1 Samuel 2:7–8).
n.18: Verse 40 repeats Job 12:21a and 12:24b. Hebrew *tohu*, a formless waste (Genesis 1:2).

v: A song. A psalm of David.[^1]
שִׁ֖יר מִזְמ֣וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
My heart is steadfast, God; I will sing and make music, with my glory too.[^2]
נָכ֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י אֱלֹהִ֑ים אָשִׁ֥ירָה וַ֝אֲזַמְּרָ֗ה אַף־כְּבוֹדִֽי׃
Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
ע֭וּרָֽה הַנֵּ֥בֶל וְכִנּ֗וֹר אָעִ֥ירָה שָּֽׁחַר׃
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, LORD;[^3] I will sing praise to you among the nations.
אוֹדְךָ֖ בָעַמִּ֥ים ׀ יְהוָ֑ה וַ֝אֲזַמֶּרְךָ֗ בַּל־אֻמִּֽים׃
For your faithful love[^4] is great, above the heavens,[^5] and your faithfulness to the clouds.
כִּֽי־גָד֣וֹל מֵֽעַל־שָׁמַ֣יִם חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽעַד־שְׁחָקִ֥ים אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
ר֣וּמָה עַל־שָׁמַ֣יִם אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ׃
So that those you love may be rescued, save by your right hand, and answer me.[^6]
לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וַעֲנֵֽנִי׃
God has spoken in his holiness:[^7] "I will exult; I will divide up Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃
Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet on my head;[^8] Judah is my scepter.[^9]
לִ֤י גִלְעָ֨ד ׀ לִ֤י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה וְ֭אֶפְרַיִם מָע֣וֹז רֹאשִׁ֑י יְ֝הוּדָ֗ה מְחֹקְקִֽי׃
Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I throw my sandal;[^10] over Philistia I shout in triumph."[^11]
מוֹאָ֤ב ׀ סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗י עַל־אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑י עֲלֵֽי־פְ֝לֶ֗שֶׁת אֶתְרוֹעָֽע׃
Who will bring me to the fortified city?[^12] Who will lead me to Edom?[^13]
מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מִבְצָ֑ר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־אֱדֽוֹם׃
Have you not rejected us, God? You no longer go out, God, with our armies.
הֲלֹֽא־אֱלֹהִ֥ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְֽלֹא־תֵצֵ֥א אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בְּצִבְאֹתֵֽינוּ׃
Give us help against the adversary, for human help is worthless.[^14]
הָֽבָה־לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָֽם׃
With God we will do valiantly; he will trample our adversaries.
בֵּֽאלֹהִ֥ים נַעֲשֶׂה־חָ֑יִל וְ֝ה֗וּא יָב֥וּס צָרֵֽינוּ׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 108:1–13 in most English Bibles. The psalm joins two passages found elsewhere, with small differences: verses 2–6 are 57:8–12 (57:7–11 in most English Bibles), and verses 7–14 are 60:7–14 (60:5–12 in most English Bibles). The notes give the main differences.
n.2: Hebrew *af-kevodi*, "also my glory", perhaps meaning "with my whole being" (compare 16:9; 57:9; 57:8 in most English Bibles). Psalm 57:8–9 (57:7–8 in most English Bibles) repeats "my heart is steadfast" and has "Wake up, my glory!"
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 57:10 (57:9 in most English Bibles) has "Lord".
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.5: Psalm 57:11 (57:10 in most English Bibles) has "reaching to the heavens".
n.6: Psalm 60:7 (60:5 in most English Bibles) is written "answer us" but read "answer me".
n.7: Or "in his holy place".
n.8: Literally "the stronghold of my head".
n.9: Or "my ruler's staff" (compare Genesis 49:10).
n.10: Throwing a sandal on land was perhaps a sign of taking possession of it (compare Ruth 4:7).
n.11: Psalm 60:10 (60:8 in most English Bibles) has "Philistia, shout aloud because of me!"
n.12: Hebrew *ir mivtsar*. Psalm 60:11 (60:9 in most English Bibles) has *ir matsor*, with the same meaning.
n.13: Literally "Who has led me to Edom?", as in 60:11 (60:9 in most English Bibles).
n.14: Literally "the salvation of *adam* (humankind) is worthless".

v: For the director. Of David. A psalm.[^1] God of my praise,[^2] do not be silent!
לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹר אֱלֹהֵ֥י תְ֝הִלָּתִ֗י אַֽל־תֶּחֱרַֽשׁ׃
For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me; they speak against me with a lying tongue.
כִּ֤י פִ֪י רָשָׁ֡ע וּֽפִי־מִ֭רְמָה עָלַ֣י פָּתָ֑חוּ דִּבְּר֥וּ אִ֝תִּ֗י לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃
They surround me with words of hatred, and attack me without cause.
וְדִבְרֵ֣י שִׂנְאָ֣ה סְבָב֑וּנִי וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֥וּנִי חִנָּֽם׃
In return for my love they accuse me,[^3] but I am in prayer.[^4]
תַּֽחַת־אַהֲבָתִ֥י יִשְׂטְנ֗וּנִי וַאֲנִ֥י תְפִלָּֽה׃
They repay me evil for good, and hatred for my love.
וַיָּ֘שִׂ֤ימוּ עָלַ֣י רָ֭עָה תַּ֣חַת טוֹבָ֑ה וְ֝שִׂנְאָ֗ה תַּ֣חַת אַהֲבָתִֽי׃
Appoint a wicked man against him; let an accuser[^5] stand at his right hand.[^6]
הַפְקֵ֣ד עָלָ֣יו רָשָׁ֑ע וְ֝שָׂטָ֗ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־יְמִינֽוֹ׃
When he is judged, let him come out guilty,[^7] and let his prayer be counted as sin.
בְּ֭הִשָּׁ֣פְטוֹ יֵצֵ֣א רָשָׁ֑ע ו֝תְפִלָּת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַֽחֲטָאָֽה׃
May his days be few; may another take his office.[^8]
יִֽהְיֽוּ־יָמָ֥יו מְעַטִּ֑ים פְּ֝קֻדָּת֗וֹ יִקַּ֥ח אַחֵֽר׃
May his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
יִֽהְיוּ־בָנָ֥יו יְתוֹמִ֑ים וְ֝אִשְׁתּוֹ אַלְמָנָֽה׃
May his children wander about and beg, searching for food far from their ruined homes.[^9]
וְנ֤וֹעַ יָנ֣וּעוּ בָנָ֣יו וְשִׁאֵ֑לוּ וְ֝דָרְשׁ֗וּ מֵחָרְבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
May the creditor seize all that he has; may strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.
יְנַקֵּ֣שׁ נ֭וֹשֶׁה לְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְיָבֹ֖זּוּ זָרִ֣ים יְגִיעֽוֹ׃
May there be no one to show him faithful love,[^10] and no one to have pity on his fatherless children.
אַל־יְהִי־ל֭וֹ מֹשֵׁ֣ךְ חָ֑סֶד וְֽאַל־יְהִ֥י ח֝וֹנֵ֗ן לִיתוֹמָֽיו׃
May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out in the next generation.
יְהִֽי־אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית בְּד֥וֹר אַ֝חֵ֗ר יִמַּ֥ח שְׁמָֽם׃
May the iniquity of his ancestors be remembered before the LORD,[^11] and do not let the sin of his mother be blotted out.
יִזָּכֵ֤ר ׀ עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה וְחַטַּ֥את אִ֝מּ֗וֹ אַל־תִּמָּֽח׃
Let them be before the LORD continually, and may he cut off their memory from the earth,
יִהְי֣וּ נֶֽגֶד־יְהוָ֣ה תָּמִ֑יד וְיַכְרֵ֖ת מֵאֶ֣רֶץ זִכְרָֽם׃
because he did not remember to show faithful love, but hounded the afflicted and needy man, and the brokenhearted, to put them to death.
יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר ׀ לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ עֲשׂ֢וֹת חָ֥סֶד וַיִּרְדֹּ֡ף אִישׁ־עָנִ֣י וְ֭אֶבְיוֹן וְנִכְאֵ֨ה לֵבָ֬ב לְמוֹתֵֽת׃
He loved cursing, and it has come on him; he took no pleasure in blessing, and it has stayed far from him.[^12]
וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב קְ֭לָלָה וַתְּבוֹאֵ֑הוּ וְֽלֹא־חָפֵ֥ץ בִּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה וַתִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
He clothed himself with cursing as with his robe; it has soaked into his body[^13] like water, and into his bones like oil.
וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ קְלָלָ֗ה כְּמַ֫דּ֥וֹ וַתָּבֹ֣א כַמַּ֣יִם בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְ֝כַשֶּׁ֗מֶן בְּעַצְמוֹתָֽיו׃
May it be to him like a garment he wraps around himself, like a belt he always wears.
תְּהִי־ל֭וֹ כְּבֶ֣גֶד יַעְטֶ֑ה וּ֝לְמֵ֗זַח תָּמִ֥יד יַחְגְּרֶֽהָ׃
May this be the reward of my accusers from the LORD, of those who speak evil against my life.[^14]
זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְהַדֹּבְרִ֥ים רָ֝֗ע עַל־נַפְשִֽׁי׃
But you, GOD my Lord,[^15] deal with me for the sake of your name; because your faithful love is good, rescue me.
וְאַתָּ֤ה ׀ יְה֘וִ֤ה אֲדֹנָ֗י עֲ‍ֽשֵׂה־אִ֭תִּי לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ כִּי־ט֥וֹב חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ הַצִּילֵֽנִי׃
For I am afflicted and needy, and my heart is pierced within me.
כִּֽי־עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֣וֹן אָנֹ֑כִי וְ֝לִבִּ֗י חָלַ֥ל בְּקִרְבִּֽי׃
I fade away like a lengthening shadow; I am shaken off like a locust.
כְּצֵל־כִּנְטוֹת֥וֹ נֶהֱלָ֑כְתִּי נִ֝נְעַ֗רְתִּי כָּֽאַרְבֶּֽה׃
My knees give way from fasting; my body has grown thin and gaunt.[^16]
בִּ֭רְכַּי כָּשְׁל֣וּ מִצּ֑וֹם וּ֝בְשָׂרִ֗י כָּחַ֥שׁ מִשָּֽׁמֶן׃
I have become a disgrace to them; when they see me, they shake their heads.[^17]
וַאֲנִ֤י ׀ הָיִ֣יתִי חֶרְפָּ֣ה לָהֶ֑ם יִ֝רְא֗וּנִי יְנִיע֥וּן רֹאשָֽׁם׃
Help me, LORD my God; save me according to your faithful love.
עָ֭זְרֵנִי יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י ה֖וֹשִׁיעֵ֣נִי כְחַסְדֶּֽךָ׃
Let them know that this is your hand, that you, LORD, have done it.
וְֽ֭יֵדְעוּ כִּי־יָ֣דְךָ זֹּ֑את אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֣ה עֲשִׂיתָֽהּ׃
Let them curse, but you will bless. When they rise up, let them be put to shame, and let your servant rejoice.
יְקַֽלְלוּ־הֵמָּה֮ וְאַתָּ֢ה תְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ קָ֤מוּ ׀ וַיֵּבֹ֗שׁוּ וְֽעַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשְׂמָֽח׃
May my accusers be clothed with disgrace, and wrapped in their own shame as in a cloak.
יִלְבְּשׁ֣וּ שׂוֹטְנַ֣י כְּלִמָּ֑ה וְיַעֲט֖וּ כַמְעִ֣יל בָּשְׁתָּֽם׃
With my mouth I will give great thanks to the LORD; I will praise him in the midst of the crowd.
א֘וֹדֶ֤ה יְהוָ֣ה מְאֹ֣ד בְּפִ֑י וּבְת֖וֹךְ רַבִּ֣ים אֲהַֽלְלֶֽנּוּ׃
For he stands at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who would condemn him to death.[^18]
כִּֽי־יַ֭עֲמֹד לִימִ֣ין אֶבְי֑וֹן לְ֝הוֹשִׁ֗יעַ מִשֹּׁפְטֵ֥י נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: That is, the God whom I praise.
n.3: Hebrew *yistenuni*, from the same root as *satan*, "accuser" (verse 6). Also in verses 20 and 29, "my accusers".
n.4: Literally "but I, prayer". Or "but I pray for them".
n.5: Hebrew *satan*, "adversary, accuser", here without the article, as in a court of law. The accuser stood at the right hand of the accused (compare Zechariah 3:1). The Septuagint reads "the devil".
n.6: Verses 6–19 contain some of the harshest curses in the Bible. They speak of one man ("him"), while the enemies in verses 2–5 and 20–29 are many. Many interpreters read verses 6–19 as the psalmist's own prayer against the leader of his enemies. Others read them as the curses his enemies speak against him (compare "they speak against me", verse 2, and "those who speak evil against my life", verse 20), which he quotes and then hands over to God. On that reading, verse 20 means "This is what my accusers seek from the LORD". The Hebrew has no quotation marks, and either reading is possible. This translation does not put them in quotation marks.
n.7: Literally "let him go out wicked", that is, condemned.
n.8: Hebrew *pequddah*, "charge, office". Acts 1:20 quotes this line from the Septuagint, with 69:26 (69:25 in most English Bibles), and applies it to Judas.
n.9: Literally "and search from their ruins".
n.10: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verses 16, 21 and 26.
n.11: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.12: Or "so let it come on him… so let it be far from him". The Hebrew verbs in verses 17–18 are in the past tense, but the context is a curse.
n.13: Literally "into his inner parts".
n.14: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 31. On the meaning of this verse, see the note on verse 6.
n.15: Hebrew *YHWH Adonai*, the reverse of the more common *Adonai YHWH*, "the Lord GOD". Next to "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.16: Literally "my flesh has grown lean, without fat".
n.17: Compare 22:8 (22:7 in most English Bibles) and Mark 15:29.
n.18: Literally "from those who judge his soul (*nephesh*)".

v: Of David. A psalm.[^1] The LORD[^2] says to my lord:[^3] "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."[^4]
לְדָוִ֗ד מִ֫זְמ֥וֹר נְאֻ֤ם יְהוָ֨ה ׀ לַֽאדֹנִ֗י שֵׁ֥ב לִֽימִינִ֑י עַד־אָשִׁ֥ית אֹ֝יְבֶ֗יךָ הֲדֹ֣ם לְרַגְלֶֽיךָ׃
The LORD will extend your mighty scepter[^5] from Zion. Rule in the midst of your enemies!
מַטֵּֽה־עֻזְּךָ֗ יִשְׁלַ֣ח יְ֭הוָה מִצִיּ֑וֹן רְ֝דֵ֗ה בְּקֶ֣רֶב אֹיְבֶֽיךָ׃
Your people will offer themselves willingly[^6] on the day of your power,[^7] in holy splendor.[^8] From the womb of the dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.[^9]
עַמְּךָ֣ נְדָבֹת֮ בְּי֢וֹם חֵ֫ילֶ֥ךָ בְּֽהַדְרֵי־קֹ֭דֶשׁ מֵרֶ֣חֶם מִשְׁחָ֑ר לְ֝ךָ֗ טַ֣ל יַלְדֻתֶֽיךָ׃
The LORD has sworn an oath and will not change his mind: "You are a priest forever, after the manner of Melchizedek."[^10]
נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָ֨ה ׀ וְלֹ֥א יִנָּחֵ֗ם אַתָּֽה־כֹהֵ֥ן לְעוֹלָ֑ם עַל־דִּ֝בְרָתִ֗י מַלְכִּי־צֶֽדֶק׃
The Lord is at your right hand;[^11] he will shatter kings on the day of his wrath.
אֲדֹנָ֥י עַל־יְמִֽינְךָ֑ מָחַ֖ץ בְּיוֹם־אַפּ֣וֹ מְלָכִֽים׃
He will judge among the nations, heaping up corpses;[^12] he will shatter heads across the wide earth.[^13]
יָדִ֣ין בַּ֭גּוֹיִם מָלֵ֣א גְוִיּ֑וֹת מָ֥חַץ רֹ֝֗אשׁ עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ רַבָּֽה׃
He will drink from the stream by the way; so he will lift up his head.[^14]
מִ֭נַּחַל בַּדֶּ֣רֶךְ יִשְׁתֶּ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן יָרִ֥ים רֹֽאשׁ׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. In Mark 12:35–37 Jesus' argument takes David as the speaker of the psalm.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *Says*: literally "The declaration of the LORD", the word (*ne'um*) that marks a prophet's oracle ("declares the LORD").
n.3: Hebrew *adoni*, "my lord", a title of respect for a superior, here the king. The vowel points distinguish it from *Adonai*, "the Lord", used of God (as in verse 5).
n.4: The place at the right hand is the place of honor and shared rule; a conquered enemy was put under the victor's feet (compare Joshua 10:24). Jesus quotes this verse in Mark 12:36 (also Matthew 22:44; Luke 20:42–43). It is one of the Old Testament verses most often quoted or echoed in the New Testament: see Acts 2:34–35; 1 Corinthians 15:25; Hebrews 1:13; 10:12–13.
n.5: Literally "the staff of your strength".
n.6: Literally "Your people (are) freewill offerings". The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult, and each of its lines is uncertain.
n.7: Or "of your army", the day the king leads out his forces.
n.8: Or "in holy garments". Some Hebrew manuscripts read "on the holy mountains".
n.9: Literally "From the womb of the dawn, to you (is) the dew of your youth": perhaps the king's youthful strength is renewed each day, like the dew at dawn. Or "your young men will come to you like the dew". The same consonants can be read "I have begotten you", as in 2:7. The Septuagint reads the verse "With you is rule on the day of your power, in the splendor of the holy ones; from the womb, before the morning star, I have begotten you."
n.10: Hebrew *al-divrati malki-tsedeq*. *Al-divrati* probably means "according to the manner of"; it can also mean "on account of", giving "on my account, a righteous king". Melchizedek was king of Salem and "priest of God Most High" (Genesis 14:18–20); his name means "my king is righteous" or "king of righteousness". The Septuagint reads "according to the order of Melchizedek", the wording quoted in Hebrews 5:6, 10; 6:20, and Hebrews 7 explains the verse at length.
n.11: In verse 1 the king sits at the LORD's right hand; here the Lord stands at the king's right hand, as his protector in battle. In verses 5–7 it is not always clear whether the subject is the Lord or the king.
n.12: Literally "he judges among the nations; full of corpses". Or "he fills (the land) with corpses".
n.13: Literally "he shatters head over a wide land". Or "he shatters the ruler of a vast land".
n.14: That is, refreshed, he stands tall in victory.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] I will give thanks to the LORD[^2] with all my heart, in the council of the upright and in the assembly.[^3]
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ אוֹדֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־לֵבָ֑ב בְּס֖וֹד יְשָׁרִ֣ים וְעֵדָֽה׃
Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them.
גְּ֭דֹלִים מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יְהוָ֑ה דְּ֝רוּשִׁ֗ים לְכָל־חֶפְצֵיהֶֽם׃
Splendor and majesty are his work, and his righteousness endures forever.
הוֹד־וְהָדָ֥ר פָּֽעֳל֑וֹ וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ עֹמֶ֥דֶת לָעַֽד׃
He has made his wonders to be remembered;[^4] the LORD is gracious and compassionate.[^5]
זֵ֣כֶר עָ֭שָׂה לְנִפְלְאֹתָ֑יו חַנּ֖וּן וְרַח֣וּם יְהוָֽה׃
He gives food[^6] to those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.
טֶ֭רֶף נָתַ֣ן לִֽירֵאָ֑יו יִזְכֹּ֖ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִיתֽוֹ׃
He has shown his people the power of his works, giving them the inheritance of the nations.
כֹּ֣חַ מַ֭עֲשָׂיו הִגִּ֣יד לְעַמּ֑וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָ֝הֶ֗ם נַחֲלַ֥ת גּוֹיִֽם׃
The works of his hands are faithfulness and justice; all his precepts are trustworthy.
מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יָ֭דָיו אֱמֶ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נֶ֝אֱמָנִ֗ים כָּל־פִּקּוּדָֽיו׃
They are established forever and ever, made in faithfulness and uprightness.
סְמוּכִ֣ים לָעַ֣ד לְעוֹלָ֑ם עֲ֝שׂוּיִ֗ם בֶּאֱמֶ֥ת וְיָשָֽׁר׃
He sent redemption to his people; he has commanded his covenant forever. Holy and awesome is his name.
פְּד֤וּת ׀ שָׁ֘לַ֤ח לְעַמּ֗וֹ צִוָּֽה־לְעוֹלָ֥ם בְּרִית֑וֹ קָד֖וֹשׁ וְנוֹרָ֣א שְׁמֽוֹ׃
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom;[^7] all who practice them have good understanding.[^8] His praise endures forever.
רֵ֘אשִׁ֤ית חָכְמָ֨ה ׀ יִרְאַ֬ת יְהוָ֗ה שֵׂ֣כֶל ט֭וֹב לְכָל־עֹשֵׂיהֶ֑ם תְּ֝הִלָּת֗וֹ עֹמֶ֥דֶת לָעַֽד׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Psalm 111 is an acrostic. After the opening "Praise Yah", each line in the Hebrew begins with the next letter of the alphabet: twenty-two lines, two to a verse in verses 1–8 and three to a verse in verses 9–10. Psalm 112 follows the same pattern, and the two psalms share several phrases (111:3 and 112:3, 9; 111:4 and 112:4).
n.4: Literally "He has made a memorial for his wonders", perhaps the festivals that recall them (compare Exodus 12:14).
n.5: Compare Exodus 34:6.
n.6: Hebrew *teref*, usually "prey", the food of wild animals: perhaps here the food he gave in the wilderness.
n.7: Or "the first principle of wisdom". Compare Proverbs 1:7; 9:10; Job 28:28.
n.8: Literally "good understanding (is) to all who do them", that is, who keep his precepts (verse 7).

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Happy[^2] is the one[^3] who fears the LORD,[^4] who greatly delights in his commands.[^5]
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ אַשְׁרֵי־אִ֭ישׁ יָרֵ֣א אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה בְּ֝מִצְוֺתָ֗יו חָפֵ֥ץ מְאֹֽד׃
His descendants will be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
גִּבּ֣וֹר בָּ֭אָרֶץ יִהְיֶ֣ה זַרְע֑וֹ דּ֖וֹר יְשָׁרִ֣ים יְבֹרָֽךְ׃
Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.[^6]
הוֹן־וָעֹ֥שֶׁר בְּבֵית֑וֹ וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ עֹמֶ֥דֶת לָעַֽד׃
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright;[^7] he is gracious, compassionate and righteous.[^8]
זָ֘רַ֤ח בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ א֭וֹר לַיְשָׁרִ֑ים חַנּ֖וּן וְרַח֣וּם וְצַדִּֽיק׃
It goes well with the one who is generous and lends, who conducts his affairs with justice.[^9]
טֽוֹב־אִ֭ישׁ חוֹנֵ֣ן וּמַלְוֶ֑ה יְכַלְכֵּ֖ל דְּבָרָ֣יו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט׃
For he will never be shaken; the righteous will be remembered forever.[^10]
כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־יִמּ֑וֹט לְזֵ֥כֶר ע֝וֹלָ֗ם יִהְיֶ֥ה צַדִּֽיק׃
He is not afraid of bad news; his heart is steady, trusting in the LORD.
מִשְּׁמוּעָ֣ה רָ֭עָה לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א נָכ֥וֹן לִ֝בּ֗וֹ בָּטֻ֥חַ בַּיהוָֽה׃
His heart is secure; he will not be afraid, until he looks in triumph on his adversaries.[^11]
סָמ֣וּךְ לִ֭בּוֹ לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־יִרְאֶ֣ה בְצָרָֽיו׃
He has scattered abroad; he has given to the needy. His righteousness endures forever;[^12] his horn[^13] will be lifted high in honor.
פִּזַּ֤ר ׀ נָ֘תַ֤ן לָאֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים צִ֭דְקָתוֹ עֹמֶ֣דֶת לָעַ֑ד קַ֝רְנ֗וֹ תָּר֥וּם בְּכָבֽוֹד׃
The wicked will see it and be angry; he will grind his teeth and melt away. The desire of the wicked will perish.
רָ֘שָׁ֤ע יִרְאֶ֨ה ׀ וְכָעָ֗ס שִׁנָּ֣יו יַחֲרֹ֣ק וְנָמָ֑ס תַּאֲוַ֖ת רְשָׁעִ֣ים תֹּאבֵֽד׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH.
n.2: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.3: Literally "the man".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Psalm 112 is an acrostic, like Psalm 111. After the opening "Praise Yah", each line in the Hebrew begins with the next letter of the alphabet: twenty-two lines, two to a verse in verses 1–8 and three to a verse in verses 9–10.
n.6: Psalm 111:3 says this of God's righteousness. Here it is said of the one who fears him (also in verse 9).
n.7: Or "He dawns in the darkness as a light for the upright".
n.8: Psalm 111:4 says that the LORD is "gracious and compassionate". Here the words probably describe the one who fears him.
n.9: Literally "Good (is) a man who is gracious and lends; he sustains his matters with justice".
n.10: Literally "will be for a memorial forever".
n.11: Literally "until he looks on his adversaries", that is, sees their defeat.
n.12: 2 Corinthians 9:9 quotes the first half of this verse.
n.13: A symbol of strength and dignity, like the horns of a wild ox.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Praise, you servants of the LORD;[^2] praise the name of the LORD.[^3]
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ הַ֭לְלוּ עַבְדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הֽ͏ַ֝לְלוּ אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
May the name of the LORD be blessed, from now on and forever.
יְהִ֤י שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה מְבֹרָ֑ךְ מֵֽ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the LORD is to be praised.
מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ עַד־מְבוֹא֑וֹ מְ֝הֻלָּ֗ל שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃
The LORD is high above all nations; his glory is above the heavens.
רָ֖ם עַל־כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם ׀ יְהוָ֑ה עַ֖ל הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃
Who is like the LORD our God, who is enthroned on high,
מִ֭י כַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ הַֽמַּגְבִּיהִ֥י לָשָֽׁבֶת׃
who stoops down to look on the heavens and the earth?[^4]
הַֽמַּשְׁפִּילִ֥י לִרְא֑וֹת בַּשָּׁמַ֥יִם וּבָאָֽרֶץ׃
He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap,[^5]
מְקִֽימִ֣י מֵעָפָ֣ר דָּ֑ל מֵֽ֝אַשְׁפֹּ֗ת יָרִ֥ים אֶבְיֽוֹן׃
to seat them with nobles, with the nobles of his people.[^6]
לְהוֹשִׁיבִ֥י עִם־נְדִיבִ֑ים עִ֝֗ם נְדִיבֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹ׃
He gives the childless woman a home, as a happy mother of children.[^7] Praise the LORD!
מֽוֹשִׁיבִ֨י ׀ עֲקֶ֬רֶת הַבַּ֗יִת אֵֽם־הַבָּנִ֥ים שְׂמֵחָ֗ה הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 9.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Psalms 113–118 are known in Jewish tradition as the Hallel ("praise"), sung at Passover and the other festivals. Psalms 113–114 are sung before the Passover meal and 115–118 after it; the hymn sung at the end of the Last Supper (Mark 14:26) may have been part of it.
n.4: Literally "who makes high to sit, who makes low to see, in the heavens and on the earth". Or "who sits enthroned on high and looks far down on the heavens and the earth".
n.5: Or "the garbage heap", the refuse dump outside a town, where beggars sat.
n.6: Verses 7–8 are nearly the same as Hannah's song in 1 Samuel 2:8.
n.7: Literally "who seats the barren woman of the house, a joyful mother of sons". Compare 1 Samuel 2:5.

v: When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech,[^1]
בְּצֵ֣את יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם בֵּ֥ית יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב מֵעַ֥ם לֹעֵֽז׃
Judah became his sanctuary,[^2] Israel his dominion.
הָיְתָ֣ה יְהוּדָ֣ה לְקָדְשׁ֑וֹ יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל מַמְשְׁלוֹתָֽיו׃
The sea looked and fled; the Jordan turned back.[^3]
הַיָּ֣ם רָ֭אָה וַיָּנֹ֑ס הַ֝יַּרְדֵּ֗ן יִסֹּ֥ב לְאָחֽוֹר׃
The mountains skipped like rams, the hills like lambs.[^4]
הֶֽ֭הָרִים רָקְד֣וּ כְאֵילִ֑ים גְּ֝בָע֗וֹת כִּבְנֵי־צֹֽאן׃
What is wrong with you, sea, that you flee? Jordan, that you turn back?
מַה־לְּךָ֣ הַ֭יָּם כִּ֣י תָנ֑וּס הַ֝יַּרְדֵּ֗ן תִּסֹּ֥ב לְאָחֽוֹר׃
You mountains, that you skip like rams? You hills, like lambs?
הֶֽ֭הָרִים תִּרְקְד֣וּ כְאֵילִ֑ים גְּ֝בָע֗וֹת כִּבְנֵי־צֹֽאן׃
Tremble,[^5] earth, before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
מִלִּפְנֵ֣י אָ֭דוֹן ח֣וּלִי אָ֑רֶץ מִ֝לִּפְנֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
who turned the rock into a pool of water, the flint into a spring of water.[^6]
הַהֹפְכִ֣י הַצּ֣וּר אֲגַם־מָ֑יִם חַ֝לָּמִ֗ישׁ לְמַעְיְנוֹ־מָֽיִם׃

n.1: The Septuagint joins Psalms 114 and 115 into a single psalm, and it divides Psalm 116 into two (116:1–9 and 116:10–19).
n.2: Or "his holy people". God is not named until verse 7.
n.3: The crossing of the Red Sea (Exodus 14:21–22) and of the Jordan (Joshua 3:14–17).
n.4: Literally "like the young of the flock". Also in verse 6.
n.5: Or "Writhe", as in labor pains.
n.6: Compare Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:8–11.

v: Not to us, LORD,[^1] not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your faithful love,[^2] because of your faithfulness.
לֹ֤א לָ֥נוּ יְהוָ֗ה לֹ֫א לָ֥נוּ כִּֽי־לְ֭שִׁמְךָ תֵּ֣ן כָּב֑וֹד עַל־חַ֝סְדְּךָ֗ עַל־אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃
Why should the nations say, "Where, then, is their God?"
לָ֭מָּה יֹאמְר֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם אַיֵּה־נָ֝֗א אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
Our God is in the heavens; he does whatever he pleases.
וֵֽאלֹהֵ֥ינוּ בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־חָפֵ֣ץ עָשָֽׂה׃
Their idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
עֲ‍ֽ֭צַבֵּיהֶם כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗ה יְדֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃
They have mouths, but cannot speak; they have eyes, but cannot see.
פֶּֽה־לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ עֵינַ֥יִם לָ֝הֶ֗ם וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֽוּ׃
They have ears, but cannot hear; they have noses, but cannot smell.
אָזְנַ֣יִם לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ אַ֥ף לָ֝הֶ֗ם וְלֹ֣א יְרִיחֽוּן׃
They have hands, but cannot feel; feet, but cannot walk; they make no sound in their throats.
יְדֵיהֶ֤ם ׀ וְלֹ֬א יְמִישׁ֗וּן רַ֭גְלֵיהֶם וְלֹ֣א יְהַלֵּ֑כוּ לֹֽא־יֶ֝הְגּ֗וּ בִּגְרוֹנָֽם׃
Those who make them will become like them, and so will all who trust in them.[^3]
כְּ֭מוֹהֶם יִהְי֣וּ עֹשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־בֹּטֵ֣חַ בָּהֶֽם׃
Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield.[^4]
יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל בְּטַ֣ח בַּיהוָ֑ה עֶזְרָ֖ם וּמָגִנָּ֣ם הֽוּא׃
House of Aaron, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield.
בֵּ֣ית אַ֭הֲרֹן בִּטְח֣וּ בַיהוָ֑ה עֶזְרָ֖ם וּמָגִנָּ֣ם הֽוּא׃
You who fear the LORD, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield.
יִרְאֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה בִּטְח֣וּ בַיהוָ֑ה עֶזְרָ֖ם וּמָגִנָּ֣ם הֽוּא׃
The LORD has remembered us; he will bless. He will bless the house of Israel; he will bless the house of Aaron.
יְהוָה֮ זְכָרָ֢נוּ יְבָ֫רֵ֥ךְ יְ֭בָרֵךְ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְ֝בָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת־בֵּ֥ית אַהֲרֹֽן׃
He will bless those who fear the LORD, the small together with the great.
יְ֭בָרֵךְ יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַ֝קְּטַנִּ֗ים עִם־הַגְּדֹלִֽים׃
May the LORD give you increase, you and your children.[^5]
יֹסֵ֣ף יְהוָ֣ה עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם עֲ֝לֵיכֶ֗ם וְעַל־בְּנֵיכֶֽם׃
May you be blessed by the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
בְּרוּכִ֣ים אַ֭תֶּם לַיהוָ֑ה עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃
The heavens are the heavens of the LORD,[^6] but the earth he has given to human beings.[^7]
הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם שָׁ֭מַיִם לַיהוָ֑ה וְ֝הָאָ֗רֶץ נָתַ֥ן לִבְנֵי־אָדָֽם׃
It is not the dead who praise the LORD,[^8] nor any who go down into silence.[^9]
לֹ֣א הַ֭מֵּתִים יְהַֽלְלוּ־יָ֑הּ וְ֝לֹ֗א כָּל־יֹרְדֵ֥י דוּמָֽה׃
But we will bless the LORD from now on and forever. Praise the LORD![^10]
וַאֲנַ֤חְנוּ ׀ נְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ יָ֗הּ מֵֽעַתָּ֥ה וְעַד־עוֹלָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. The Septuagint makes Psalm 115 part of Psalm 114 (see the note on 114:1). Verses 4–11 appear again, with small differences, in 135:15–20.
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.3: Or "May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them."
n.4: Verses 9–11 call on Israel, the priests (the house of Aaron) and all who fear the LORD to trust in him. Each verse ends with the same refrain, which turns to speak of them as "their". Compare 118:2–4.
n.5: Literally "May the LORD add to you, to you and to your sons".
n.6: Literally "The heavens are heavens for the LORD".
n.7: Literally "to the sons of *adam* (humankind)".
n.8: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH. Also in verse 18.
n.9: That is, into the silent world of the dead (compare 94:17).
n.10: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah".

v: I love the LORD,[^1] for he hears my voice, my pleas for mercy.[^2]
אָ֭הַבְתִּי כִּֽי־יִשְׁמַ֥ע ׀ יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־ק֝וֹלִ֗י תַּחֲנוּנָֽי׃
Because he has turned his ear to me, I will call on him as long as I live.[^3]
כִּֽי־הִטָּ֣ה אָזְנ֣וֹ לִ֑י וּבְיָמַ֥י אֶקְרָֽא׃
The cords of death surrounded me; the distress of Sheol[^4] found me; I found trouble and sorrow.
אֲפָפ֤וּנִי ׀ חֶבְלֵי־מָ֗וֶת וּמְצָרֵ֣י שְׁא֣וֹל מְצָא֑וּנִי צָרָ֖ה וְיָג֣וֹן אֶמְצָֽא׃
Then I called on the name of the LORD: "Please, LORD, rescue my life!"[^5]
וּבְשֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֶקְרָ֑א אָנָּ֥ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה מַלְּטָ֥ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
The LORD is gracious and righteous; our God is compassionate.
חַנּ֣וּן יְהֹוָ֣ה וְצַדִּ֑יק וֵ֖אלֹהֵ֣ינוּ מְרַחֵֽם׃
The LORD protects the simple; I was brought low, and he saved me.
שֹׁמֵ֣ר פְּתָאיִ֣ם יְהֹוָ֑ה דַּ֝לּוֹתִ֗י וְלִ֣י יְהוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
Return to your rest, my soul,[^6] for the LORD has dealt generously with you.
שׁוּבִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי לִמְנוּחָ֑יְכִי כִּֽי־יְ֝הוָ֗ה גָּמַ֥ל עָלָֽיְכִי׃
For you have rescued my life from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
כִּ֤י חִלַּ֥צְתָּ נַפְשִׁ֗י מִ֫מָּ֥וֶת אֶת־עֵינִ֥י מִן־דִּמְעָ֑ה אֶת־רַגְלִ֥י מִדֶּֽחִי׃
I will walk before the LORD in the land of the living.[^7]
אֶ֭תְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּ֝אַרְצ֗וֹת הַֽחַיִּֽים׃
I kept faith, even when I said,[^8] "I am greatly afflicted."
הֶ֭אֱמַנְתִּי כִּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֲ֝נִ֗י עָנִ֥יתִי מְאֹֽד׃
I said in my alarm, "Everyone is a liar."[^9]
אֲ֭נִי אָמַ֣רְתִּי בְחָפְזִ֑י כָּֽל־הָאָדָ֥ם כֹּזֵֽב׃
What can I give back to the LORD for all his goodness to me?
מָֽה־אָשִׁ֥יב לַיהוָ֑ה כָּֽל־תַּגְמוּל֥וֹהִי עָלָֽי׃
I will lift up the cup of salvation[^10] and call on the name of the LORD.
כּוֹס־יְשׁוּע֥וֹת אֶשָּׂ֑א וּבְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָֽא׃
I will fulfill my vows to the LORD in the presence of all his people.
נְ֭דָרַי לַיהוָ֣ה אֲשַׁלֵּ֑ם נֶגְדָה־נָּ֝֗א לְכָל־עַמּֽוֹ׃
Precious in the eyes of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.[^11]
יָ֭קָר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַ֝מָּ֗וְתָה לַחֲסִידָֽיו׃
Please, LORD, truly I am your servant; I am your servant, the son of your female servant.[^12] You have loosed my bonds.
אֽ͏ָנָּ֣ה יְהוָה֮ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֢י עַ֫בְדֶּ֥ךָ אֲ‍ֽנִי־עַ֭בְדְּךָ בֶּן־אֲמָתֶ֑ךָ פִּ֝תַּ֗חְתָּ לְמוֹסֵרָֽי׃
To you I will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving,[^13] and call on the name of the LORD.
לְֽךָ־אֶ֭זְבַּח זֶ֣בַח תּוֹדָ֑ה וּבְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָֽא׃
I will fulfill my vows to the LORD in the presence of all his people,
נְ֭דָרַי לַיהוָ֣ה אֲשַׁלֵּ֑ם נֶגְדָה־נָּ֝֗א לְכָל־עַמּֽוֹ׃
in the courts of the house of the LORD, in your midst, Jerusalem. Praise the LORD![^14]
בְּחַצְר֤וֹת ׀ בֵּ֤ית יְהוָ֗ה בְּֽת֘וֹכֵ֤כִי יְֽרוּשָׁלִָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *I love the LORD*: literally "I love, for the LORD hears". The Septuagint divides this psalm into two, verses 1–9 and verses 10–19 (see the note on 114:1).
n.2: Literally "my voice, my supplications".
n.3: Literally "in my days".
n.4: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. *The distress*: or "the straits", "the pangs". Compare 18:5–6 (18:4–5 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 7 and 8.
n.6: Literally "to your resting places". The psalmist speaks to his own soul (*nephesh*), as in 42:6 (42:5 in most English Bibles).
n.7: Literally "in the lands of the living". Compare 56:14 (56:13 in most English Bibles).
n.8: Literally "I believed, for I speak". Or "I believed, even when I spoke". The Septuagint reads "I believed, therefore I spoke", the wording quoted in 2 Corinthians 4:13.
n.9: Literally "All humankind (*adam*) is a liar". Compare Romans 3:4.
n.10: Literally "the cup of salvations", perhaps a drink offering poured out, or a cup raised in thanksgiving for being rescued.
n.11: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". *Precious*: that is, costly: their death is no small matter to him.
n.12: That is, a servant born in the household, and so bound to it for life (compare 86:16).
n.13: Hebrew *todah*: a sacrifice given in thanksgiving (Leviticus 7:12).
n.14: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH.

v: Praise the LORD,[^1] all nations! Extol him, all peoples![^2]
הַֽלְל֣וּ אֶת־יְ֭הוָה כָּל־גּוֹיִ֑ם שַׁ֝בְּח֗וּהוּ כָּל־הָאֻמִּֽים׃
For great is his faithful love[^3] toward us,[^4] and the faithfulness of the LORD endures forever. Praise the LORD![^5]
כִּ֥י גָ֘בַ֤ר עָלֵ֨ינוּ ׀ חַסְדּ֗וֹ וֶֽאֱמֶת־יְהוָ֥ה לְעוֹלָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. Psalm 117 is the shortest psalm.
n.2: Romans 15:11 quotes this verse.
n.3: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.4: Literally "is mighty over us".
n.5: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH.

v: Give thanks to the LORD,[^1] for he is good; his faithful love[^2] endures forever.[^3]
הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Let Israel say, "His faithful love endures forever."
יֹֽאמַר־נָ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Let the house of Aaron say, "His faithful love endures forever."
יֹֽאמְרוּ־נָ֥א בֵֽית־אַהֲרֹ֑ן כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Let those who fear the LORD say, "His faithful love endures forever."[^4]
יֹֽאמְרוּ־נָ֭א יִרְאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
In my distress I called on the LORD;[^5] the LORD answered me and set me in a broad place.[^6]
מִֽן־הַ֭מֵּצַ֥ר קָרָ֣אתִי יָּ֑הּ עָנָ֖נִי בַמֶּרְחָ֣ב יָֽהּ׃
The LORD is for me; I will not be afraid. What can anyone[^7] do to me?[^8]
יְהוָ֣ה לִ֭י לֹ֣א אִירָ֑א מַה־יַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לִ֣י אָדָֽם׃
The LORD is for me as my helper;[^9] I will look in triumph on those who hate me.
יְהוָ֣ה לִ֭י בְּעֹזְרָ֑י וַ֝אֲנִ֗י אֶרְאֶ֥ה בְשֹׂנְאָֽי׃
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in human beings.
ט֗וֹב לַחֲס֥וֹת בַּיהוָ֑ה מִ֝בְּטֹ֗חַ בָּאָדָֽם׃
It is better to take refuge in the LORD than to trust in nobles.
ט֗וֹב לַחֲס֥וֹת בַּיהוָ֑ה מִ֝בְּטֹ֗חַ בִּנְדִיבִֽים׃
All the nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them off.[^10]
כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם סְבָב֑וּנִי בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them off.
סַבּ֥וּנִי גַם־סְבָב֑וּנִי בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
They surrounded me like bees; they died out like a fire of thorns.[^11] In the name of the LORD I cut them off.
סַבּ֤וּנִי כִדְבוֹרִ֗ים דֹּ֭עֲכוּ כְּאֵ֣שׁ קוֹצִ֑ים בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲמִילַֽם׃
You pushed me hard to make me fall,[^12] but the LORD helped me.
דַּחֹ֣ה דְחִיתַ֣נִי לִנְפֹּ֑ל וַ֖יהוָ֣ה עֲזָרָֽנִי׃
The LORD is my strength and my song;[^13] he has become my salvation.
עָזִּ֣י וְזִמְרָ֣ת יָ֑הּ וַֽיְהִי־לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה׃
The sound of joyful shouting and salvation is in the tents of the righteous: "The right hand of the LORD does mighty deeds!
ק֤וֹל ׀ רִנָּ֬ה וִֽישׁוּעָ֗ה בְּאָהֳלֵ֥י צַדִּיקִ֑ים יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל׃
The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does mighty deeds!"
יְמִ֣ין יְ֭הוָה רוֹמֵמָ֑ה יְמִ֥ין יְ֝הוָה עֹ֣שָׂה חָֽיִל׃
I will not die, but live, and I will tell of the works of the LORD.
לֹֽא־אָמ֥וּת כִּי־אֶֽחְיֶ֑ה וַ֝אֲסַפֵּ֗ר מַֽעֲשֵׂ֥י יָֽהּ׃
The LORD has disciplined me severely, but he has not given me over to death.
יַסֹּ֣ר יִסְּרַ֣נִּי יָּ֑הּ וְ֝לַמָּ֗וֶת לֹ֣א נְתָנָֽנִי׃
Open the gates of righteousness for me; I will enter through them and give thanks to the LORD.
פִּתְחוּ־לִ֥י שַׁעֲרֵי־צֶ֑דֶק אָֽבֹא־בָ֝ם אוֹדֶ֥ה יָֽהּ׃
This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous will enter through it.
זֶֽה־הַשַּׁ֥עַר לַיהוָ֑ה צַ֝דִּיקִ֗ים יָבֹ֥אוּ בֽוֹ׃
I will give thanks to you, for you have answered me, and have become my salvation.
א֭וֹדְךָ כִּ֣י עֲנִיתָ֑נִי וַתְּהִי־לִ֝֗י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה׃
The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.[^14]
אֶ֭בֶן מָאֲס֣וּ הַבּוֹנִ֑ים הָ֝יְתָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ פִּנָּֽה׃
This was the LORD's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes.[^15]
מֵאֵ֣ת יְ֭הוָה הָ֣יְתָה זֹּ֑את הִ֖יא נִפְלָ֣את בְּעֵינֵֽינוּ׃
This is the day that the LORD has made;[^16] let us rejoice and be glad in it.
זֶה־הַ֭יּוֹם עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה נָגִ֖ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֣ה בֽוֹ׃
Please, LORD, save us![^17] Please, LORD, give us success!
אָֽנָּ֣א יְ֭הוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה נָּ֑א אָֽנָּ֥א יְ֝הוָ֗ה הַצְלִ֘יחָ֥ה נָּֽא׃
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD![^18] We bless you[^19] from the house of the LORD.
בָּר֣וּךְ הַ֭בָּא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה בֵּ֝רַֽכְנוּכֶ֗ם מִבֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃
The LORD is God, and he has given us light. Bind the festival sacrifice with cords to the horns of the altar.[^20]
אֵ֤ל ׀ יְהוָה֮ וַיָּ֢אֶ֫ר לָ֥נוּ אִסְרוּ־חַ֥ג בַּעֲבֹתִ֑ים עַד־קַ֝רְנ֗וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
You are my God, and I will give thanks to you; my God, I will exalt you.
אֵלִ֣י אַתָּ֣ה וְאוֹדֶ֑ךָּ אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אֲרוֹמְמֶֽךָּ׃
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love endures forever.
הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.3: Literally "for his faithful love is forever". Also in verses 2–4 and 29. The same refrain runs through Psalm 136.
n.4: Verses 2–4 call on Israel, the priests (the house of Aaron) and all who fear the LORD, as in 115:9–11.
n.5: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH. Also in verses 14 and 17–19.
n.6: Literally "Yah answered me in the broad place". *Distress* is literally "the narrow place".
n.7: Hebrew *adam*, "a human being".
n.8: Hebrews 13:6 quotes this verse from the Septuagint, which reads "The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid."
n.9: Literally "The LORD is for me among my helpers".
n.10: Hebrew *amilam*, a rare form, perhaps "I cut them off" or "I fended them off". Also in verses 11 and 12. The verb may be the one used for circumcision.
n.11: That is, as quickly as a fire of dry thorns. The Septuagint reads "they blazed up like a fire among thorns".
n.12: Literally "You pushed, pushed me to fall", speaking to the enemy. The Septuagint reads "I was pushed hard, so that I fell".
n.13: Or "my might". Hebrew *zimrah*. This line repeats Exodus 15:2 (compare Isaiah 12:2).
n.14: Literally "the head of the corner": either a cornerstone in the foundation or the capstone at the top of a wall. Jesus quotes verses 22–23 in Mark 12:10–11 (also Matthew 21:42; Luke 20:17), and Acts 4:11 and 1 Peter 2:7 apply verse 22 to him.
n.15: Literally "From the LORD this has come".
n.16: Or "This is the day on which the LORD has acted". *In it*: or "in him".
n.17: Hebrew *hoshi'ah na*, "save, please", the phrase that became "Hosanna" (Mark 11:9–10). The Hebrew does not say whom.
n.18: The crowds greet Jesus with this line in Mark 11:9 (also Matthew 21:9; Luke 19:38; John 12:13), and Jesus quotes it in Matthew 23:39 and Luke 13:35.
n.19: "You" is plural: the priests bless those who come up to the temple.
n.20: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "Bind the festival with cords (or branches) up to the horns of the altar", perhaps the animal for the festival sacrifice, or a festal procession with branches as far as the altar. The horns of the altar were the projections at its four corners (Exodus 27:2).

v: Happy[^1] are those whose way is blameless,[^2] who walk in the law[^3] of the LORD.[^4]
אַשְׁרֵ֥י תְמִֽימֵי־דָ֑רֶךְ הַֽ֝הֹלְכִ֗ים בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
Happy are those who keep his statutes,[^5] who seek him with all their heart.
אַ֭שְׁרֵי נֹצְרֵ֥י עֵדֹתָ֗יו בְּכָל־לֵ֥ב יִדְרְשֽׁוּהוּ׃
They do no wrong; they walk in his ways.
אַ֭ף לֹֽא־פָעֲל֣וּ עַוְלָ֑ה בִּדְרָכָ֥יו הָלָֽכוּ׃
You have commanded your precepts, to be kept with all care.
אַ֭תָּה צִוִּ֥יתָה פִקֻּדֶ֗יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְאֹֽד׃
Oh, that my ways were steady in keeping your decrees!
אַ֭חֲלַי יִכֹּ֥נוּ דְרָכָ֗י לִשְׁמֹ֥ר חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Then I would not be put to shame, when I look to all your commands.
אָ֥ז לֹא־אֵב֑וֹשׁ בְּ֝הַבִּיטִ֗י אֶל־כָּל־מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
I will give thanks to you with an upright heart, as I learn your righteous rulings.[^6]
א֭וֹדְךָ בְּיֹ֣שֶׁר לֵבָ֑ב בְּ֝לָמְדִ֗י מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
I will keep your decrees; do not utterly forsake me.
אֶת־חֻקֶּ֥יךָ אֶשְׁמֹ֑ר אַֽל־תַּעַזְבֵ֥נִי עַד־מְאֹֽד׃
How can a young man keep his path pure?[^7] By guarding it according to your word.
בַּמֶּ֣ה יְזַכֶּה־נַּ֭עַר אֶת־אָרְח֑וֹ לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
With all my heart I seek you; do not let me stray from your commands.
בְּכָל־לִבִּ֥י דְרַשְׁתִּ֑יךָ אַל־תַּ֝שְׁגֵּ֗נִי מִמִּצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
I have treasured your promise[^8] in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
בְּ֭לִבִּי צָפַ֣נְתִּי אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ לְ֝מַ֗עַן לֹ֣א אֶֽחֱטָא־לָֽךְ׃
Blessed are you, LORD; teach me your decrees.
בָּר֖וּךְ אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֗ה לַמְּדֵ֥נִי חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
With my lips I recount all the rulings of your mouth.
בִּשְׂפָתַ֥י סִפַּ֑רְתִּי כֹּ֝֗ל מִשְׁפְּטֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
I rejoice in the way of your statutes as much as in all riches.
בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ עֵדְוֺתֶ֥יךָ שַּׂ֗[t]שְׂתִּי כְּעַ֣ל כָּל־הֽוֹן׃
I will meditate on your precepts and fix my eyes on your paths.
בְּפִקֻּדֶ֥יךָ אָשִׂ֑יחָה וְ֝אַבִּ֗יטָה אֹרְחֹתֶֽיךָ׃
I will delight in your decrees; I will not forget your word.
בְּחֻקֹּתֶ֥יךָ אֶֽשְׁתַּעֲשָׁ֑ע לֹ֖א אֶשְׁכַּ֣ח דְּבָרֶֽךָ׃
Deal generously with your servant,[^9] so that I may live and keep your word.
גְּמֹ֖ל עַֽל־עַבְדְּךָ֥ אֶֽחְיֶ֗ה וְאֶשְׁמְרָ֥ה דְבָרֶֽךָ׃
Open my eyes, so that I may see wonderful things in your law.
גַּל־עֵינַ֥י וְאַבִּ֑יטָה נִ֝פְלָא֗וֹת מִתּוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
I am a stranger[^10] on the earth; do not hide your commands from me.
גֵּ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י בָאָ֑רֶץ אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֥ר מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
My soul[^11] is crushed with longing for your rulings at all times.
גָּרְסָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֣י לְתַאֲבָ֑ה אֶֽל־מִשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ בְכָל־עֵֽת׃
You rebuke the arrogant, the accursed, who stray from your commands.[^12]
גָּ֭עַרְתָּ זֵדִ֣ים אֲרוּרִ֑ים הַ֝שֹּׁגִים מִמִּצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
Take scorn and contempt away from me,[^13] for I keep your statutes.
גַּ֣ל מֵֽ֭עָלַי חֶרְפָּ֣ה וָב֑וּז כִּ֖י עֵדֹתֶ֣יךָ נָצָֽרְתִּי׃
Even though rulers sit and talk together against me, your servant meditates on your decrees.
גַּ֤ם יָֽשְׁב֣וּ שָׂ֭רִים בִּ֣י נִדְבָּ֑רוּ עַ֝בְדְּךָ֗ יָשִׂ֥יחַ בְּחֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Your statutes are my delight; they are my counselors.[^14]
גַּֽם־עֵ֭דֹתֶיךָ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָ֗י אַנְשֵׁ֥י עֲצָתִֽי׃
My soul clings to the dust;[^15] give me life[^16] according to your word.
דָּֽבְקָ֣ה לֶעָפָ֣ר נַפְשִׁ֑י חַ֝יֵּ֗נִי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
I told you of my ways, and you answered me; teach me your decrees.
דְּרָכַ֣י סִ֭פַּרְתִּי וַֽתַּעֲנֵ֗נִי לַמְּדֵ֥נִי חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wonders.
דֶּֽרֶךְ־פִּקּוּדֶ֥יךָ הֲבִינֵ֑נִי וְ֝אָשִׂ֗יחָה בְּנִפְלְאוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
My soul weeps[^17] from grief; raise me up according to your word.
דָּלְפָ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִתּוּגָ֑ה קַ֝יְּמֵ֗נִי כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
Keep me from the way of falsehood, and graciously give me your law.
דֶּֽרֶךְ־שֶׁ֭קֶר הָסֵ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְֽתוֹרָתְךָ֥ חָנֵּֽנִי׃
I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I have set your rulings before me.[^18]
דֶּֽרֶךְ־אֱמוּנָ֥ה בָחָ֑רְתִּי מִשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ שִׁוִּֽיתִי׃
I cling to your statutes; LORD, do not let me be put to shame.
דָּבַ֥קְתִּי בְעֵֽדְוֺתֶ֑יךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַל־תְּבִישֵֽׁנִי׃
I will run in the way of your commands, for you set my heart free.[^19]
דֶּֽרֶךְ־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אָר֑וּץ כִּ֖י תַרְחִ֣יב לִבִּֽי׃
Teach me, LORD, the way of your decrees,[^20] and I will keep it to the end.[^21]
הוֹרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֥רֶךְ חֻקֶּ֗יךָ וְאֶצְּרֶ֥נָּה עֵֽקֶב׃
Give me understanding, and I will keep your law and obey it with all my heart.
הֲ֭בִינֵנִי וְאֶצְּרָ֥ה תֽוֹרָתֶ֗ךָ וְאֶשְׁמְרֶ֥נָּה בְכָל־לֵֽב׃
Lead me in the path of your commands, for I delight in it.
הַ֭דְרִיכֵנִי בִּנְתִ֣יב מִצְוֺתֶ֑יךָ כִּי־ב֥וֹ חָפָֽצְתִּי׃
Turn my heart to your statutes, and not to selfish gain.
הַט־לִ֭בִּי אֶל־עֵדְוֺתֶ֗יךָ וְאַ֣ל אֶל־בָּֽצַע׃
Turn my eyes away from looking at what is worthless; give me life in your way.
הַעֲבֵ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי מֵרְא֣וֹת שָׁ֑וְא בִּדְרָכֶ֥ךָ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
Confirm to your servant your promise, which is for those who fear you.[^22]
הָקֵ֣ם לְ֭עַבְדְּךָ אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ אֲ֝שֶׁ֗ר לְיִרְאָתֶֽךָ׃
Turn away the disgrace that I dread, for your rulings are good.
הַעֲבֵ֣ר חֶ֭רְפָּתִי אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָגֹ֑רְתִּי כִּ֖י מִשְׁפָּטֶ֣יךָ טוֹבִֽים׃
See, I long for your precepts; in your righteousness give me life.
הִ֭נֵּה תָּאַ֣בְתִּי לְפִקֻּדֶ֑יךָ בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֥ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
May your faithful love[^23] come to me, LORD,[^24] your salvation according to your promise.
וִֽיבֹאֻ֣נִי חֲסָדֶ֣ךָ יְהוָ֑ה תְּ֝שׁ֥וּעָתְךָ֗ כְּאִמְרָתֶֽךָ׃
Then I will have an answer for the one who taunts me,[^25] for I trust in your word.
וְאֶֽעֱנֶ֣ה חֹרְפִ֣י דָבָ֑ר כִּֽי־בָ֝טַחְתִּי בִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
Do not take the word of truth utterly out of my mouth, for I hope in your rulings.
וְֽאַל־תַּצֵּ֬ל מִפִּ֣י דְבַר־אֱמֶ֣ת עַד־מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֖י לְמִשְׁפָּטֶ֣ךָ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
I will keep your law continually, forever and ever.
וְאֶשְׁמְרָ֖ה תוֹרָתְךָ֥ תָמִ֗יד לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
I will walk about in freedom,[^26] for I have sought your precepts.
וְאֶתְהַלְּכָ֥ה בָרְחָבָ֑ה כִּ֖י פִקֻּדֶ֣יךָ דָרָֽשְׁתִּי׃
I will speak of your statutes before kings, and I will not be put to shame.
וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה בְ֭עֵדֹתֶיךָ נֶ֥גֶד מְלָכִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א אֵבֽוֹשׁ׃
I will delight in your commands, which I love.
וְאֶשְׁתַּֽעֲשַׁ֥ע בְּמִצְוֺתֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהָֽבְתִּי׃
I will lift up my hands to your commands, which I love,[^27] and I will meditate on your decrees.
וְאֶשָּֽׂא־כַפַּ֗י אֶֽל־מִ֭צְוֺתֶיךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָהָ֗בְתִּי וְאָשִׂ֥יחָה בְחֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Remember your word to your servant,[^28] by which you have given me hope.
זְכֹר־דָּבָ֥ר לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ עַ֝֗ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽחַלְתָּֽנִי׃
This is my comfort in my affliction: that your promise gives me life.
זֹ֣את נֶחָמָתִ֣י בְעָנְיִ֑י כִּ֖י אִמְרָתְךָ֣ חִיָּֽתְנִי׃
The arrogant mock me without restraint, but I do not turn away from your law.
זֵ֭דִים הֱלִיצֻ֣נִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד מִ֝תּ֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א נָטִֽיתִי׃
I remember your rulings of old, LORD, and I take comfort.
זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי מִשְׁפָּטֶ֖יךָ מֵעוֹלָ֥ם ׀ יְהוָ֗ה וָֽאֶתְנֶחָֽם׃
Burning anger seizes me because of the wicked, who forsake your law.
זַלְעָפָ֣ה אֲ֭חָזַתְנִי מֵרְשָׁעִ֑ים עֹ֝זְבֵ֗י תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
Your decrees have been my songs in the house where I live as a stranger.[^29]
זְ֭מִרוֹת הָֽיוּ־לִ֥י חֻקֶּ֗יךָ בְּבֵ֣ית מְגוּרָֽי׃
In the night I remember your name, LORD, and I keep your law.
זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי בַלַּ֣יְלָה שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה וָֽ֝אֶשְׁמְרָ֗ה תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
This has been my lot: I have kept your precepts.[^30]
זֹ֥את הָֽיְתָה־לִּ֑י כִּ֖י פִקֻּדֶ֣יךָ נָצָֽרְתִּי׃
The LORD is my portion;[^31] I have promised to keep your words.[^32]
חֶלְקִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אָמַ֗רְתִּי לִשְׁמֹ֥ר דְּבָרֶֽיךָ׃
I have sought your favor[^33] with all my heart; be gracious to me according to your promise.
חִלִּ֣יתִי פָנֶ֣יךָ בְכָל־לֵ֑ב חָ֝נֵּ֗נִי כְּאִמְרָתֶֽךָ׃
I have thought about my ways, and turned my feet to your statutes.
חִשַּׁ֥בְתִּי דְרָכָ֑י וָאָשִׁ֥יבָה רַ֝גְלַ֗י אֶל־עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
I hurry and do not delay to keep your commands.
חַ֭שְׁתִּי וְלֹ֣א הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְתִּי לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
The cords of the wicked are wrapped around me,[^34] but I do not forget your law.
חֶבְלֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֣ים עִוְּדֻ֑נִי תּ֥֝וֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
At midnight I rise to give thanks to you for your righteous rulings.
חֲצֽוֹת־לַ֗יְלָה אָ֭קוּם לְהוֹד֣וֹת לָ֑ךְ עַ֝֗ל מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
I am a companion of all who fear you, of those who keep your precepts.
חָבֵ֣ר אָ֭נִי לְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְרֵא֑וּךָ וּ֝לְשֹׁמְרֵ֗י פִּקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
The earth is full of your faithful love, LORD; teach me your decrees.
חַסְדְּךָ֣ יְ֭הוָה מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֗רֶץ חֻקֶּ֥יךָ לַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
You have dealt well with your servant,[^35] LORD, according to your word.
ט֭וֹב עָשִׂ֣יתָ עִֽם־עַבְדְּךָ֑ יְ֝הוָ֗ה כִּדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
Teach me good judgment[^36] and knowledge, for I believe in your commands.
ט֤וּב טַ֣עַם וָדַ֣עַת לַמְּדֵ֑נִי כִּ֖י בְמִצְוֺתֶ֣יךָ הֶאֱמָֽנְתִּי׃
Before I was afflicted I went astray, but now I keep your promise.
טֶ֣רֶם אֶ֭עֱנֶה אֲנִ֣י שֹׁגֵ֑ג וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה אִמְרָתְךָ֥ שָׁמָֽרְתִּי׃
You are good, and you do good; teach me your decrees.
טוֹב־אַתָּ֥ה וּמֵטִ֗יב לַמְּדֵ֥נִי חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
The arrogant smear me with lies, but I keep your precepts with all my heart.
טָפְל֬וּ עָלַ֣י שֶׁ֣קֶר זֵדִ֑ים אֲ֝נִ֗י בְּכָל־לֵ֤ב ׀ אֱצֹּ֬ר פִּקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
Their hearts are unfeeling, like fat,[^37] but I delight in your law.
טָפַ֣שׁ כַּחֵ֣לֶב לִבָּ֑ם אֲ֝נִ֗י תּוֹרָתְךָ֥ שִֽׁעֲשָֽׁעְתִּי׃
It was good for me that I was afflicted, so that I might learn your decrees.
טֽוֹב־לִ֥י כִֽי־עֻנֵּ֑יתִי לְ֝מַ֗עַן אֶלְמַ֥ד חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
The law from your mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.
טֽוֹב־לִ֥י תֽוֹרַת־פִּ֑יךָ מֵ֝אַלְפֵ֗י זָהָ֥ב וָכָֽסֶף׃
Your hands made me and formed me;[^38] give me understanding, so that I may learn your commands.
יָדֶ֣יךָ עָ֭שׂוּנִי וַֽיְכוֹנְנ֑וּנִי הֲ֝בִינֵ֗נִי וְאֶלְמְדָ֥ה מִצְוֺתֶֽיךָ׃
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, for I hope in your word.
יְ֭רֵאֶיךָ יִרְא֣וּנִי וְיִשְׂמָ֑חוּ כִּ֖י לִדְבָרְךָ֣ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
I know, LORD, that your rulings are righteous, and that in faithfulness you have afflicted me.
יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְ֭הוָה כִּי־צֶ֣דֶק מִשְׁפָּטֶ֑יךָ וֶ֝אֱמוּנָ֗ה עִנִּיתָֽנִי׃
May your faithful love comfort me, according to your promise to your servant.
יְהִי־נָ֣א חַסְדְּךָ֣ לְנַחֲמֵ֑נִי כְּאִמְרָתְךָ֥ לְעַבְדֶּֽךָ׃
Let your compassion come to me, so that I may live, for your law is my delight.
יְבֹא֣וּנִי רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ וְאֶֽחְיֶ֑ה כִּי־ת֥֝וֹרָתְךָ֗ שַֽׁעֲשֻׁעָֽי׃
Let the arrogant be put to shame, for they have wronged me with lies; but I will meditate on your precepts.
יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ זֵ֭דִים כִּי־שֶׁ֣קֶר עִוְּת֑וּנִי אֲ֝נִ֗י אָשִׂ֥יחַ בְּפִקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
Let those who fear you turn to me, those who know your statutes.[^39]
יָשׁ֣וּבוּ לִ֣י יְרֵאֶ֑יךָ *וידעו **וְ֝יֹדְעֵ֗י עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
May my heart be blameless in your decrees, so that I may not be put to shame.
יְהִֽי־לִבִּ֣י תָמִ֣ים בְּחֻקֶּ֑יךָ לְ֝מַ֗עַן לֹ֣א אֵבֽוֹשׁ׃
My soul faints with longing for your salvation;[^40] I hope in your word.
כָּלְתָ֣ה לִתְשׁוּעָתְךָ֣ נַפְשִׁ֑י לִדְבָרְךָ֥ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
My eyes fail, looking for your promise; I say, "When will you comfort me?"
כָּל֣וּ עֵ֭ינַי לְאִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ לֵ֝אמֹ֗ר מָתַ֥י תְּֽנַחֲמֵֽנִי׃
For I have become like a wineskin in the smoke,[^41] yet I do not forget your decrees.
כִּֽי־הָ֭יִיתִי כְּנֹ֣אד בְּקִיט֑וֹר חֻ֝קֶּ֗יךָ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
How many are the days of your servant? When will you bring judgment[^42] on those who persecute me?
כַּמָּ֥ה יְמֵֽי־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ מָתַ֬י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בְרֹדְפַ֣י מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
The arrogant have dug pits for me, they who do not live by your law.[^43]
כָּֽרוּ־לִ֣י זֵדִ֣ים שִׁיח֑וֹת אֲ֝שֶׁ֗ר לֹ֣א כְתוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
All your commands are faithful;[^44] they persecute me with lies; help me!
כָּל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמוּנָ֑ה שֶׁ֖קֶר רְדָפ֣וּנִי עָזְרֵֽנִי׃
They have almost wiped me from the earth, but I have not forsaken your precepts.
כִּ֭מְעַט כִּלּ֣וּנִי בָאָ֑רֶץ וַ֝אֲנִ֗י לֹא־עָזַ֥בְתִּי פִקֻּודֶֽיךָ׃
In your faithful love give me life, and I will keep the statutes[^45] of your mouth.
כְּחַסְדְּךָ֥ חַיֵּ֑נִי וְ֝אֶשְׁמְרָ֗ה עֵד֥וּת פִּֽיךָ׃
Forever, LORD, your word stands firm in the heavens.[^46]
לְעוֹלָ֥ם יְהוָ֑ה דְּ֝בָרְךָ֗ נִצָּ֥ב בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
Your faithfulness endures from generation to generation; you established the earth, and it stands.
לְדֹ֣ר וָ֭דֹר אֱמֽוּנָתֶ֑ךָ כּוֹנַ֥נְתָּ אֶ֝֗רֶץ וַֽתַּעֲמֹֽד׃
By your rulings they stand to this day,[^47] for all things are your servants.
לְֽ֭מִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ עָמְד֣וּ הַיּ֑וֹם כִּ֖י הַכֹּ֣ל עֲבָדֶֽיךָ׃
If your law had not been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.
לוּלֵ֣י ת֭וֹרָתְךָ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָ֑י אָ֝֗ז אָבַ֥דְתִּי בְעָנְיִֽי׃
I will never forget your precepts, for by them you have given me life.
לְ֭עוֹלָם לֹא־אֶשְׁכַּ֣ח פִּקּוּדֶ֑יךָ כִּ֥י בָ֝֗ם חִיִּיתָֽנִי׃
I am yours; save me, for I have sought your precepts.
לְֽךָ־אֲ֭נִי הוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי כִּ֖י פִקּוּדֶ֣יךָ דָרָֽשְׁתִּי׃
The wicked lie in wait to destroy me, but I consider your statutes.
לִ֤י קִוּ֣וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים לְאַבְּדֵ֑נִי עֵ֝דֹתֶ֗יךָ אֶתְבּוֹנָֽן׃
I have seen a limit to all perfection, but your command is exceedingly broad.[^48]
לְֽכָל־תִּ֭כְלָה רָאִ֣יתִי קֵ֑ץ רְחָבָ֖ה מִצְוָתְךָ֣ מְאֹֽד׃
Oh, how I love your law![^49] It is my meditation all day long.
מָֽה־אָהַ֥בְתִּי תוֹרָתֶ֑ךָ כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם הִ֣יא שִׂיחָתִֽי׃
Your commands make me wiser than my enemies, for they are always with me.
מֵ֭אֹ֣יְבַי תְּחַכְּמֵ֣נִי מִצְוֺתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם הִיא־לִֽי׃
I have more insight than all my teachers, for your statutes are my meditation.
מִכָּל־מְלַמְּדַ֥י הִשְׂכַּ֑לְתִּי כִּ֥י עֵ֝דְוֺתֶ֗יךָ שִׂ֣יחָה לִֽֿי׃
I understand more than the elders, for I keep your precepts.
מִזְּקֵנִ֥ים אֶתְבּוֹנָ֑ן כִּ֖י פִקּוּדֶ֣יךָ נָצָֽרְתִּי׃
I hold back my feet from every evil path, so that I may keep your word.
מִכָּל־אֹ֣רַח רָ֭ע כָּלִ֣אתִי רַגְלָ֑י לְ֝מַ֗עַן אֶשְׁמֹ֥ר דְּבָרֶֽךָ׃
I do not turn aside from your rulings, for you yourself have taught me.
מִמִּשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ לֹא־סָ֑רְתִּי כִּֽי־אַ֝תָּ֗ה הוֹרֵתָֽנִי׃
How sweet your promise is to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
מַה־נִּמְלְצ֣וּ לְ֭חִכִּי אִמְרָתֶ֗ךָ מִדְּבַ֥שׁ לְפִֽי׃
From your precepts I gain understanding; so I hate every false path.
מִפִּקּוּדֶ֥יךָ אֶתְבּוֹנָ֑ן עַל־כֵּ֝[t]ן שָׂנֵ֤אתִי ׀ כָּל־אֹ֬רַח שָֽׁקֶר׃
Your word is a lamp for my feet[^50] and a light for my path.
נֵר־לְרַגְלִ֥י דְבָרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝א֗וֹר לִנְתִיבָתִֽי׃
I have sworn an oath and confirmed it, to keep your righteous rulings.
נִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי וָאֲקַיֵּ֑מָה לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
I am severely afflicted; LORD, give me life according to your word.
נַעֲנֵ֥יתִי עַד־מְאֹ֑ד יְ֝הוָ֗ה חַיֵּ֥נִי כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃
Accept, LORD, the freewill offerings of my mouth,[^51] and teach me your rulings.
נִדְב֣וֹת פִּ֭י רְצֵה־נָ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּֽמִשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ לַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
My life is always in my hand,[^52] yet I do not forget your law.
נַפְשִׁ֣י בְכַפִּ֣י תָמִ֑יד וְ֝ת֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
The wicked have set a trap for me, but I have not strayed from your precepts.
נָתְנ֬וּ רְשָׁעִ֣ים פַּ֣ח לִ֑י וּ֝מִפִּקּוּדֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א תָעִֽיתִי׃
Your statutes are my inheritance forever;[^53] they are the joy of my heart.
נָחַ֣לְתִּי עֵדְוֺתֶ֣יךָ לְעוֹלָ֑ם כִּֽי־שְׂשׂ֖וֹן לִבִּ֣י הֵֽמָּה׃
I have set my heart on doing your decrees, forever, to the end.
נָטִ֣יתִי לִ֭בִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת חֻקֶּ֗יךָ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֵֽקֶב׃
I hate the double-minded,[^54] but I love your law.
סֵעֲפִ֥ים שָׂנֵ֑אתִי וְֽתוֹרָתְךָ֥ אָהָֽבְתִּי׃
You are my hiding place and my shield; I hope in your word.
סִתְרִ֣י וּמָגִנִּ֣י אָ֑תָּה לִדְבָרְךָ֥ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
Go away from me, you evildoers, so that I may keep the commands of my God.
סֽוּרוּ־מִמֶּ֥נִּי מְרֵעִ֑ים וְ֝אֶצְּרָ֗ה מִצְוֺ֥ת אֱלֹהָֽי׃
Sustain me according to your promise, so that I may live; do not let me be put to shame in my hope.
סָמְכֵ֣נִי כְאִמְרָתְךָ֣ וְאֶֽחְיֶ֑ה וְאַל־תְּ֝בִישֵׁ֗נִי מִשִּׂבְרִֽי׃
Uphold me, so that I may be safe, and I will always have regard for your decrees.
סְעָדֵ֥נִי וְאִוָּשֵׁ֑עָה וְאֶשְׁעָ֖ה בְחֻקֶּ֣יךָ תָמִֽיד׃
You reject all who stray from your decrees, for their deceit is in vain.[^55]
סָ֭לִיתָ כָּל־שׁוֹגִ֣ים מֵחֻקֶּ֑יךָ כִּי־שֶׁ֝֗קֶר תַּרְמִיתָֽם׃
You remove all the wicked of the earth like dross;[^56] so I love your statutes.
סִגִ֗ים הִשְׁבַּ֥תָּ כָל־רִשְׁעֵי־אָ֑רֶץ לָ֝כֵ֗ן אָהַ֥בְתִּי עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
My flesh shudders[^57] in fear of you, and I am afraid of your rulings.
סָמַ֣ר מִפַּחְדְּךָ֣ בְשָׂרִ֑י וּֽמִמִּשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ יָרֵֽאתִי׃
I have done what is just and right;[^58] do not abandon me to my oppressors.
עָ֭שִׂיתִי מִשְׁפָּ֣ט וָצֶ֑דֶק בַּל־תַּ֝נִּיחֵ֗נִי לְעֹֽשְׁקָֽי׃
Guarantee your servant's well-being;[^59] do not let the arrogant oppress me.
עֲרֹ֣ב עַבְדְּךָ֣ לְט֑וֹב אַֽל־יַעַשְׁקֻ֥נִי זֵדִֽים׃
My eyes fail, looking for your salvation and for your righteous promise.[^60]
עֵ֭ינַי כָּל֣וּ לִֽישׁוּעָתֶ֑ךָ וּלְאִמְרַ֥ת צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
Deal with your servant according to your faithful love, and teach me your decrees.
עֲשֵׂ֖ה עִם־עַבְדְּךָ֥ כְחַסְדֶּ֗ךָ וְחֻקֶּ֥יךָ לַמְּדֵֽנִי׃
I am your servant; give me understanding, so that I may know your statutes.
עַבְדְּךָ־אָ֥נִי הֲבִינֵ֑נִי וְ֝אֵדְעָ֗ה עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
It is time for the LORD to act;[^61] they have broken your law.
עֵ֭ת לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה הֵ֝פֵ֗רוּ תּוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
Therefore I love your commands more than gold, more than fine gold.
עַל־כֵּ֭ן אָהַ֣בְתִּי מִצְוֺתֶ֑יךָ מִזָּהָ֥ב וּמִפָּֽז׃
Therefore I consider all the precepts right in everything;[^62] I hate every false path.
עַל־כֵּ֤ן ׀ כָּל־פִּקּ֣וּדֵי כֹ֣ל יִשָּׁ֑רְתִּי כָּל־אֹ֖רַח שֶׁ֣קֶר שָׂנֵֽאתִי׃
Your statutes are wonderful;[^63] so my soul keeps them.
פְּלָא֥וֹת עֵדְוֺתֶ֑יךָ עַל־כֵּ֝֗ן נְצָרָ֥תַם נַפְשִֽׁי׃
The unfolding[^64] of your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple.
פֵּ֖תַח דְּבָרֶ֥יךָ יָאִ֗יר מֵבִ֥ין פְּתָיִֽים׃
I open my mouth and pant, for I long for your commands.
פִּֽי־פָ֭עַרְתִּי וָאֶשְׁאָ֑פָה כִּ֖י לְמִצְוֺתֶ֣יךָ יָאָֽבְתִּי׃
Turn to me and be gracious to me, as is your way[^65] with those who love your name.
פְּנֵה־אֵלַ֥י וְחָנֵּ֑נִי כְּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט לְאֹהֲבֵ֥י שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
Make my steps steady by your promise, and let no wickedness rule over me.
פְּ֭עָמַי הָכֵ֣ן בְּאִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ וְֽאַל־תַּשְׁלֶט־בִּ֥י כָל־אָֽוֶן׃
Redeem me from human oppression,[^66] so that I may keep your precepts.
פְּ֭דֵנִי מֵעֹ֣שֶׁק אָדָ֑ם וְ֝אֶשְׁמְרָ֗ה פִּקּוּדֶֽיךָ׃
Make your face shine on your servant,[^67] and teach me your decrees.
פָּ֭נֶיךָ הָאֵ֣ר בְּעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝לַמְּדֵ֗נִי אֶת־חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Streams of water flow down from my eyes, because they do not keep your law.
פַּלְגֵי־מַ֭יִם יָרְד֣וּ עֵינָ֑י עַ֝֗ל לֹא־שָׁמְר֥וּ תוֹרָתֶֽךָ׃
You are righteous, LORD,[^68] and your rulings are upright.
צַדִּ֣יק אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר מִשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃
You have commanded your statutes in righteousness and in great faithfulness.[^69]
צִ֭וִּיתָ צֶ֣דֶק עֵדֹתֶ֑יךָ וֶֽאֱמוּנָ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
My zeal consumes me, because my adversaries forget your words.
