צִמְּתַ֥תְנִי קִנְאָתִ֑י כִּֽי־שָׁכְח֖וּ דְבָרֶ֣יךָ צָרָֽי׃
Your promise is thoroughly refined,[^70] and your servant loves it.
צְרוּפָ֖ה אִמְרָתְךָ֥ מְאֹ֗ד וְֽעַבְדְּךָ֥ אֲהֵבָֽהּ׃
I am small and despised, yet I do not forget your precepts.
צָעִ֣יר אָנֹכִ֣י וְנִבְזֶ֑ה פִּ֝קֻּדֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and your law is truth.
צִדְקָתְךָ֣ צֶ֣דֶק לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְֽתוֹרָתְךָ֥ אֱמֶֽת׃
Trouble and distress have found me, but your commands are my delight.
צַר־וּמָצ֥וֹק מְצָא֑וּנִי מִ֝צְוֺתֶ֗יךָ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָֽי׃
Your statutes are righteous forever; give me understanding, so that I may live.
צֶ֖דֶק עֵדְוֺתֶ֥יךָ לְעוֹלָ֗ם הֲבִינֵ֥נִי וְאֶחְיֶֽה׃
I call with all my heart;[^71] answer me, LORD, and I will keep your decrees.
קָרָ֣אתִי בְכָל־לֵ֭ב עֲנֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֗ה חֻקֶּ֥יךָ אֶצֹּֽרָה׃
I call to you; save me, and I will keep your statutes.
קְרָאתִ֥יךָ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי וְ֝אֶשְׁמְרָ֗ה עֵדֹתֶֽיךָ׃
I rise before dawn and cry for help; I hope in your word.[^72]
קִדַּ֣מְתִּי בַ֭נֶּשֶׁף וָאֲשַׁוֵּ֑עָה *לדבריך **לִדְבָרְךָ֥ יִחָֽלְתִּי׃
My eyes are awake before the watches of the night,[^73] so that I may meditate on your promise.
קִדְּמ֣וּ עֵ֭ינַי אַשְׁמֻר֑וֹת לָ֝שִׂ֗יחַ בְּאִמְרָתֶֽךָ׃
Hear my voice according to your faithful love; LORD, give me life according to your justice.[^74]
ק֭וֹלִי שִׁמְעָ֣ה כְחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ יְ֝הוָ֗ה כְּֽמִשְׁפָּטֶ֥ךָ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
Those who pursue wicked schemes draw near; they are far from your law.
קָ֭רְבוּ רֹדְפֵ֣י זִמָּ֑ה מִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ רָחָֽקוּ׃
You are near, LORD, and all your commands are truth.
קָר֣וֹב אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃
Long ago I learned from your statutes that you have established them forever.
קֶ֣דֶם יָ֭דַעְתִּי מֵעֵדֹתֶ֑יךָ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם יְסַדְתָּֽם׃
Look on my affliction and rescue me,[^75] for I do not forget your law.
רְאֵֽה־עָנְיִ֥י וְחַלְּצֵ֑נִי כִּי־תֽ֝וֹרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃
Plead my case and redeem me; give me life according to your promise.
רִיבָ֣ה רִ֭יבִי וּגְאָלֵ֑נִי לְאִמְרָתְךָ֥ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
Salvation is far from the wicked, for they do not seek your decrees.
רָח֣וֹק מֵרְשָׁעִ֣ים יְשׁוּעָ֑ה כִּֽי־חֻ֝קֶּיךָ לֹ֣א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃
Your compassion is great, LORD; give me life according to your rulings.
רַחֲמֶ֖יךָ רַבִּ֥ים ׀ יְהוָ֑ה כְּֽמִשְׁפָּטֶ֥יךָ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
Many are my persecutors and my adversaries, but I do not turn away from your statutes.
רַ֭בִּים רֹדְפַ֣י וְצָרָ֑י מֵ֝עֵדְוֺתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א נָטִֽיתִי׃
I look on the treacherous with disgust, because they do not keep your promise.
רָאִ֣יתִי בֹ֭גְדִים וָֽאֶתְקוֹטָ֑טָה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִ֝מְרָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁמָֽרוּ׃
See how I love your precepts! LORD, give me life according to your faithful love.
רְ֭אֵה כִּי־פִקּוּדֶ֣יךָ אָהָ֑בְתִּי יְ֝הוָ֗ה כְּֽחַסְדְּךָ֥ חַיֵּֽנִי׃
The sum of your word[^76] is truth, and every one of your righteous rulings endures forever.
רֹאשׁ־דְּבָרְךָ֥ אֱמֶ֑ת וּ֝לְעוֹלָ֗ם כָּל־מִשְׁפַּ֥ט צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
Rulers persecute me without cause,[^77] but my heart stands in awe of your word.[^78]
שָׂ֭רִים רְדָפ֣וּנִי חִנָּ֑ם *ומדבריך **וּ֝מִדְּבָרְךָ֗ פָּחַ֥ד לִבִּֽי׃
I rejoice over your promise like one who finds great plunder.
שָׂ֣שׂ אָ֭נֹכִֽי עַל־אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ כְּ֝מוֹצֵ֗א שָׁלָ֥ל רָֽב׃
I hate and detest falsehood, but I love your law.
שֶׁ֣קֶר שָׂ֭נֵאתִי וַאֲתַעֵ֑בָה תּוֹרָתְךָ֥ אָהָֽבְתִּי׃
Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous rulings.
שֶׁ֣בַע בַּ֭יּוֹם הִלַּלְתִּ֑יךָ עַ֝֗ל מִשְׁפְּטֵ֥י צִדְקֶֽךָ׃
Great peace have those who love your law; nothing makes them stumble.[^79]
שָׁל֣וֹם רָ֭ב לְאֹהֲבֵ֣י תוֹרָתֶ֑ךָ וְאֵֽין־לָ֥מוֹ מִכְשֽׁוֹל׃
I wait for your salvation, LORD, and I do your commands.
שִׂבַּ֣רְתִּי לִֽישׁוּעָתְךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה וּֽמִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
My soul keeps your statutes; I love them greatly.
שָֽׁמְרָ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי עֵדֹתֶ֑יךָ וָאֹהֲבֵ֥ם מְאֹֽד׃
I keep your precepts and your statutes, for all my ways are before you.
שָׁמַ֣רְתִּי פִ֭קּוּדֶיךָ וְעֵדֹתֶ֑יךָ כִּ֖י כָל־דְּרָכַ֣י נֶגְדֶּֽךָ׃
Let my cry come near to you, LORD;[^80] give me understanding according to your word.
תִּקְרַ֤ב רִנָּתִ֣י לְפָנֶ֣יךָ יְהוָ֑ה כִּדְבָרְךָ֥ הֲבִינֵֽנִי׃
Let my plea come before you; rescue me according to your promise.
תָּב֣וֹא תְחִנָּתִ֣י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כְּ֝אִמְרָתְךָ֗ הַצִּילֵֽנִי׃
Let my lips pour out praise, for you teach me your decrees.
תַּבַּ֣עְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י תְּהִלָּ֑ה כִּ֖י תְלַמְּדֵ֣נִי חֻקֶּֽיךָ׃
Let my tongue sing of your promise, for all your commands are righteous.
תַּ֣עַן לְ֭שׁוֹנִי אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֖י כָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֣יךָ צֶּֽדֶק׃
Let your hand be ready to help me, for I have chosen your precepts.
תְּהִֽי־יָדְךָ֥ לְעָזְרֵ֑נִי כִּ֖י פִקּוּדֶ֣יךָ בָחָֽרְתִּי׃
I long for your salvation, LORD, and your law is my delight.
תָּאַ֣בְתִּי לִֽישׁוּעָתְךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝ת֥וֹרָתְךָ֗ שַׁעֲשֻׁעָֽי׃
Let my soul live, and it will praise you; and let your rulings help me.
תְּֽחִי־נַ֭פְשִׁי וּֽתְהַֽלְלֶ֑ךָּ וּֽמִשְׁפָּטֶ֥ךָ יַעֲזְרֻֽנִי׃
I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek your servant, for I do not forget your commands.[^81]
תָּעִ֗יתִי כְּשֶׂ֣ה אֹ֭בֵד בַּקֵּ֣שׁ עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י מִ֝צְוֺתֶיךָ֗ לֹ֣א שָׁכָֽחְתִּי׃

n.1: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed". Also in verse 2.
n.2: *Aleph*: each verse of this stanza (verses 1–8) begins in Hebrew with this letter, the first of the alphabet. Psalm 119, the longest psalm, is an acrostic: it has twenty-two stanzas of eight verses, one stanza for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet in order, and every verse of a stanza begins with its letter. Almost every verse names God's teaching with one of eight words, and this translation keeps one English word for each: *law* (*torah*), *statutes* (*edot*), *precepts* (*piqqudim*), *commands* (*mitsvot*), *rulings* (*mishpatim*), *decrees* (*chuqqim*), *promise* (*imrah*) and *word* (*davar*). Compare Psalm 19:8–10 (19:7–9 in most English Bibles).
n.3: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching": here God's teaching as a whole.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrew *edot*, traditionally "testimonies": the solemn terms of the covenant.
n.6: Literally "the rulings of your righteousness". Also in verses 62, 106, 160 and 164.
n.7: *Bet*: each verse of this stanza (verses 9–16) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.8: Hebrew *imrah*, "saying, word": what God has said, often his promise. This translation keeps "promise" for *imrah* and "word" for *davar*.
n.9: *Gimel*: each verse of this stanza (verses 17–24) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.10: Hebrew *ger*, a foreigner living in a land not his own. Or "in the land".
n.11: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 25, 28, 81, 129, 167 and 175.
n.12: Or "You rebuke the arrogant; cursed are those who stray from your commands."
n.13: Literally "Roll scorn and contempt off me".
n.14: Literally "the men of my counsel".
n.15: *Dalet*: each verse of this stanza (verses 25–32) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.16: Or "revive me", "preserve my life". Also in verses 37, 40, 88, 107, 149, 154, 156 and 159.
n.17: Literally "drips", that is, melts away in tears.
n.18: Literally "I have set your rulings", perhaps "before me", as in 16:8.
n.19: Literally "you make my heart wide". Or "when you enlarge my understanding".
n.20: *He*: each verse of this stanza (verses 33–40) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.21: Or "as my reward". Hebrew *eqev*, also in verse 112.
n.22: Literally "which (is) for the fear of you". Or "which leads to the fear of you".
n.23: Hebrew *chasadekha*, the plural of *chesed*, "loyal, faithful love": "your acts of faithful love". In verses 64, 76, 88, 124, 149 and 159 the word is singular.
n.24: *Vav*: each verse of this stanza (verses 41–48) begins in Hebrew with this letter, which is also the word "and". Each verse here begins "and".
n.25: Literally "I will answer the one who taunts me a word (*davar*)".
n.27: Lifting up the hands was a gesture of prayer and reverence.
n.28: *Zayin*: each verse of this stanza (verses 49–56) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.29: Literally "in the house of my sojourning", that is, in this life, where I live like a foreigner (compare verse 19).
n.30: Literally "This has been to me, that I have kept your precepts": either keeping them is my reward, or my blessing has come because I kept them.
n.31: *Chet*: each verse of this stanza (verses 57–64) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.32: Or "My portion, LORD, I have said, is to keep your words." *Portion*: one's share of land, here the LORD himself (compare 16:5; Numbers 18:20).
n.33: Literally "I have softened your face", that is, entreated you.
n.34: Or "The bands of the wicked surround me".
n.35: *Tet*: each verse of this stanza (verses 65–72) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.36: Literally "goodness of taste", that is, discernment.
n.37: Literally "Their heart is gross like fat", that is, insensitive.
n.38: *Yod*: each verse of this stanza (verses 73–80) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.39: The Hebrew text is written "so that they may know your statutes" but read "those who know your statutes".
n.40: *Kaph*: each verse of this stanza (verses 81–88) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.41: A skin bottle hung in the smoke of a fire dries out, shrivels and blackens.
n.42: Hebrew *mishpat*, the word translated "rulings" elsewhere in this psalm.
n.43: Literally "which is not according to your law".
n.46: *Lamed*: each verse of this stanza (verses 89–96) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.47: That is, the heavens and the earth (verses 89–90).
n.48: That is, it has no limit. *Perfection*: or "completeness".
n.49: *Mem*: each verse of this stanza (verses 97–104) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.50: *Nun*: each verse of this stanza (verses 105–112) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.51: That is, my prayers and praises, offered willingly like freewill offerings.
n.52: That is, I am always in danger (compare Judges 12:3; 1 Samuel 19:5). Hebrew *nephesh*.
n.53: Literally "I have inherited your statutes forever".
n.54: *Samek*: each verse of this stanza (verses 113–120) begins in Hebrew with this letter. *The double-minded*: Hebrew *se'afim*, those divided in their loyalty (compare 1 Kings 18:21).
n.55: Literally "for falsehood is their deceit", that is, their schemes come to nothing.
n.56: The waste skimmed off when metal is refined.
n.57: Literally "bristles", as the hair stands on end.
n.58: *Ayin*: each verse of this stanza (verses 121–128) begins in Hebrew with this letter. *What is just and right*: literally "justice (*mishpat*) and righteousness". *Mishpat* is the word translated "rulings" elsewhere in this psalm.
n.59: Literally "Be surety for your servant for good", that is, stand guarantee for me, as one who pledges to pay another's debt. This verse has none of the eight words for God's teaching.
n.61: Or "It is time to act for the LORD".
n.62: Literally "all precepts of all I consider right". The Hebrew is difficult. Some scholars read "all your precepts", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.63: *Pe*: each verse of this stanza (verses 129–136) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.65: Literally "according to the ruling (*mishpat*) for those who love your name", that is, as you always do for them.
n.67: Compare the priestly blessing in Numbers 6:25.
n.68: *Tsade*: each verse of this stanza (verses 137–144) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.69: Literally "You have commanded righteousness, your statutes, and faithfulness, greatly".
n.70: Like metal tested in the fire and found pure (compare 12:7; 12:6 in most English Bibles).
n.71: *Qof*: each verse of this stanza (verses 145–152) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.72: The Hebrew text is written "your words" but read "your word".
n.73: The night was divided into watches. Or "My eyes are awake through the watches of the night".
n.74: Hebrew *mishpat*, the word translated "rulings" elsewhere in this psalm.
n.75: *Resh*: each verse of this stanza (verses 153–160) begins in Hebrew with this letter.
n.76: Literally "The head of your word": its sum, or its beginning.
n.77: *Shin*: each verse of this stanza (verses 161–168) begins in Hebrew with this letter or with *sin*, written with the same sign.
n.78: The Hebrew text is written "your words" but read "your word".
n.79: Literally "there is no stumbling block for them".
n.80: *Tav*: each verse of this stanza (verses 169–176) begins in Hebrew with this letter, the last of the alphabet.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] To the LORD[^2] I called in my distress, and he answered me.
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצָּרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י קָ֝רָ֗אתִי וֽ͏ַיַּעֲנֵֽנִי׃
LORD, rescue me[^3] from lying lips, from a deceitful tongue.
יְֽהוָ֗ה הַצִּ֣ילָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת־שֶׁ֑קֶר מִלָּשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃
What will he give you, and what more will he do to you,[^4] you deceitful tongue?
מַה־יִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭ךָ וּמַה־יֹּסִ֥יף לָ֗ךְ לָשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃
A warrior's sharp arrows, with burning coals of the broom tree![^5]
חִצֵּ֣י גִבּ֣וֹר שְׁנוּנִ֑ים עִ֝֗ם גַּחֲלֵ֥י רְתָמִֽים׃
Woe is me, that I live as a stranger in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar![^6]
אֽוֹיָה־לִ֭י כִּי־גַ֣רְתִּי מֶ֑שֶׁךְ שָׁ֝כַ֗נְתִּי עִֽם־אָהֳלֵ֥י קֵדָֽר׃
Too long I have lived[^7] with those who hate peace.
רַ֭בַּת שָֽׁכְנָה־לָּ֣הּ נַפְשִׁ֑י עִ֝֗ם שׂוֹנֵ֥א שָׁלֽוֹם׃
I am for peace,[^8] but when I speak, they are for war.
אֲ‍ֽנִי־שָׁ֭לוֹם וְכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר הֵ֝֗מָּה לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

n.1: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot*, "a song of the goings up". Psalms 120–134 all have this title. They were probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the festivals; Jewish tradition also linked them with the fifteen steps in the temple courts where the Levites sang. In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "rescue my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.4: The words echo an oath, "May God do so to you, and more also" (1 Samuel 3:17): what punishment will God give the liar?
n.5: The wood of the broom tree makes charcoal that burns long and hot. The liar's punishment will fit the tongue's sharp, burning words.
n.6: Meshech was a people of the far north, near the Black Sea (Genesis 10:2; Ezekiel 38:2), and Kedar a tribe of the Arabian desert (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16–17). The two names, far apart, probably stand for hostile, warlike neighbors in general.
n.7: Literally "My soul (*nephesh*) has dwelt for itself too long".
n.8: Literally "I (am) peace".

v: A song of ascents.[^1] I lift up my eyes to the mountains. Where does my help come from?
שִׁ֗יר לַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אֶשָּׂ֣א עֵ֭ינַי אֶל־הֶהָרִ֑ים מֵ֝אַ֗יִן יָבֹ֥א עֶזְרִֽי׃
My help comes from the LORD,[^2] the maker of heaven and earth.
עֶ֭זְרִי מֵעִ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃
He will not let your foot slip;[^3] the one who guards you[^4] will not slumber.
אַל־יִתֵּ֣ן לַמּ֣וֹט רַגְלֶ֑ךָ אַל־יָ֝נ֗וּם שֹֽׁמְרֶֽךָ׃
Look, the one who guards Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
הִנֵּ֣ה לֹֽא־יָ֭נוּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
The LORD is the one who guards you; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
יְהוָ֥ה שֹׁמְרֶ֑ךָ יְהוָ֥ה צִ֝לְּךָ֗ עַל־יַ֥ד יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.[^5]
יוֹמָ֗ם הַשֶּׁ֥מֶשׁ לֹֽא־יַכֶּ֗כָּה וְיָרֵ֥חַ בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃
The LORD will guard you from all harm; he will guard your life.[^6]
יְֽהוָ֗ה יִשְׁמָרְךָ֥ מִכָּל־רָ֑ע יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר אֶת־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
The LORD will guard your going out and your coming in,[^7] from now on and forever.
יְֽהוָ֗ה יִשְׁמָר־צֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֶ֑ךָ מֵֽ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

n.1: Here the Hebrew has *shir lamma'alot*, "a song for the ascents", a slightly different form of the title of Psalms 120–134 (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "May he not let your foot slip; may the one who guards you not slumber."
n.4: Hebrew *shomer*, "guard, keeper", from *shamar*, "guard, keep", the word that runs through verses 3–8.
n.5: The sun's heat could cause sunstroke, and the moon was thought to cause harm by night.
n.6: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.7: That is, all that you do, wherever you go.

v: A song of ascents. Of David.[^1] I was glad when they said to me, "Let us go to the house of the LORD."[^2]
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד שָׂ֭מַחְתִּי בְּאֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֑י בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה נֵלֵֽךְ׃
Our feet are standing within your gates, Jerusalem.
עֹ֭מְדוֹת הָי֣וּ רַגְלֵ֑ינוּ בִּ֝שְׁעָרַ֗יִךְ יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Jerusalem, built as a city that is bound firmly together,[^3]
יְרוּשָׁלַ֥͏ִם הַבְּנוּיָ֑ה כְּ֝עִ֗יר שֶׁחֻבְּרָה־לָּ֥הּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
where the tribes go up, the tribes of the LORD,[^4] according to the statute[^5] given to Israel, to give thanks to the name of the LORD.
שֶׁשָּׁ֨ם עָל֪וּ שְׁבָטִ֡ים שִׁבְטֵי־יָ֭הּ עֵד֣וּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְ֝הֹד֗וֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃
For there the thrones for judgment stand,[^6] the thrones of the house of David.
כִּ֤י שָׁ֨מָּה ׀ יָשְׁב֣וּ כִסְא֣וֹת לְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֝סְא֗וֹת לְבֵ֣ית דָּוִֽיד׃
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem:[^7] "May those who love you be secure.
שַׁ֭אֲלוּ שְׁל֣וֹם יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם יִ֝שְׁלָ֗יוּ אֹהֲבָֽיִךְ׃
May there be peace within your walls, security within your fortresses."
יְהִֽי־שָׁל֥וֹם בְּחֵילֵ֑ךְ שַׁ֝לְוָ֗ה בְּאַרְמְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃
For the sake of my brothers and my friends, I will say, "Peace be within you."
לְ֭מַעַן אַחַ֣י וְרֵעָ֑י אֲדַבְּרָה־נָּ֖א שָׁל֣וֹם בָּֽךְ׃
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
לְ֭מַעַן בֵּית־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ אֲבַקְשָׁ֖ה ט֣וֹב לָֽךְ׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "compact", its houses joined closely together.
n.4: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH.
n.5: Hebrew *edut*, traditionally "testimony": the solemn terms of the covenant. The law required every Israelite man to appear before the LORD three times a year (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16).
n.6: Literally "sit", or "sat".
n.7: Literally "Ask the peace (*shalom*) of Jerusalem". Verses 6–7 play on the sound of the city's name, *Yerushalayim*: *sha'alu shelom* "ask the peace", *yishlayu* "be secure", *shalom* "peace", *shalvah* "security".

v: A song of ascents.[^1] To you I lift up my eyes, you who are enthroned in the heavens.
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אֵ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי אֶת־עֵינַ֑י הַ֝יֹּשְׁבִ֗י בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
As the eyes of servants[^2] look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a female servant look to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD[^3] our God, until he is gracious to us.
הִנֵּ֨ה כְעֵינֵ֪י עֲבָדִ֡ים אֶל־יַ֤ד אֲ‍ֽדוֹנֵיהֶ֗ם כְּעֵינֵ֣י שִׁפְחָה֮ אֶל־יַ֢ד גְּבִ֫רְתָּ֥הּ כֵּ֣ן עֵ֭ינֵינוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ עַ֝֗ד שֶׁיְּחָנֵּֽנוּ׃
Be gracious to us, LORD, be gracious to us, for we have had more than enough of contempt.
חָנֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֣ה חָנֵּ֑נוּ כִּֽי־רַ֝֗ב שָׂבַ֥עְנוּ בֽוּז׃
We have had more than enough[^4] of the scorn of those who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud.
רַבַּת֮ שָֽׂבְעָה־לָּ֢הּ נַ֫פְשֵׁ֥נוּ הַלַּ֥עַג הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֑ים הַ֝בּ֗וּז לִגְאֵ֥יוֹנִֽים׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Or "slaves".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "Our soul (*nephesh*) has been filled for itself".

v: A song of ascents. Of David.[^1] If it had not been the LORD[^2] who was on our side, let Israel now say,
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ יֹֽאמַר־נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
if it had not been the LORD who was on our side when people[^3] rose up against us,
לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ בְּק֖וּם עָלֵ֣ינוּ אָדָֽם׃
then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger blazed against us;
אֲ֭זַי חַיִּ֣ים בְּלָע֑וּנוּ בַּחֲר֖וֹת אַפָּ֣ם בָּֽנוּ׃
then the waters would have swept us away; the torrent would have gone over us;[^4]
אֲ֭זַי הַמַּ֣יִם שְׁטָפ֑וּנוּ נַ֗֜[c]חְלָה עָבַ֥ר עַל־נַפְשֵֽׁנוּ׃
then the raging[^5] waters would have gone over us.
אֲ֭זַי עָבַ֣ר עַל־נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ הַ֝מַּ֗יִם הַזֵּֽידוֹנִֽים׃
Blessed be the LORD, who has not given us as prey to their teeth.
בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה שֶׁלֹּ֥א נְתָנָ֥נוּ טֶ֝֗רֶף לְשִׁנֵּיהֶֽם׃
We have escaped[^6] like a bird from the fowler's trap; the trap is broken, and we have escaped.
נַפְשֵׁ֗נוּ כְּצִפּ֥וֹר נִמְלְטָה֮ מִפַּ֢ח י֫וֹקְשִׁ֥ים הַפַּ֥ח נִשְׁבָּ֗ר וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ נִמְלָֽטְנוּ׃
Our help is in the name of the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
עֶ֭זְרֵנוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *adam*, "human beings".
n.4: Literally "over our soul (*nephesh*)". Also in verse 5.
n.5: Or "arrogant". Hebrew *zeidonim*, related to *zedim*, "the arrogant".
n.6: Literally "Our soul (*nephesh*) has escaped".

v: A song of ascents.[^1] Those who trust in the LORD[^2] are like Mount Zion, which cannot be shaken but stands firm forever.[^3]
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת הַבֹּטְחִ֥ים בַּיהוָ֑ה כְּֽהַר־צִיּ֥וֹן לֹא־יִ֝מּ֗וֹט לְעוֹלָ֥ם יֵשֵֽׁב׃
As the mountains surround Jerusalem, so the LORD surrounds his people, from now on and forever.[^4]
יְֽרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָרִים֮ סָבִ֢יב לָ֥הּ וַ֭יהוָה סָבִ֣יב לְעַמּ֑וֹ מֵ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
For the scepter of wickedness will not rest on the land allotted to the righteous,[^5] so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands to do wrong.
כִּ֤י ׀[t] לֹ֪א יָנ֡[t]וּחַ שֵׁ֤בֶט הָרֶ֗שַׁע עַל֮ גּוֹרַ֢ל הַֽצַּדִּ֫יקִ֥ים לְמַ֡עַן לֹא־יִשְׁלְח֖וּ הַצַדִּיקִ֨ים בְּעַוְלָ֬תָה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃
Do good, LORD, to those who are good, to those who are upright in their hearts.
הֵיטִ֣יבָה יְ֭הוָה לַטּוֹבִ֑ים וְ֝לִֽישָׁרִ֗ים בְּלִבּוֹתָֽם׃
But those who turn aside to their crooked ways, the LORD will lead away with the evildoers. Peace be on Israel!
וְהַמַּטִּ֤ים עַֽקַלְקַלּוֹתָ֗ם יוֹלִיכֵ֣ם יְ֭הוָה אֶת־פֹּעֲלֵ֣י הָאָ֑וֶן שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "sits forever", or "is inhabited forever".
n.4: Literally "Jerusalem: mountains are around her, and the LORD is around his people".
n.5: Literally "on the lot of the righteous", the share of land assigned to them by lot (compare Joshua 14:2). The scepter of a wicked ruler stands for foreign rule over the land.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] When the LORD[^2] restored the fortunes of Zion,[^3] we were like those who dream.[^4]
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת בְּשׁ֣וּב יְ֭הוָה אֶת־שִׁיבַ֣ת צִיּ֑וֹן הָ֝יִ֗ינוּ כְּחֹלְמִֽים׃
Then our mouths were filled with laughter, and our tongues with shouts of joy. Then they said among the nations, "The LORD has done great things for them."
אָ֤ז יִמָּלֵ֪א שְׂח֡וֹק פִּינוּ֮ וּלְשׁוֹנֵ֢נוּ רִ֫נָּ֥ה אָ֭ז יֹאמְר֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֑ם הִגְדִּ֥יל יְ֝הוָ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עִם־אֵֽלֶּה׃
The LORD has done great things for us, and we were glad.[^5]
הִגְדִּ֣יל יְ֭הוָה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עִמָּ֗נוּ הָיִ֥ינוּ שְׂמֵחִֽים׃
Restore our fortunes, LORD, like streams in the Negev.[^6]
שׁוּבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־*שבותנו **שְׁבִיתֵ֑נוּ כַּאֲפִיקִ֥ים בַּנֶּֽגֶב׃
Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy.
הַזֹּרְעִ֥ים בְּדִמְעָ֗ה בְּרִנָּ֥ה יִקְצֹֽרוּ׃
The one who goes out weeping, carrying the seed to sow,[^7] will surely come back with shouts of joy, carrying his sheaves.
הָ֘ל֤וֹךְ יֵלֵ֨ךְ ׀ וּבָכֹה֮ נֹשֵׂ֢א מֶֽשֶׁךְ־הַ֫זָּ֥רַע בֹּֽא־יָב֥וֹא בְרִנָּ֑ה נֹ֝שֵׂ֗א אֲלֻמֹּתָֽיו׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "brought back the captives of Zion". Hebrew *shivat tsiyyon*. Also in verse 4. The return from exile in Babylon may be meant.
n.4: The Septuagint reads "like those who are comforted".
n.5: Or "and we are glad".
n.6: The dry south of Judah, whose empty streambeds fill suddenly with water when the rains come.
n.7: Literally "carrying the drawing of seed", perhaps a bag of seed, or the handfuls drawn out for sowing.

v: A song of ascents. Of Solomon.[^1] Unless the LORD[^2] builds the house, its builders labor over it in vain. Unless the LORD guards the city, the guard keeps watch in vain.
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לִשְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה אִם־יְהוָ֤ה ׀ לֹא־יִבְנֶ֬ה בַ֗יִת שָׁ֤וְא ׀ עָמְל֣וּ בוֹנָ֣יו בּ֑וֹ אִם־יְהוָ֥ה לֹֽא־יִשְׁמָר־עִ֝֗יר שָׁ֤וְא ׀ שָׁקַ֬ד שׁוֹמֵֽר׃
It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives sleep to the one he loves.[^3]
שָׁ֤וְא לָכֶ֨ם ׀ מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי ק֡וּם מְאַֽחֲרֵי־שֶׁ֗בֶת אֹ֭כְלֵי לֶ֣חֶם הָעֲצָבִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן יִתֵּ֖ן לִֽידִיד֣וֹ שֵׁנָֽא׃
Look, children[^4] are an inheritance from the LORD, the fruit of the womb a reward.
הִנֵּ֤ה נַחֲלַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה בָּנִ֑ים שָׂ֝כָ֗ר פְּרִ֣י הַבָּֽטֶן׃
Like arrows in the hand of a warrior are the children of one's youth.
כְּחִצִּ֥ים בְּיַד־גִּבּ֑וֹר כֵּ֝֗ן בְּנֵ֣י הַנְּעוּרִֽים׃
Happy[^5] is the man who has filled his quiver with them! They will not be put to shame when they speak with enemies at the gate.[^6]
אַשְׁרֵ֤י הַגֶּ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִלֵּ֥א אֶת־אַשְׁפָּת֗וֹ מֵ֫הֶ֥ם לֹֽא־יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ כִּֽי־יְדַבְּר֖וּ אֶת־אוֹיְבִ֣ים בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). *Of Solomon*: or "for Solomon". Solomon built the house of the LORD (1 Kings 6), and he was also named *Jedidiah*, "loved by Yah" (2 Samuel 12:25; compare "the one he loves" in verse 2). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "for he gives to the one he loves while he sleeps". Hebrew *yedido*, "his beloved".
n.4: Literally "sons". Also in verse 4.
n.5: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.6: The town gate, where legal cases were heard and business was done. A man with grown sons had others to stand with him.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] Happy[^2] is everyone who fears the LORD,[^3] who walks in his ways.
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אַ֭שְׁרֵי כָּל־יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה הַ֝הֹלֵ֗ךְ בִּדְרָכָֽיו׃
You will eat the fruit of your labor;[^4] you will be happy, and it will go well with you.
יְגִ֣יעַ כַּ֭פֶּיךָ כִּ֣י תֹאכֵ֑ל אַ֝שְׁרֶ֗יךָ וְט֣וֹב לָֽךְ׃
Your wife will be like a fruitful vine within your house,[^5] your children[^6] like olive shoots around your table.
אֶשְׁתְּךָ֤ ׀ כְּגֶ֥פֶן פֹּרִיָּה֮ בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֢י בֵ֫יתֶ֥ךָ בָּ֭נֶיךָ כִּשְׁתִלֵ֣י זֵיתִ֑ים סָ֝בִ֗יב לְשֻׁלְחָנֶֽךָ׃
Look, this is how the man who fears the LORD will be blessed.
הִנֵּ֣ה כִי־כֵ֭ן יְבֹ֥רַךְ גָּ֗בֶר יְרֵ֣א יְהוָֽה׃
May the LORD bless you from Zion; may you see the prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָ֗ה מִצִ֫יּ֥וֹן וּ֖[d]רְאֵה בְּט֣וּב יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כֹּ֝֗ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
May you see your children's children. Peace be on Israel!
וּרְאֵֽה־בָנִ֥ים לְבָנֶ֑יךָ שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed". Also in verse 2.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "the labor of your hands".
n.5: Literally "in the innermost parts of your house".
n.6: Literally "your sons". Also in verse 6.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] "Often they have attacked me from my youth," let Israel now say,
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרַ֑י יֹֽאמַר־נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
"often they have attacked me from my youth, yet they have not overcome me.
רַ֭בַּת צְרָר֣וּנִי מִנְּעוּרָ֑י גַּ֝ם לֹא־יָ֥כְלוּ לִֽי׃
The plowers plowed over my back; they made their furrows long."[^2]
עַל־גַּ֭בִּי חָרְשׁ֣וּ חֹרְשִׁ֑ים הֶ֝אֱרִ֗יכוּ *למענותם **לְמַעֲנִיתָֽם׃
The LORD[^3] is righteous; he has cut the cords of the wicked.[^4]
יְהוָ֥ה צַדִּ֑יק קִ֝צֵּ֗ץ עֲב֣וֹת רְשָׁעִֽים׃
May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turned back.
יֵ֭בֹשׁוּ וְיִסֹּ֣גוּ אָח֑וֹר כֹּ֝֗ל שֹׂנְאֵ֥י צִיּֽוֹן׃
May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it grows up,[^5]
יִ֭הְיוּ כַּחֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֑וֹת שֶׁקַּדְמַ֖ת שָׁלַ֣ף יָבֵֽשׁ׃
with which the reaper does not fill his hand, nor the binder of sheaves his arms,[^6]
שֶׁלֹּ֤א מִלֵּ֖א כַפּ֥וֹ קוֹצֵ֗ר וְחִצְנ֥וֹ מְעַמֵּֽר׃
and those who pass by do not say, "The blessing of the LORD be on you! We bless you in the name of the LORD."[^7]
וְלֹ֤א אָֽמְר֨וּ ׀ הָעֹבְרִ֗ים בִּרְכַּֽת־יְהוָ֥ה אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם בֵּרַ֥כְנוּ אֶ֝תְכֶ֗ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָֽה׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: That is, they cut deep wounds in me, like a plow cutting furrows, perhaps by flogging.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Perhaps the ropes that harnessed the plow to the ox, or the cords that bound Israel.
n.5: Or "before it is pulled up". Grass that sprouted in the thin soil of a flat roof soon dried up in the sun.
n.6: Literally "his bosom", the fold of the garment where an armful of grain was carried.
n.7: Passersby greeted reapers with a blessing (compare Ruth 2:4). The last words may be the psalm's own closing blessing.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] Out of the depths I call to you, LORD.[^2]
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֑וֹת מִמַּעֲמַקִּ֖ים קְרָאתִ֣יךָ יְהוָֽה׃
Lord, hear my voice! Let your ears be attentive to my voice as I plead for mercy.[^3]
אֲדֹנָי֮ שִׁמְעָ֢ה בְק֫וֹלִ֥י תִּהְיֶ֣ינָה אָ֭זְנֶיךָ קַשֻּׁב֑וֹת לְ֝ק֗וֹל תַּחֲנוּנָֽי׃
If you, LORD,[^4] kept a record of iniquities,[^5] Lord, who could stand?
אִם־עֲוֺנ֥וֹת תִּשְׁמָר־יָ֑הּ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י מִ֣י יַעֲמֹֽד׃
But with you there is forgiveness, so that you may be feared.
כִּֽי־עִמְּךָ֥ הַסְּלִיחָ֑ה לְ֝מַ֗עַן תִּוָּרֵֽא׃
I wait for the LORD; my soul[^6] waits, and in his word I put my hope.
קִוִּ֣יתִי יְ֭הוָה קִוְּתָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֑י וְֽלִדְבָר֥וֹ הוֹחָֽלְתִּי׃
My soul waits for the Lord[^7] more than watchmen wait for the morning, more than watchmen for the morning.
נַפְשִׁ֥י לַֽאדֹנָ֑י מִשֹּׁמְרִ֥ים לַ֝בֹּ֗קֶר שֹׁמְרִ֥ים לַבֹּֽקֶר׃
Israel, put your hope in the LORD! For with the LORD there is faithful love,[^8] and with him is abundant redemption.
יַחֵ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־יְה֫וָה כִּֽי־עִם־יְהוָ֥ה הַחֶ֑סֶד וְהַרְבֵּ֖ה עִמּ֣וֹ פְדֽוּת׃
He himself will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.
וְ֭הוּא יִפְדֶּ֣ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִ֝כֹּ֗ל עֲוֺנֹתָֽיו׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "to the voice of my supplications".
n.4: Hebrew *Yah*, a short form of the name YHWH.
n.5: Literally "If you watch iniquities".
n.6: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 6.
n.7: The Hebrew has no verb: literally "My soul (is) for the Lord".
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.

v: A song of ascents. Of David.[^1] LORD,[^2] my heart is not proud, and my eyes are not haughty. I do not concern myself[^3] with great matters, or with things too wonderful for me.
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּֽעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד יְהוָ֤ה ׀ לֹא־גָבַ֣הּ לִ֭בִּי וְלֹא־רָמ֣וּ עֵינַ֑י וְלֹֽא־הִלַּ֓כְתִּי ׀ בִּגְדֹל֖וֹת וּבְנִפְלָא֣וֹת מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
Instead,[^4] I have calmed and quieted my soul,[^5] like a weaned child with its mother; my soul within me is like a weaned child.
אִם־לֹ֤א שִׁוִּ֨יתִי ׀ וְדוֹמַ֗מְתִּי נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י כְּ֭גָמֻל עֲלֵ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ כַּגָּמֻ֖ל עָלַ֣י נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Israel, put your hope in the LORD, from now on and forever.
יַחֵ֣ל יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל אֶל־יְהוָ֑ה מֵֽ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "I do not walk".
n.4: Literally "If not", a form used in oaths: "Surely".
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in the next line. A weaned child no longer frets for the breast, but rests content on its mother.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] LORD,[^2] remember David and all his hardships,[^3]
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת זְכוֹר־יְהוָ֥ה לְדָוִ֑ד אֵ֝ת כָּל־עֻנּוֹתֽוֹ׃
how he swore an oath to the LORD and made a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob:[^4]
אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֭שְׁבַּע לַיהוָ֑ה נָ֝דַ֗ר לַאֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃
"I will not enter the tent of my house or get into my bed;[^5]
אִם־אָ֭בֹא בְּאֹ֣הֶל בֵּיתִ֑י אִם־אֶ֝עֱלֶ֗ה עַל־עֶ֥רֶשׂ יְצוּעָֽי׃
I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids,
אִם־אֶתֵּ֣ן שְׁנַ֣ת לְעֵינָ֑י לְֽעַפְעַפַּ֥י תְּנוּמָֽה׃
until I find a place for the LORD, a dwelling place for the Mighty One of Jacob."
עַד־אֶמְצָ֣א מָ֭קוֹם לַיהוָ֑ה מִ֝שְׁכָּנ֗וֹת לַאֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.[^6]
הִנֵּֽה־שְׁמַֽעֲנ֥וּהָ בְאֶפְרָ֑תָה מְ֝צָאנ֗וּהָ בִּשְׂדֵי־יָֽעַר׃
Let us go to his dwelling place; let us bow down at his footstool.[^7]
נָב֥וֹאָה לְמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֑יו נִ֝שְׁתַּחֲוֶ֗ה לַהֲדֹ֥ם רַגְלָֽיו׃
Rise up, LORD, and go to your resting place, you and the ark of your might.[^8]
קוּמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לִמְנוּחָתֶ֑ךָ אַ֝תָּ֗ה וַאֲר֥וֹן עֻזֶּֽךָ׃
May your priests be clothed with righteousness, and may your faithful ones[^9] shout for joy.
כֹּהֲנֶ֥יךָ יִלְבְּשׁוּ־צֶ֑דֶק וַחֲסִידֶ֥יךָ יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
For the sake of David your servant, do not reject your anointed one.[^10]
בַּ֭עֲבוּר דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ אַל־תָּ֝שֵׁ֗ב פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
The LORD swore to David a sure oath, from which he will not turn back: "One of your own descendants[^11] I will set on your throne.
נִשְׁבַּֽע־יְהוָ֨ה ׀ לְדָוִ֡ד אֱמֶת֮ לֹֽא־יָשׁ֢וּב מִ֫מֶּ֥נָּה מִפְּרִ֥י בִטְנְךָ֑ אָ֝שִׁ֗ית לְכִסֵּא־לָֽךְ׃
If your sons keep my covenant and my statutes[^12] that I will teach them, their sons also will sit on your throne forever."
אִֽם־יִשְׁמְר֬וּ בָנֶ֨יךָ ׀ בְּרִיתִי֮ וְעֵדֹתִ֥י ז֗וֹ אֲלַ֫מְּדֵ֥ם גַּם־בְּנֵיהֶ֥ם עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד יֵ֝שְׁב֗וּ לְכִסֵּא־לָֽךְ׃
For the LORD has chosen Zion; he has desired it for his dwelling:
כִּֽי־בָחַ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה בְּצִיּ֑וֹן אִ֝וָּ֗הּ לְמוֹשָׁ֥ב לֽוֹ׃
"This is my resting place forever; here I will dwell,[^13] for I have desired it.
זֹאת־מְנוּחָתִ֥י עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד פֹּֽה־אֵ֝שֵׁ֗ב כִּ֣י אִוִּתִֽיהָ׃
I will richly bless its provisions; I will satisfy its needy with bread.
צֵ֭ידָהּ בָּרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֵ֑ךְ אֶ֝בְיוֹנֶ֗יהָ אַשְׂבִּ֥יעַֽ לָֽחֶם׃
Its priests I will clothe with salvation, and its faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.
וְֽ֭כֹהֲנֶיהָ אַלְבִּ֣ישׁ יֶ֑שַׁע וַ֝חֲסִידֶ֗יהָ רַנֵּ֥ן יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.[^14]
שָׁ֤ם אַצְמִ֣יחַ קֶ֣רֶן לְדָוִ֑ד עָרַ֥כְתִּי נֵ֝֗ר לִמְשִׁיחִֽי׃
His enemies I will clothe with shame, but on him his crown will shine."[^15]
א֭וֹיְבָיו אַלְבִּ֣ישׁ בֹּ֑שֶׁת וְ֝עָלָ֗יו יָצִ֥יץ נִזְרֽוֹ׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. The psalm recalls how David brought the ark to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6) and the LORD's promise to him (2 Samuel 7).
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "all his self-denial", the oath he kept (verses 3–5). Literally "all his being afflicted".
n.4: Hebrew *avir ya'aqov*, an ancient title of God (Genesis 49:24; Isaiah 49:26). Also in verse 5.
n.5: Literally "If I enter the tent of my house, if I go up on the couch of my bed", the form of an oath. Also in verse 4.
n.6: *It* is probably the ark (verse 8). *Ephrathah* is another name for Bethlehem (Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:1; 5:2 in most English Bibles), or for the clan around Kiriath-jearim (1 Chronicles 2:50). *Jaar*, "forest", is probably Kiriath-jearim, "town of forests", where the ark stayed for twenty years until David brought it to Jerusalem (1 Samuel 7:1–2).
n.7: The ark was pictured as the footstool of the LORD, who is enthroned above the cherubim (1 Chronicles 28:2; compare 99:5).
n.8: Verses 8–10 are nearly the same as Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple in 2 Chronicles 6:41–42. Compare also Numbers 10:35.
n.9: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". Also in verse 16.
n.10: Literally "do not turn away the face of your anointed one", that is, do not refuse his request (compare 1 Kings 2:16). Hebrew *meshichekha*, "your anointed one", the king of David's line, anointed at the LORD's command.
n.11: Literally "From the fruit of your body". Compare 2 Samuel 7:12–16. Acts 2:30 recalls this oath.
n.12: Hebrew *edot*, traditionally "testimonies": the solemn terms of the covenant.
n.13: Or "here I will sit enthroned".
n.14: Hebrew *meshichi*, "my anointed one", the king of David's line. The horn is a symbol of strength, and the lamp of a line of kings that does not die out (1 Kings 11:36). Later Jewish and Christian readers heard the promised Messiah in this verse; Luke 1:69 echoes it ("a horn of salvation in the house of his servant David").
n.15: Or "will flourish", like the horn that sprouts in verse 17. Hebrew *nezer*, a crown or diadem, the sign of consecration worn by the king and the high priest (2 Samuel 1:10; Exodus 29:6).

v: A song of ascents. Of David.[^1] Look, how good and how pleasant it is when brothers live together in unity![^2]
שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥ד הִנֵּ֣ה מַה־טּ֭וֹב וּמַה־נָּעִ֑ים שֶׁ֖בֶת אַחִ֣ים גַּם־יָֽחַד׃
It is like the fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, the beard of Aaron, running down over the collar of his robes.[^3]
כַּשֶּׁ֤מֶן הַטּ֨וֹב ׀ עַל־הָרֹ֗אשׁ יֹרֵ֗ד עַֽל־הַזָּקָ֥ן זְקַֽן־אַהֲרֹ֑ן שֶׁ֝יֹּרֵ֗ד עַל־פִּ֥י מִדּוֹתָֽיו׃
It is like the dew of Hermon,[^4] which falls on the mountains of Zion. For there the LORD[^5] has commanded the blessing: life forevermore.
כְּטַל־חֶרְמ֗וֹן שֶּׁיֹּרֵד֮ עַל־הַרְרֵ֢י צִ֫יּ֥וֹן כִּ֤י שָׁ֨ם ׀ צִוָּ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־הַבְּרָכָ֑ה חַ֝יִּ֗ים עַד־הָעוֹלָֽם׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "the dwelling of brothers also together".
n.3: Literally "over the mouth of his garments", the opening at the neck. The oil is the oil of anointing poured on Aaron's head when he was consecrated as high priest (Exodus 29:7; Leviticus 8:12).
n.4: Mount Hermon, the highest mountain in the region, in the far north, known for its heavy dew.
n.5: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.

v: A song of ascents.[^1] Come,[^2] bless the LORD,[^3] all you servants of the LORD, who stand in the house of the LORD by night.
שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּעֲ֫ל֥וֹת הִנֵּ֤ה ׀ בָּרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־יְ֭הוָה כָּל־עַבְדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הָעֹמְדִ֥ים בְּבֵית־יְ֝הוָ֗ה בַּלֵּילֽוֹת׃
Lift up your hands toward the sanctuary,[^4] and bless the LORD.
שְׂאֽוּ־יְדֵכֶ֥ם קֹ֑דֶשׁ וּ֝בָרֲכוּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
May the LORD bless you from Zion, the maker of heaven and earth.[^5]
יְבָרֶכְךָ֣ יְ֭הוָה מִצִיּ֑וֹן עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: *A song of ascents*: Hebrew *shir ha-ma'alot* (see the note on 120:1). In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. This is the last of the Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134).
n.2: Literally "Look".
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Or "in holiness". Hebrew *qodesh*, "holiness, the holy place".
n.5: "You" is singular: the priests' blessing on each worshiper (compare Numbers 6:24).

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Praise the name of the LORD;[^2] praise him, you servants of the LORD,
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ הַֽ֭לְלוּ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה הֽ͏ַ֝לְלוּ עַבְדֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.
שֶׁ֣֭עֹֽמְדִים בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה בְּ֝חַצְר֗וֹת בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; sing praises to his name, for it is pleasant.[^3]
הַֽ֭לְלוּ־יָהּ כִּי־ט֣וֹב יְהוָ֑ה זַמְּר֥וּ לִ֝שְׁמ֗וֹ כִּ֣י נָעִֽים׃
For the LORD has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as his treasured possession.[^4]
כִּֽי־יַעֲקֹ֗ב בָּחַ֣ר ל֣וֹ יָ֑הּ יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל לִסְגֻלָּתֽוֹ׃
For I know that the LORD is great, and our Lord is above all gods.
כִּ֤י אֲנִ֣י יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּי־גָד֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וַ֝אֲדֹנֵ֗ינוּ מִכָּל־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Whatever the LORD pleases, he does, in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all the depths.
כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־חָפֵ֥ץ יְהוָ֗ה עָ֫שָׂ֥ה בַּשָּׁמַ֥יִם וּבָאָ֑רֶץ בַּ֝יַּמִּ֗ים וְכָל־תְּהוֹמֽוֹת׃
He makes the clouds[^5] rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from his storehouses.[^6]
מַֽעֲלֶ֣ה נְשִׂאִים֮ מִקְצֵ֢ה הָ֫אָ֥רֶץ בְּרָקִ֣ים לַמָּטָ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה מֽוֹצֵא־ר֝וּחַ מֵאֽוֹצְרוֹתָֽיו׃
He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, both human and animal.
שֶֽׁ֭הִכָּה בְּכוֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם מֵ֝אָדָ֗ם עַד־בְּהֵמָֽה׃
He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
שָׁלַ֤ח ׀ אֹת֣וֹת וּ֖[d]מֹפְתִים בְּתוֹכֵ֣כִי מִצְרָ֑יִם בְּ֝פַרְעֹ֗ה וּבְכָל־עֲבָדָֽיו׃
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
שֶֽׁ֭הִכָּה גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝הָרַ֗ג מְלָכִ֥ים עֲצוּמִֽים׃
Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.[^7]
לְסִיח֤וֹן ׀ מֶ֤לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֗י וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וּ֝לְכֹ֗ל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to his people Israel.
וְנָתַ֣ן אַרְצָ֣ם נַחֲלָ֑ה נַ֝חֲלָ֗ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עַמּֽוֹ׃
LORD, your name endures forever, your renown,[^8] LORD, from generation to generation.
יְ֭הוָה שִׁמְךָ֣ לְעוֹלָ֑ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה זִכְרְךָ֥ לְדֹר־וָדֹֽר׃
For the LORD will give justice to his people[^9] and have compassion on his servants.
כִּֽי־יָדִ֣ין יְהוָ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ וְעַל־עֲ֝בָדָ֗יו יִתְנֶחָֽם׃
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.[^10]
עֲצַבֵּ֣י הַ֭גּוֹיִם כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֑ב מַ֝עֲשֵׂ֗ה יְדֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃
They have mouths, but cannot speak; they have eyes, but cannot see.
פֶּֽה־לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ עֵינַ֥יִם לָ֝הֶ֗ם וְלֹ֣א יִרְאֽוּ׃
They have ears, but cannot hear, and there is no breath in their mouths.
אָזְנַ֣יִם לָ֭הֶם וְלֹ֣א יַאֲזִ֑ינוּ אַ֝֗ף אֵין־יֶשׁ־ר֥וּחַ בְּפִיהֶֽם׃
Those who make them will become like them, and so will all who trust in them.
כְּ֭מוֹהֶם יִהְי֣וּ עֹשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כֹּ֭ל אֲשֶׁר־בֹּטֵ֣חַ בָּהֶֽם׃
House of Israel, bless the LORD! House of Aaron, bless the LORD!
בֵּ֣ית יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל בָּרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה בֵּ֥ית אַ֝הֲרֹ֗ן בָּרֲכ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
House of Levi, bless the LORD! You who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
בֵּ֣ית הַ֭לֵּוִי בָּרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה יִֽרְאֵ֥י יְ֝הוָ֗ה בָּרֲכ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
Blessed be the LORD from Zion, he who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה ׀ מִצִיּ֗וֹן שֹׁ֘כֵ֤ן יְֽרוּשָׁלִָ֗ם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also in verses 3 and 21.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "for he is gracious", "for it (his name) is lovely".
n.4: Hebrew *segullah*, a king's or an owner's personal treasure (Exodus 19:5).
n.5: Or "vapors".
n.6: This verse is the same as Jeremiah 10:13b and 51:16b.
n.7: Compare Numbers 21:21–35 and Joshua 12.
n.8: Literally "your remembrance", the name by which you are remembered (compare Exodus 3:15).
n.9: Literally "will judge his people", that is, vindicate them. This verse is the same as Deuteronomy 32:36a.
n.10: Verses 15–18 are nearly the same as 115:4–8.

v: Give thanks to the LORD,[^1] for he is good, for his faithful love[^2] endures forever.[^3]
הוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his faithful love endures forever.
ה֭וֹדוּ לֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his faithful love endures forever;
ה֭וֹדוּ לַאֲדֹנֵ֣י הָאֲדֹנִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
to him who alone does great wonders, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְעֹ֘שֵׂ֤ה נִפְלָא֣וֹת גְּדֹל֣וֹת לְבַדּ֑וֹ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who by understanding made the heavens, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְעֹשֵׂ֣ה הַ֭שָּׁמַיִם בִּתְבוּנָ֑ה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who spread out the earth on the waters, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְרֹקַ֣ע הָ֭אָרֶץ עַל־הַמָּ֑יִם כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who made the great lights, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְ֭עֹשֵׂה אוֹרִ֣ים גְּדֹלִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
the sun to rule by day, for his faithful love endures forever;
אֶת־הַ֭שֶּׁמֶשׁ לְמֶמְשֶׁ֣לֶת בַּיּ֑וֹם כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
the moon and the stars to rule by night, for his faithful love endures forever;
אֶת־הַיָּרֵ֣חַ וְ֭כוֹכָבִים לְמֶמְשְׁל֣וֹת בַּלָּ֑יְלָה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who struck down Egypt through their firstborn, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְמַכֵּ֣ה מִ֭צְרַיִם בִּבְכוֹרֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and brought Israel out from among them, for his faithful love endures forever;
וַיּוֹצֵ֣א יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹכָ֑ם כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for his faithful love endures forever;
בְּיָ֣ד חֲ֭זָקָה וּבִזְר֣וֹעַ נְטוּיָ֑ה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who divided the Red Sea[^4] in two,[^5] for his faithful love endures forever;
לְגֹזֵ֣ר יַם־ס֭וּף לִגְזָרִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and made Israel pass through the middle of it, for his faithful love endures forever;
וְהֶעֱבִ֣יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל בְּתוֹכ֑וֹ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
but swept[^6] Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, for his faithful love endures forever;
וְנִ֘עֵ֤ר פַּרְעֹ֣ה וְחֵיל֣וֹ בְיַם־ס֑וּף כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who led his people through the wilderness, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְמוֹלִ֣יךְ עַ֭מּוֹ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who struck down great kings, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְ֭מַכֵּה מְלָכִ֣ים גְּדֹלִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and killed mighty kings, for his faithful love endures forever;
וֽ͏ַ֭יַּהֲרֹג מְלָכִ֣ים אַדִּירִ֑ים כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Sihon king of the Amorites, for his faithful love endures forever;
לְ֭סִיחוֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֑י כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and Og king of Bashan,[^7] for his faithful love endures forever;
וּ֭לְעוֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and gave their land as an inheritance, for his faithful love endures forever;
וְנָתַ֣ן אַרְצָ֣ם לְנַחֲלָ֑ה כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
an inheritance to Israel his servant, for his faithful love endures forever;
נַ֭חֲלָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עַבְדּ֑וֹ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who remembered us in our low condition, for his faithful love endures forever;
שֶׁ֭בְּשִׁפְלֵנוּ זָ֣כַר לָ֑נוּ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
and rescued us from our adversaries, for his faithful love endures forever;
וַיִּפְרְקֵ֥נוּ מִצָּרֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
who gives food to every living creature,[^8] for his faithful love endures forever.
נֹתֵ֣ן לֶ֭חֶם לְכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his faithful love endures forever.
ה֭וֹדוּ לְאֵ֣ל הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.3: Literally "for his faithful love is forever". The refrain ends every verse of the psalm, probably sung by the congregation in response to the leader (compare 118:1–4; 2 Chronicles 7:3, 6; Ezra 3:11). In Jewish tradition this psalm is called the Great Hallel.
n.4: Hebrew *Yam Suph*, literally "Sea of Reeds". The Greek Septuagint calls it "the Red Sea"; also in verse 15.
n.5: Literally "who cut the Red Sea into pieces".
n.6: Literally "shook off".
n.7: Verses 19–22 are nearly the same as 135:11–12. Compare Numbers 21:21–35.
n.8: Literally "to all flesh".

v: By the rivers of Babylon,[^1] there we sat down and wept when we remembered Zion.
עַ֥ל נַהֲר֨וֹת ׀ בָּבֶ֗ל שָׁ֣ם יָ֭שַׁבְנוּ גַּם־בָּכִ֑ינוּ בְּ֝זָכְרֵ֗נוּ אֶת־צִיּֽוֹן׃
On the poplars[^2] there we hung up our lyres.
עַֽל־עֲרָבִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָ֑הּ תָּ֝לִ֗ינוּ כִּנֹּרוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
For there our captors asked us for songs, and our tormentors[^3] asked for joy: "Sing us one of the songs of Zion!"
כִּ֤י שָׁ֨ם שְֽׁאֵל֪וּנוּ שׁוֹבֵ֡ינוּ דִּבְרֵי־שִׁ֭יר וְתוֹלָלֵ֣ינוּ שִׂמְחָ֑ה שִׁ֥ירוּ לָ֝֗נוּ מִשִּׁ֥יר צִיּֽוֹן׃
How can we sing the song of the LORD[^4] in a foreign land?
אֵ֗יךְ נָשִׁ֥יר אֶת־שִׁיר־יְהוָ֑ה עַ֝֗ל אַדְמַ֥ת נֵכָֽר׃
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.[^5]
אִֽם־אֶשְׁכָּחֵ֥ךְ יְֽרוּשָׁלִָ֗ם תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח יְמִינֽ͏ִי׃
May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
תִּדְבַּֽק־לְשׁוֹנִ֨י ׀ לְחִכִּי֮ אִם־לֹ֢א אֶזְכְּ֫רֵ֥כִי אִם־לֹ֣א אַ֭עֲלֶה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֑͏ִם עַ֝֗ל רֹ֣אשׁ שִׂמְחָתֽ͏ִי׃
Remember, LORD, against the Edomites the day of Jerusalem,[^6] when they said, "Tear it down! Tear it down to its foundations!"[^7]
זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָ֨ה ׀ לִבְנֵ֬י אֱד֗וֹם אֵת֮ י֤וֹם יְֽרוּשָׁ֫לָ֥͏ִם הָ֭אֹ֣מְרִים עָ֤רוּ ׀ עָ֑רוּ עָ֝֗ד הַיְס֥וֹד בָּֽהּ׃
Daughter Babylon,[^8] doomed to destruction,[^9] happy[^10] is the one who pays you back for what you have done to us.
בַּת־בָּבֶ֗ל הַשְּׁד֫וּדָ֥ה אַשְׁרֵ֥י שֶׁיְשַׁלֶּם־לָ֑ךְ אֶת־גְּ֝מוּלֵ֗ךְ שֶׁגָּמַ֥לְתְּ לָֽנוּ׃
Happy is the one who seizes your little ones and dashes them against the rock![^11]
אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ שֶׁיֹּאחֵ֓ז וְנִפֵּ֬ץ אֶֽת־עֹלָלַ֗יִךְ אֶל־הַסָּֽלַע׃

n.1: The rivers and canals of the land of Babylon, between the Tigris and the Euphrates, where the people of Judah lived in exile after Jerusalem fell in 587 or 586 BC (2 Kings 25).
n.2: Hebrew *aravim*, traditionally "willows", probably the poplars that grow along the Euphrates.
n.3: Hebrew *tolalenu*, a word found only here, so the meaning is uncertain. Perhaps "those who plundered us".
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Literally "may my right hand forget", that is, forget how to play the lyre. Some scholars read "may my right hand wither", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.6: Literally "Remember, LORD, for the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem", the day the city fell. The Edomites, Israel's neighbors to the south and descendants of Esau, rejoiced at its fall and joined in the plunder (Obadiah 10–14; Lamentations 4:21–22; Ezekiel 25:12).
n.7: Literally "Lay it bare, lay it bare, down to the foundation in it."
n.8: A poetic name for the city of Babylon and its people, pictured as a woman.
n.9: Literally "devastated", that is, about to be devastated.
n.10: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed". Also in verse 9.
n.11: Conquering armies of the time killed the children of a captured city in this way (2 Kings 8:12; Hosea 14:1; 13:16 in most English Bibles; Nahum 3:10), and the exiles had seen the children of Jerusalem die when the city fell (Lamentations 2:11, 19–21). The psalm asks that Babylon be paid back in kind (verse 8), as the prophets announced against it (Isaiah 13:16; Jeremiah 51:24, 56).

v: Of David.[^1] I will give thanks to you with all my heart; before the gods[^2] I will sing your praise.
לְדָוִ֨ד ׀ אוֹדְךָ֥ בְכָל־לִבִּ֑י נֶ֖גֶד אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲזַמְּרֶֽךָּ׃
I will bow down toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name for your faithful love[^3] and your faithfulness, for you have made your promise greater than all your name.[^4]
אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֨ה אֶל־הֵיכַ֪ל קָדְשְׁךָ֡ וְא֘וֹדֶ֤ה אֶת־שְׁמֶ֗ךָ עַל־חַסְדְּךָ֥ וְעַל־אֲמִתֶּ֑ךָ כִּֽי־הִגְדַּ֥לְתָּ עַל־כָּל־שִׁ֝מְךָ֗ אִמְרָתֶֽךָ׃
On the day I called, you answered me; you made me bold, with strength in my soul.[^5]
בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָֽאתִי וַֽתַּעֲנֵ֑נִי תַּרְהִבֵ֖נִי בְנַפְשִׁ֣י עֹֽז׃
All the kings of the earth will give thanks to you, LORD,[^6] when they hear the words of your mouth.[^7]
יוֹד֣וּךָ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־מַלְכֵי־אָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ אִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃
They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.
וְ֭יָשִׁירוּ בְּדַרְכֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־גָ֝ד֗וֹל כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָֽה׃
For though the LORD is high, he looks on the lowly; but the proud he knows from far away.
כִּי־רָ֣ם יְ֭הוָה וְשָׁפָ֣ל יִרְאֶ֑ה וְ֝גָבֹ֗הַּ מִמֶּרְחָ֥ק יְיֵדָֽע׃
Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you preserve my life; you stretch out your hand against the anger of my enemies, and your right hand saves me.
אִם־אֵלֵ֤ךְ ׀ בְּקֶ֥רֶב צָרָ֗ה תְּחַ֫יֵּ֥נִי עַ֤ל אַ֣ף אֹ֖[d]יְבַי תִּשְׁלַ֣ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וְת֖וֹשִׁיעֵ֣נִי יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me.[^8] LORD, your faithful love endures forever; do not abandon the works of your hands.
יְהוָה֮ יִגְמֹ֢ר בַּ֫עֲדִ֥י יְ֭הוָה חַסְדְּךָ֣ לְעוֹלָ֑ם מַעֲשֵׂ֖י יָדֶ֣יךָ אַל־תֶּֽרֶף׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. Psalms 138–145 all have David's name in their titles.
n.2: Hebrew *elohim*, which can mean "God", "gods" or "heavenly beings". Here probably the gods of the nations, or the heavenly beings around God's throne. The Septuagint reads "before the angels".
n.3: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 8.
n.4: Literally "for you have made great your promise (*imrah*) above all your name". The Hebrew is difficult. Perhaps "you have done even more than you promised", or "you have exalted your name and your promise above everything".
n.5: Literally "you made me bold in my soul (*nephesh*), strength".
n.6: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Or "for they have heard".
n.8: Literally "The LORD will complete (it) on my behalf".

v: For the director. Of David. A psalm.[^1] LORD,[^2] you have searched me and you know me.
לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ לְדָוִ֣ד מִזְמ֑וֹר יְהוָ֥ה חֲ֝קַרְתַּ֗נִי וַתֵּדָֽע׃
You know when I sit down and when I rise up; you understand my thoughts from far away.
אַתָּ֣ה יָ֭דַעְתָּ שִׁבְתִּ֣י וְקוּמִ֑י בַּ֥נְתָּה לְ֝רֵעִ֗י מֵרָחֽוֹק׃
You sift[^3] my path and my lying down; you are familiar with all my ways.
אָרְחִ֣י וְרִבְעִ֣י זֵרִ֑יתָ וְֽכָל־דְּרָכַ֥י הִסְכַּֽנְתָּה׃
Even before a word is on my tongue, look, LORD, you know it completely.[^4]
כִּ֤י אֵ֣ין מִ֭לָּה בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֑י הֵ֥ן יְ֝הוָ֗ה יָדַ֥עְתָּ כֻלָּֽהּ׃
You hem me in behind and before; you have laid your hand on me.
אָח֣וֹר וָקֶ֣דֶם צַרְתָּ֑נִי וַתָּ֖שֶׁת עָלַ֣י כַּפֶּֽכָה׃
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is too high, I cannot reach it.
*פלאיה **פְּלִ֣יאָֽה דַ֣עַת מִמֶּ֑נִּי נִ֝שְׂגְּבָ֗ה לֹא־א֥וּכַֽל לָֽהּ׃
Where can I go from your Spirit?[^5] Where can I flee from your presence?
אָ֭נָ֥ה אֵלֵ֣ךְ מֵרוּחֶ֑ךָ וְ֝אָ֗נָה מִפָּנֶ֥יךָ אֶבְרָֽח׃
If I go up to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol,[^6] you are there too.
אִם־אֶסַּ֣ק שָׁ֭מַיִם שָׁ֣ם אָ֑תָּה וְאַצִּ֖יעָה שְּׁא֣וֹל הִנֶּֽךָּ׃
If I take the wings of the dawn and settle at the far side of the sea,[^7]
אֶשָּׂ֥א כַנְפֵי־שָׁ֑חַר אֶ֝שְׁכְּנָ֗ה בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית יָֽם׃
even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me fast.
גַּם־שָׁ֭ם יָדְךָ֣ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְֽתֹאחֲזֵ֥נִי יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
If I say, "Surely the darkness will overwhelm me,[^8] and the light around me will become night,"
וָ֭אֹמַר אַךְ־חֹ֣שֶׁךְ יְשׁוּפֵ֑נִי וְ֝לַ֗יְלָה א֣וֹר בַּעֲדֵֽנִי׃
even the darkness is not dark to you; the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to you.[^9]
גַּם־חֹשֶׁךְ֮ לֹֽא־יַחְשִׁ֢יךְ מִ֫מֶּ֥ךָ וְ֭לַיְלָה כַּיּ֣וֹם יָאִ֑יר כַּ֝חֲשֵׁיכָ֗ה כָּאוֹרָֽה׃
For you created my inmost being;[^10] you wove me together in my mother's womb.
כִּֽי־אַ֭תָּה קָנִ֣יתָ כִלְיֹתָ֑י תְּ֝סֻכֵּ֗נִי בְּבֶ֣טֶן אִמִּֽי׃
I praise you, for I am awesomely and wonderfully made.[^11] Wonderful are your works; my soul[^12] knows it very well.
אֽוֹדְךָ֗ עַ֤ל כִּ֥י נוֹרָא֗וֹת נִ֫פְלֵ֥יתִי נִפְלָאִ֥ים מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י יֹדַ֥עַת מְאֹֽד׃
My frame[^13] was not hidden from you when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.[^14]
לֹא־נִכְחַ֥ד עָצְמִ֗י מִ֫מֶּ֥ךָּ אֲשֶׁר־עֻשֵּׂ֥יתִי בַסֵּ֑תֶר רֻ֝קַּ֗מְתִּי בְּֽתַחְתִּיּ֥וֹת אָֽרֶץ׃
Your eyes saw my unformed body;[^15] in your book they were all written, the days that were shaped for me, each one of them.[^16]
גָּלְמִ֤י ׀ רָ֘א֤וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־סִפְרְךָ֮ כֻּלָּ֢ם יִכָּ֫תֵ֥בוּ יָמִ֥ים יֻצָּ֑רוּ *ולא **וְל֖וֹ אֶחָ֣ד בָּהֶֽם׃
How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is the sum of them!
וְלִ֗י מַה־יָּקְר֣וּ רֵעֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑ל מֶ֥ה עָ֝צְמוּ רָאשֵׁיהֶֽם׃
If I counted them, they would outnumber the grains of sand. I awake, and I am still with you.[^17]
אֶ֭סְפְּרֵם מֵח֣וֹל יִרְבּ֑וּן הֱ֝קִיצֹ֗תִי וְעוֹדִ֥י עִמָּֽךְ׃
If only you would kill the wicked, God![^18] You bloodthirsty people,[^19] go away from me!
אִם־תִּקְטֹ֖ל אֱל֥וֹהַּ ׀ רָשָׁ֑ע וְאַנְשֵׁ֥י דָ֝מִ֗ים ס֣וּרוּ מֶֽנִּי׃
They speak of you with evil intent; your enemies take your name in vain.[^20]
אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹ֭אמְרֻךָ לִמְזִמָּ֑ה נָשֻׂ֖א לַשָּׁ֣וְא עָרֶֽיךָ׃
Do I not hate those who hate you, LORD? Do I not loathe those who rise up against you?
הֲלֽוֹא־מְשַׂנְאֶ֖יךָ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ אֶשְׂנָ֑א וּ֝בִתְקוֹמְמֶ֗יךָ אֶתְקוֹטָֽט׃
I hate them with complete hatred; they have become my enemies.
תַּכְלִ֣ית שִׂנְאָ֣ה שְׂנֵאתִ֑ים לְ֝אוֹיְבִ֗ים הָ֣יוּ לִֽי׃
Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.
חָקְרֵ֣נִי אֵ֭ל וְדַ֣ע לְבָבִ֑י בְּ֝חָנֵ֗נִי וְדַ֣ע שַׂרְעַפָּֽי׃
See if there is any hurtful way in me,[^21] and lead me in the everlasting way.[^22]
וּרְאֵ֗ה אִם־דֶּֽרֶךְ־עֹ֥צֶב בִּ֑י וּ֝נְחֵ֗נִי בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ עוֹלָֽם׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "measure", "examine". Hebrew *zerita*, perhaps from the verb for winnowing grain.
n.4: Literally "For there is not a word on my tongue, (but) look, LORD, you know all of it."
n.5: Or "your spirit", "your breath". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: That is, the far west. The dawn is in the east, and the sea, the Mediterranean, in the west.
n.8: Hebrew *yeshufeni*, a verb that elsewhere means "crush" or "strike" (Genesis 3:15). Many scholars read "will cover me", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.9: Literally "as the darkness, so the light".
n.10: Literally "my kidneys", thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings and thoughts.
n.11: Literally "for awesomely I am set apart (or wonderfully made)". The Septuagint reads "for you are awesomely wonderful".
n.12: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self.
n.13: Literally "my bone(s)".
n.14: A poetic picture of the womb, as hidden as the depths of the earth.
n.15: Hebrew *golmi*, a word found only here: "my embryo", "my shapeless form".
n.16: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. The Hebrew text is written "and not (one) among them" (traditionally "when as yet there was none of them") but read "and to it (was) one among them".
n.17: Some scholars read "I come to the end (of them)", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.18: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic word for God.
n.19: Literally "men of blood", that is, murderers.
n.20: Literally "they lift up to falsehood, your enemies", echoing the command not to misuse the LORD's name (Exodus 20:7). *Your enemies*: Hebrew *arekha*, a rare word, probably from Aramaic; it usually means "your cities".
n.21: Or "any way of pain", "any idolatrous way". Hebrew *otsev* can mean "pain" or "idol".
n.22: Or "the ancient way", the way of old.

v: For the director. A psalm of David.[^1]
לַמְנַצֵּ֗חַ מִזְמ֥וֹר לְדָוִֽד׃
Rescue me, LORD,[^2] from evil people;[^3] guard me from the violent,
חַלְּצֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה מֵאָדָ֣ם רָ֑ע מֵאִ֖ישׁ חֲמָסִ֣ים תִּנְצְרֵֽנִי׃
who plan evil things in their hearts and stir up wars every day.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשְׁב֣וּ רָע֣וֹת בְּלֵ֑ב כָּל־י֝֗וֹם יָג֥וּרוּ מִלְחָמֽוֹת׃
They sharpen their tongues like a serpent's; the venom of vipers is under their lips.[^4] Selah.[^5]
שָֽׁנֲנ֣וּ לְשׁוֹנָם֮ כְּֽמוֹ נָ֫חָ֥שׁ חֲמַ֥ת עַכְשׁ֑וּב תַּ֖חַת שְׂפָתֵ֣ימוֹ סֶֽלָה׃
Keep me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; guard me from the violent, who plan to trip up my feet.
שָׁמְרֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה ׀ מִ֘ידֵ֤י רָשָׁ֗ע מֵאִ֣ישׁ חֲמָסִ֣ים תִּנְצְרֵ֑נִי אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָ֝שְׁב֗וּ לִדְח֥וֹת פְּעָמָֽי׃
The arrogant have hidden a trap for me, and cords; they have spread a net beside the path; they have set snares for me. Selah.
טָֽמְנֽוּ־גֵאִ֨ים ׀ פַּ֡ח לִ֗י וַחֲבָלִ֗ים פָּ֣רְשׂוּ רֶ֭שֶׁת לְיַד־מַעְגָּ֑ל מֹקְשִׁ֖ים שָֽׁתוּ־לִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃
I say to the LORD, "You are my God." Listen, LORD, to my voice as I plead for mercy.
אָמַ֣רְתִּי לַ֭יהוָה אֵ֣לִי אָ֑תָּה הַאֲזִ֥ינָה יְ֝הוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל תַּחֲנוּנָֽי׃
GOD the Lord, my strong salvation,[^6] you shield my head on the day of battle.
יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי עֹ֣ז יְשׁוּעָתִ֑י סַכֹּ֥תָה לְ֝רֹאשִׁ֗י בְּי֣וֹם נָֽשֶׁק׃
Do not grant, LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not let their schemes succeed, or they will be exalted. Selah.
אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן יְ֭הוָה מַאֲוַיֵּ֣י רָשָׁ֑ע זְמָמ֥וֹ אַל־תָּ֝פֵ֗ק יָר֥וּמוּ סֶֽלָה׃
As for the heads of those who surround me,[^7] may the trouble their own lips cause cover them.
רֹ֥אשׁ מְסִבָּ֑י עֲמַ֖ל שְׂפָתֵ֣ימוֹ *יכסומו **יְכַסֵּֽמוֹ׃
May burning coals fall on them;[^8] may they be thrown into the fire, into deep pits,[^9] never to rise again.
*ימיטו **יִמּ֥וֹטוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם גֶּֽחָ֫לִ֥ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יַפִּלֵ֑ם בְּ֝מַהֲמֹר֗וֹת בָּל־יָקֽוּמוּ׃
Do not let a slanderer[^10] be established in the land; may evil hunt down the violent with blow upon blow.[^11]
אִ֥ישׁ לָשׁוֹן֮ בַּל־יִכּ֢וֹן בָּ֫אָ֥רֶץ אִישׁ־חָמָ֥ס רָ֑ע יְ֝צוּדֶ֗נּוּ לְמַדְחֵפֹֽת׃
I know[^12] that the LORD upholds the cause of the afflicted, and justice for the needy.
*ידעת **יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְ֭הוָה דִּ֣ין עָנִ֑י מִ֝שְׁפַּ֗ט אֶבְיֹנִֽים׃
Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will live in your presence.
אַ֣ךְ צַ֭דִּיקִים יוֹד֣וּ לִשְׁמֶ֑ךָ יֵשְׁב֥וּ יְ֝שָׁרִ֗ים אֶת־פָּנֶֽיךָ׃

n.1: *For the director*: Hebrew *lamenatseach*, probably the leader of the temple music. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–14 are 140:1–13 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "from an evil human being (*adam*); from a man of violence". Also in verse 5.
n.4: Romans 3:13 quotes this line.
n.5: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning. Also in verses 6 and 9.
n.6: Literally "the strength of my salvation". *GOD the Lord*: Hebrew *YHWH Adonai*. Next to "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.7: Literally "The head of those who surround me". Or, joining the word to the end of verse 9, "they lift up their heads".
n.8: The Hebrew text is written "May they bring down burning coals on them" but read "May burning coals fall on them". *May they be thrown*: literally "may he make them fall".
n.9: Hebrew *mahamorot*, a word found only here, perhaps "pits of water" or "deep pits".
n.10: Literally "a man of tongue".
n.11: Hebrew *lemadchefot*, a word found only here, perhaps "with thrust upon thrust" or "to their overthrow".
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "you know" but read "I know".

v: A psalm of David.[^1] LORD,[^2] I call to you; come quickly to me. Listen to my voice when I call to you.
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥ד יְהוָ֣ה קְ֭רָאתִיךָ ח֣וּשָׁה לִּ֑י הַאֲזִ֥ינָה ק֝וֹלִ֗י בְּקָרְאִי־לָֽךְ׃
May my prayer be set before you like incense, the lifting up of my hands like the evening offering.[^3]
תִּכּ֤וֹן תְּפִלָּתִ֣י קְטֹ֣רֶת לְפָנֶ֑יךָ מַֽשְׂאַ֥ת כַּ֝פַּ֗י מִנְחַת־עָֽרֶב׃
Set a guard, LORD, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips.
שִׁיתָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה שָׁמְרָ֣ה לְפִ֑י נִ֝צְּרָ֗ה עַל־דַּ֥ל שְׂפָתָֽי׃
Do not let my heart turn to anything evil, to do wicked deeds with those who are evildoers; do not let me eat of their delicacies.
אַל־תַּט־לִבִּ֨י לְדָבָ֪ר ׀ רָ֡ע לְהִתְע֘וֹלֵ֤ל עֲלִל֨וֹת ׀ בְּרֶ֗שַׁע אֶת־אִישִׁ֥ים פֹּֽעֲלֵי־אָ֑וֶן וּבַל־אֶ֝לְחַ֗ם בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם׃
Let a righteous person strike me: it is faithful love;[^4] let him rebuke me: it is oil for my head; let my head not refuse it. For my prayer is still against their evil deeds.[^5]
יֶֽהֶלְמֵֽנִי־צַדִּ֨יק ׀ חֶ֡סֶד וְֽיוֹכִיחֵ֗נִי שֶׁ֣מֶן רֹ֭אשׁ אַל־יָנִ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י כִּי־ע֥וֹד ו֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
When their rulers are thrown down from the sides of the cliff,[^6] they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
נִשְׁמְט֣וּ בִֽידֵי־סֶ֭לַע שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם וְשָׁמְע֥וּ אֲ֝מָרַ֗י כִּ֣י נָעֵֽמוּ׃
As when one plows and breaks up the ground, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.[^7]
כְּמ֤וֹ פֹלֵ֣חַ וּבֹקֵ֣עַ בָּאָ֑רֶץ נִפְזְר֥וּ עֲ֝צָמֵ֗ינוּ לְפִ֣י שְׁאֽוֹל׃
But my eyes are on you, GOD the Lord; in you I take refuge; do not pour out my life.[^8]
כִּ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ ׀ יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲדֹנָ֣י עֵינָ֑י בְּכָ֥ה חָ֝סִ֗יתִי אַל־תְּעַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Keep me from the trap they have laid for me,[^9] and from the snares of the evildoers.
שָׁמְרֵ֗נִי מִ֣ידֵי פַ֭ח יָ֣קְשׁוּ לִ֑י וּ֝מֹקְשׁ֗וֹת פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
Let the wicked fall into their own nets,[^10] while I pass by safely.
יִפְּל֣וּ בְמַכְמֹרָ֣יו רְשָׁעִ֑ים יַ֥חַד אָ֝נֹכִ֗י עַֽד־אֶעֱבֽוֹר׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *minchah*, often the grain offering (Leviticus 2), but also any gift or offering. Incense was offered morning and evening (Exodus 30:7–8), and an offering was made each evening (Exodus 29:39–41; 2 Kings 16:15).
n.4: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love; here, a kindness. Or "Let a righteous person strike me in faithful love and rebuke me", or "If a righteous person strikes me, it is a kindness".
n.5: Literally "for still, and my prayer in their evils". The Hebrew of verses 5–7 is very difficult, and every rendering of them is uncertain. Or "my prayer continues even in their troubles".
n.6: Literally "into the hands of the rock". Or "When their judges are handed over to the rock".
n.7: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.8: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Or "do not leave me defenseless". Compare Isaiah 53:12, "he poured out his life to death". *GOD the Lord*: Hebrew *YHWH Adonai*. Next to "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.9: Literally "from the hands of the trap they have set for me".
n.10: Literally "into his nets", perhaps God's nets, or each into his own.

v: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.[^1]
מַשְׂכִּ֥יל לְדָוִ֑ד בִּהְיוֹת֖וֹ בַמְּעָרָ֣ה תְפִלָּֽה׃
With my voice I cry out to the LORD;[^2] with my voice I plead with the LORD for mercy.
ק֭וֹלִי אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֶזְעָ֑ק ק֝וֹלִ֗י אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֶתְחַנָּֽן׃
I pour out my complaint before him; I tell him of my trouble.
אֶשְׁפֹּ֣ךְ לְפָנָ֣יו שִׂיחִ֑י צָ֝רָתִ֗י לְפָנָ֥יו אַגִּֽיד׃
When my spirit grows faint within me, you know my way. In the path where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
בְּהִתְעַטֵּ֬ף עָלַ֨י ׀ רוּחִ֗י וְאַתָּה֮ יָדַ֢עְתָּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י בְּאֹֽרַח־ז֥וּ אֲהַלֵּ֑ךְ טָמְנ֖וּ פַ֣ח לִֽי׃
Look to my right and see: there is no one who takes notice of me.[^3] I have no refuge;[^4] no one cares for my life.[^5]
הַבֵּ֤יט יָמִ֨ין ׀ וּרְאֵה֮ וְאֵֽין־לִ֢י מַ֫כִּ֥יר אָבַ֣ד מָנ֣וֹס מִמֶּ֑נִּי אֵ֖ין דּוֹרֵ֣שׁ לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃
I cry out to you, LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."
זָעַ֥קְתִּי אֵלֶ֗יךָ יְה֫וָ֥ה אָ֭מַרְתִּי אַתָּ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י חֶ֝לְקִ֗י בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחַיִּים׃
Listen to my cry, for I am brought very low. Rescue me from my persecutors, for they are too strong for me.
הַקְשִׁ֤יבָה ׀ אֶֽל־רִנָּתִי֮ כִּֽי־דַלּ֢וֹתִ֫י מְאֹ֥ד הַצִּילֵ֥נִי מֵרֹדְפַ֑י כִּ֖י אָמְצ֣וּ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
Bring me out of prison,[^6] so that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will gather around me,[^7] for you will deal generously with me.
ה֘וֹצִ֤יאָה מִמַּסְגֵּ֨ר ׀ נַפְשִׁי֮ לְהוֹד֢וֹת אֶת־שְׁ֫מֶ֥ךָ בִּ֭י יַכְתִּ֣רוּ צַדִּיקִ֑ים כִּ֖י תִגְמֹ֣ל עָלֽ͏ָי׃

n.1: *Maskil*: a term of uncertain meaning, perhaps "a skillful psalm" or "a psalm of instruction". *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". *In the cave*: David hid from Saul in the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) and in a cave near En-gedi (1 Samuel 24:4; 24:3 in most English Bibles); compare the title of Psalm 57. In the Hebrew text the title is verse 1, so verses 2–8 are 142:1–7 in most English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: An advocate or protector stood at a person's right hand (compare 16:8; 109:31; 110:5).
n.4: Literally "Refuge has perished from me".
n.5: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verse 8.
n.6: Literally "Bring my soul (*nephesh*) out of prison".
n.7: Or "will put a crown on me". Hebrew *yakhtiru*, from the word for "crown".

v: A psalm of David.[^1] LORD,[^2] hear my prayer; listen to my pleas for mercy. In your faithfulness answer me, in your righteousness.
מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥ד יְהוָ֤ה ׀ שְׁמַ֬ע תְּפִלָּתִ֗י הַאֲזִ֥ינָה אֶל־תַּחֲנוּנַ֑י בֶּאֱמֻנָתְךָ֥ עֲ֝נֵ֗נִי בְּצִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
Do not bring your servant into judgment, for no one living is righteous before you.[^3]
וְאַל־תָּב֣וֹא בְ֭מִשְׁפָּט אֶת־עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֤י לֹֽא־יִצְדַּ֖ק לְפָנֶ֣יךָ כָל־חָֽי׃
For the enemy has pursued my soul;[^4] he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me sit in darkness like those long dead.[^5]
כִּ֥י רָ֘דַ֤ף אוֹיֵ֨ב ׀ נַפְשִׁ֗י דִּכָּ֣א לָ֭אָרֶץ חַיָּתִ֑י הוֹשִׁיבַ֥נִי בְ֝מַחֲשַׁכִּ֗ים כְּמֵתֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃
So my spirit grows faint within me; my heart within me is appalled.
וַתִּתְעַטֵּ֣ף עָלַ֣י רוּחִ֑י בְּ֝תוֹכִ֗י יִשְׁתּוֹמֵ֥ם לִבִּֽי׃
I remember the days of old; I meditate on all your deeds; I reflect on the work of your hands.
זָ֘כַ֤רְתִּי יָמִ֨ים ׀ מִקֶּ֗דֶם הָגִ֥יתִי בְכָל־פָּעֳלֶ֑ךָ בְּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדֶ֣יךָ אֲשׂוֹחֵֽחַ׃
I spread out my hands to you; my soul thirsts for you like a parched land.[^6] Selah.[^7]
פֵּרַ֣שְׂתִּי יָדַ֣י אֵלֶ֑יךָ נַפְשִׁ֓י ׀ כְּאֶֽרֶץ־עֲיֵפָ֖ה לְךָ֣ סֶֽלָה׃
Answer me quickly, LORD; my spirit fails. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
מַ֘הֵ֤ר עֲנֵ֨נִי ׀ יְהוָה֮ כָּלְתָ֢ה ר֫וּחִ֥י אַל־תַּסְתֵּ֣ר פָּנֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי וְ֝נִמְשַׁ֗לְתִּי עִם־יֹ֥רְדֵי בֽוֹר׃
Let me hear of your faithful love[^8] in the morning, for in you I trust. Make me know the way I should go, for to you I lift up my soul.
הַשְׁמִ֘יעֵ֤נִי בַבֹּ֨קֶר ׀ חַסְדֶּךָ֮ כִּֽי־בְךָ֢ בָ֫טָ֥חְתִּי הוֹדִיעֵ֗נִי דֶּֽרֶךְ־ז֥וּ אֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־אֵ֝לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֥אתִי נַפְשִֽׁי׃
Rescue me from my enemies, LORD; I hide myself in you.[^9]
הַצִּילֵ֖נִי מֵאֹיְבַ֥י ׀ יְהוָ֗ה אֵלֶ֥יךָ כִסִּֽתִי׃
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. May your good Spirit[^10] lead me on level ground.
לַמְּדֵ֤נִי ׀ לַ֥עֲשׂ֣וֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ֮ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֢ה אֱל֫וֹהָ֥י רוּחֲךָ֥ טוֹבָ֑ה תַּ֝נְחֵ֗נִי בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִישֽׁוֹר׃
For the sake of your name, LORD, give me life; in your righteousness bring me[^11] out of trouble.
לְמַֽעַן־שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה תְּחַיֵּ֑נִי בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֓ ׀ תּוֹצִ֖יא מִצָּרָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
In your faithful love, destroy my enemies, and wipe out all my adversaries,[^12] for I am your servant.
וּֽבְחַסְדְּךָ֮ תַּצְמִ֢ית אֹ֫יְבָ֥י וְֽ֭הַאֲבַדְתָּ כָּל־צֹרֲרֵ֣י נַפְשִׁ֑י כִּ֝֗י אֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Or "for no one living will be found in the right before you". Paul echoes this line in Romans 3:20 and Galatians 2:16.
n.4: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. Also in verses 6 and 8.
n.5: Literally "like the dead of long ago". Compare Lamentations 3:6.
n.6: Literally "my soul (*nephesh*) (is) like a weary land for you".
n.7: Hebrew *selah*, a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning.
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 12.
n.9: Literally "to you I have covered", perhaps "I have hidden myself with you". The Septuagint reads "to you I have fled for refuge".
n.10: Or "your good spirit". Hebrew *ruach*. Compare Nehemiah 9:20.
n.11: Literally "bring my soul (*nephesh*)".
n.12: Literally "all the adversaries of my soul (*nephesh*)".

v: Of David.[^1] Blessed be the LORD,[^2] my rock, who trains my hands for war, my fingers for battle,
לְדָוִ֨ד ׀ בָּ֘ר֤וּךְ יְהוָ֨ה ׀ צוּרִ֗י הַֽמְלַמֵּ֣ד יָדַ֣י לַקְרָ֑ב אֶ֝צְבְּעוֹתַ֗י לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
my faithful love[^3] and my fortress, my stronghold and my deliverer, my shield, in whom I take refuge, who subdues my people under me.[^4]
חַסְדִּ֥י וּמְצוּדָתִי֮ מִשְׂגַּבִּ֢י וּֽמְפַלְטִ֫י לִ֥י מָ֭גִנִּי וּב֣וֹ חָסִ֑יתִי הָרוֹדֵ֖ד עַמִּ֣י תַחְתָּֽי׃
LORD, what is a human being, that you take notice of him, a son of man,[^5] that you think of him?
יְֽהוָ֗ה מָה־אָ֭דָם וַתֵּדָעֵ֑הוּ בֶּן־אֱ֝נ֗וֹשׁ וַֽתְּחַשְּׁבֵֽהוּ׃
A human being is like a breath;[^6] his days are like a passing shadow.
אָ֭דָם לַהֶ֣בֶל דָּמָ֑ה יָ֝מָ֗יו כְּצֵ֣ל עוֹבֵֽר׃
LORD, bend your heavens and come down; touch the mountains, so that they smoke.
יְ֭הוָה הַט־שָׁמֶ֣יךָ וְתֵרֵ֑ד גַּ֖ע בֶּהָרִ֣ים וְֽיֶעֱשָֽׁנוּ׃
Flash out lightning and scatter them; send out your arrows and throw them into confusion.
בְּר֣וֹק בָּ֭רָק וּתְפִיצֵ֑ם שְׁלַ֥ח חִ֝צֶּ֗יךָ וּתְהֻמֵּֽם׃
Stretch out your hands from on high; set me free and rescue me from the mighty waters, from the hand of foreigners,
שְׁלַ֥ח יָדֶ֗יךָ מִמָּ֫ר֥וֹם פְּצֵ֣נִי וְ֭הַצִּילֵנִי מִמַּ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים מִ֝יַּ֗ד בְּנֵ֣י נֵכָֽר׃
whose mouths speak lies, and whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.[^7]
אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃
God, I will sing a new song to you; on a ten-stringed harp I will make music to you,
אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים שִׁ֣יר חָ֭דָשׁ אָשִׁ֣ירָה לָּ֑ךְ בְּנֵ֥בֶל עָ֝שׂ֗וֹר אֲזַמְּרָה־לָּֽךְ׃
the one who gives victory to kings, who sets David his servant free from the cruel sword.[^8]
הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן תְּשׁוּעָ֗ה לַמְּלָ֫כִ֥ים הַ֭פּוֹצֶה אֶת־דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדּ֗וֹ מֵחֶ֥רֶב רָעָֽה׃
Set me free and rescue me from the hand of foreigners, whose mouths speak lies, and whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
פְּצֵ֥נִי וְהַצִּילֵנִי֮ מִיַּ֢ד בְּֽנֵי־נֵ֫כָ֥ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּ֭יהֶם דִּבֶּר־שָׁ֑וְא וִֽ֝ימִינָ֗ם יְמִ֣ין שָֽׁקֶר׃
May our sons in their youth be like plants grown tall,[^9] our daughters like corner pillars carved for a palace.[^10]
אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּנֵ֨ינוּ ׀ כִּנְטִעִים֮ מְגֻדָּלִ֢ים בִּֽנְעוּרֵ֫יהֶ֥ם בְּנוֹתֵ֥ינוּ כְזָוִיֹּ֑ת מְ֝חֻטָּב֗וֹת תַּבְנִ֥ית הֵיכָֽל׃
May our barns be full, supplying every kind of produce; may our flocks increase by thousands, by tens of thousands in our fields.
מְזָוֵ֣ינוּ מְלֵאִים֮ מְפִיקִ֥ים מִזַּ֗ן אֶ֫ל־זַ֥ן צֹאונֵ֣נוּ מַ֭אֲלִיפוֹת מְרֻבָּב֗וֹת בְּחוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ׃
May our cattle be heavy with young;[^11] may there be no breach in the walls, no going into exile,[^12] and no cry of distress in our streets.
אַלּוּפֵ֗ינוּ מְֽסֻבָּ֫לִ֥ים אֵֽין־פֶּ֭רֶץ וְאֵ֣ין יוֹצֵ֑את וְאֵ֥ין צְ֝וָחָ֗ה בִּרְחֹבֹתֵֽינוּ׃
Happy[^13] are the people for whom it is so; happy are the people whose God is the LORD!
אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם שֶׁכָּ֣כָה לּ֑וֹ אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י הָ֝עָ֗ם שֶׁיֲהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

n.1: *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles. Verses 1–11 draw on many lines of Psalm 18 (compare 18:3, 10, 15, 17, 35, 48; 18:2, 9, 14, 16, 34, 47 in most English Bibles).
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *chasdi*, "my *chesed*" (loyal, faithful love): the God who shows me faithful love.
n.4: Some Hebrew manuscripts read "who subdues peoples under me", as in 18:48 (18:47 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Literally "a son of *enosh* (mortal)". Compare 8:5 (8:4 in most English Bibles).
n.6: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor", the word of Ecclesiastes 1:2.
n.7: The right hand was raised to swear an oath: their oaths are false.
n.8: Literally "the evil sword". Verse 10 continues verse 9: the song is sung to the one who gives victory to kings.
n.9: Literally "That our sons...". The Hebrew links verses 12–14 to what goes before with the word *asher*, "which, that", in an unclear way. Or "Then our sons will be like plants".
n.10: Or "for a temple". Hebrew *heikhal*.
n.11: Or "May our oxen be well laden". Hebrew *alluf*, "ox, cow".
n.12: Literally "no breach and no going out". Or, continuing the picture of the cattle, "no miscarriage and no untimely birth".
n.13: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed". Also in the next line.

v: A song of praise. Of David.[^1] I will exalt you, my God the King, and bless your name forever and ever.[^2]
תְּהִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד אֲרוֹמִמְךָ֣ אֱלוֹהַ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲבָרֲכָ֥ה שִׁ֝מְךָ֗ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and ever.
בְּכָל־י֥וֹם אֲבָרֲכֶ֑ךָּ וַאֲהַלְלָ֥ה שִׁ֝מְךָ֗ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
Great is the LORD,[^3] and most worthy of praise; his greatness is beyond searching out.
גָּ֘ד֤וֹל יְהוָ֣ה וּמְהֻלָּ֣ל מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝לִגְדֻלָּת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃
One generation will commend your works to another; they will tell of your mighty acts.
דּ֣וֹר לְ֭דוֹר יְשַׁבַּ֣ח מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וּגְב֖וּרֹתֶ֣יךָ יַגִּֽידוּ׃
On the glorious splendor of your majesty and on your wonderful works[^4] I will meditate.
הֲ֭דַר כְּב֣וֹד הוֹדֶ֑ךָ וְדִבְרֵ֖י נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֣יךָ אָשִֽׂיחָה׃
They will speak of the power of your awesome deeds, and I will tell of your greatness.[^5]
וֶעֱז֣וּז נוֹרְאֹתֶ֣יךָ יֹאמֵ֑רוּ *וגדולתיך **וּגְדוּלָּתְךָ֥ אֲסַפְּרֶֽנָּה׃
