They will pour out the memory of your abundant goodness[^6] and sing joyfully of your righteousness.
זֵ֣כֶר רַב־טוּבְךָ֣ יַבִּ֑יעוּ וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
The LORD is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and great in faithful love.[^7]
חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֣וּם יְהוָ֑ה אֶ֥רֶךְ אַ֝פַּ֗יִם וּגְדָל־חָֽסֶד׃
The LORD is good to all, and his compassion is over all that he has made.
טוֹב־יְהוָ֥ה לַכֹּ֑ל וְ֝רַחֲמָ֗יו עַל־כָּל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃
All your works will give thanks to you, LORD, and your faithful ones[^8] will bless you.
יוֹד֣וּךָ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂ֑יךָ וַ֝חֲסִידֶ֗יךָ יְבָרֲכֽוּכָה׃
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and talk of your might,
כְּב֣וֹד מַלְכוּתְךָ֣ יֹאמֵ֑רוּ וּגְבוּרָתְךָ֥ יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃
to make known to human beings[^9] his mighty acts, and the glorious splendor of his kingdom.
לְהוֹדִ֤יעַ ׀ לִבְנֵ֣י הָ֭אָדָם גְּבוּרֹתָ֑יו וּ֝כְב֗וֹד הֲדַ֣ר מַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion endures through all generations.[^10]
מַֽלְכוּתְךָ֗ מַלְכ֥וּת כָּל־עֹֽלָמִ֑ים וּ֝מֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֗ בְּכָל־דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃
The LORD upholds all who fall, and raises up all who are bowed down.
סוֹמֵ֣ךְ יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־הַנֹּפְלִ֑ים וְ֝זוֹקֵ֗ף לְכָל־הַכְּפוּפִֽים׃
The eyes of all look to you, and you give them their food at the proper time.
עֵֽינֵי־כֹ֭ל אֵלֶ֣יךָ יְשַׂבֵּ֑רוּ וְאַתָּ֤ה נֽוֹתֵן־לָהֶ֖ם אֶת־אָכְלָ֣ם בְּעִתּֽוֹ׃
You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
פּוֹתֵ֥חַ אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ וּמַשְׂבִּ֖יעַ לְכָל־חַ֣י רָצֽוֹן׃
The LORD is righteous in all his ways and faithful[^11] in all his deeds.
צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֑יו וְ֝חָסִ֗יד בְּכָל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃
The LORD is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃
He fulfills the desire of those who fear him; he hears their cry and saves them.
רְצוֹן־יְרֵאָ֥יו יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְֽאֶת־שַׁוְעָתָ֥ם יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע וְיוֹשִׁיעֵֽם׃
The LORD watches over all who love him, but all the wicked he will destroy.
שׁוֹמֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה אֶת־כָּל־אֹהֲבָ֑יו וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־הָרְשָׁעִ֣ים יַשְׁמִֽיד׃
My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and let every creature[^12] bless his holy name forever and ever.
תְּהִלַּ֥ת יְהוָ֗ה יְֽדַבֶּ֫ר פִּ֥י וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ כָּל־בָּ֭שָׂר שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשׁ֗וֹ לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃

n.1: *A song of praise*: Hebrew *tehillah*, "praise", the word that gives the book its Hebrew name, *Tehillim*, "Praises". This is the only psalm with this title. *Of David*: or "for David", "about David". In the Hebrew text the title is part of verse 1. In this psalm it shares the verse with the first line, so the verse numbers match English Bibles.
n.2: Psalm 145 is an acrostic: in the Hebrew, each verse begins with the next letter of the alphabet, from *aleph* (verse 1) to *tav* (verse 21). There is no verse for *nun* (see the note on verse 13).
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "the words (or matters) of your wonders".
n.5: The Hebrew text is written "your great deeds" but read "your greatness".
n.6: That is, tell of it eagerly, like water bubbling from a spring. Literally "They will pour out the memory of the abundance of your goodness".
n.7: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. The line repeats God's description of himself in Exodus 34:6 (compare 86:15; 103:8).
n.8: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.9: Literally "to the sons of *adam* (humankind)". *His mighty acts*: the Hebrew turns here from speaking to God ("your") to speaking of him ("his").
n.10: In the Hebrew text there is no verse for the letter *nun*, which should come between verses 13 and 14. A Dead Sea Scroll (11QPs-a) has one: "God is faithful in his words, and faithful (*chasid*) in all his deeds." The Septuagint has the same line, with "the Lord" for "God". Its second half is the same as verse 17b. Compare also Daniel 3:33 (4:3 in most English Bibles).
n.11: Hebrew *chasid*, "faithful, loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love".
n.12: Literally "all flesh".

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Praise the LORD,[^2] my soul![^3]
הַֽלְלוּ־יָ֡הּ הַלְלִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
I will praise the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praises to my God while I have being.[^4]
אֲהַלְלָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה בְּחַיָּ֑י אֲזַמְּרָ֖ה לֵֽאלֹהַ֣י בְּעוֹדִֽי׃
Do not put your trust in nobles, in a mortal,[^5] who cannot save.
אַל־תִּבְטְח֥וּ בִנְדִיבִ֑ים בְּבֶן־אָדָ֓ם ׀ שֶׁ֤אֵֽין ל֥וֹ תְשׁוּעָֽה׃
When his breath departs, he returns to his ground;[^6] on that very day his plans perish.
תֵּצֵ֣א ר֭וּחוֹ יָשֻׁ֣ב לְאַדְמָת֑וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַ֝ה֗וּא אָבְד֥וּ עֶשְׁתֹּנֹתָֽיו׃
Happy[^7] is the one whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God,
אַשְׁרֵ֗י שֶׁ֤אֵ֣ל יַעֲקֹ֣ב בְּעֶזְר֑וֹ שִׂ֝בְר֗וֹ עַל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
the maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, who keeps faith forever,[^8]
עֹשֶׂ֤ה ׀ שָׁ֘מַ֤יִם וָאָ֗רֶץ אֶת־הַיָּ֥ם וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑ם הַשֹּׁמֵ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת לְעוֹלָֽם׃
who brings about justice for the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets the prisoners free;
עֹשֶׂ֤ה מִשְׁפָּ֨ט ׀ לָעֲשׁוּקִ֗ים נֹתֵ֣ן לֶ֭חֶם לָרְעֵבִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה מַתִּ֥יר אֲסוּרִֽים׃
the LORD opens the eyes of the blind; the LORD raises up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
יְהוָ֤ה ׀ פֹּ֘קֵ֤חַ עִוְרִ֗ים יְ֭הוָה זֹקֵ֣ף כְּפוּפִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה אֹהֵ֥ב צַדִּיקִֽים׃
The LORD watches over the foreigners;[^9] he upholds the orphan and the widow, but he twists the way of the wicked.[^10]
יְהוָ֤ה ׀ שֹׁ֘מֵ֤ר אֶת־גֵּרִ֗ים יָת֣וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֣ה יְעוֹדֵ֑ד וְדֶ֖רֶךְ רְשָׁעִ֣ים יְעַוֵּֽת׃
The LORD will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation. Praise the LORD!
יִמְלֹ֤ךְ יְהוָ֨ה ׀ לְעוֹלָ֗ם אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִ֭יּוֹן לְדֹ֥ר וָדֹ֗ר הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 10. Each of the last five psalms (146–150) begins and ends with this call.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *nephesh*: soul, life, self. The psalmist speaks to his own soul, as in 103:1 and 104:1.
n.4: Literally "while I am still".
n.5: Literally "in a son of *adam* (humankind)".
n.6: Hebrew *adamah*, "ground", which sounds like *adam*, "humankind" (compare Genesis 2:7; 3:19). *His breath*: or "his spirit". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.7: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.8: Literally "who keeps faithfulness (*emet*) forever". Acts 4:24 and 14:15 echo the first line of this verse.
n.9: Hebrew *gerim*, foreigners living in a land not their own, who like orphans and widows had no family to protect them (Deuteronomy 10:18).
n.10: That is, he makes it lead to ruin.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and praise is fitting.
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ כִּי־ט֭וֹב זַמְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ כִּֽי־נָ֝עִים נָאוָ֥ה תְהִלָּֽה׃
The LORD[^2] builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel.[^3]
בּוֹנֵ֣ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֣͏ִם יְהוָ֑ה נִדְחֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל יְכַנֵּֽס׃
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
הָ֭רֹפֵא לִשְׁב֣וּרֵי לֵ֑ב וּ֝מְחַבֵּ֗שׁ לְעַצְּבוֹתָֽם׃
He counts the number of the stars; he gives names to all of them.[^4]
מוֹנֶ֣ה מִ֭סְפָּר לַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים לְ֝כֻלָּ֗ם שֵׁמ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽא׃
Great is our Lord, and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond measure.[^5]
גָּד֣וֹל אֲדוֹנֵ֣ינוּ וְרַב־כֹּ֑חַ לִ֝תְבוּנָת֗וֹ אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃
The LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked down to the ground.
מְעוֹדֵ֣ד עֲנָוִ֣ים יְהוָ֑ה מַשְׁפִּ֖יל רְשָׁעִ֣ים עֲדֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make music to our God on the lyre.
עֱנ֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה בְּתוֹדָ֑ה זַמְּר֖וּ לֵאלֹהֵ֣ינוּ בְכִנּֽוֹר׃
He covers the heavens with clouds; he prepares rain for the earth; he makes grass grow on the mountains.[^6]
הַֽמְכַסֶּ֬ה שָׁמַ֨יִם ׀ בְּעָבִ֗ים הַמֵּכִ֣ין לָאָ֣רֶץ מָטָ֑ר הַמַּצְמִ֖יחַ הָרִ֣ים חָצִֽיר׃
He gives the animals their food, and the young ravens when they call.
נוֹתֵ֣ן לִבְהֵמָ֣ה לַחְמָ֑הּ לִבְנֵ֥י עֹ֝רֵ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִקְרָֽאוּ׃
He takes no delight in the strength of the horse, no pleasure in the legs of a warrior.[^7]
לֹ֤א בִגְבוּרַ֣ת הַסּ֣וּס יֶחְפָּ֑ץ לֹֽא־בְשׁוֹקֵ֖י הָאִ֣ישׁ יִרְצֶֽה׃
The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his faithful love.[^8]
רוֹצֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־יְרֵאָ֑יו אֶת־הַֽמְיַחֲלִ֥ים לְחַסְדּֽוֹ׃
Extol the LORD, Jerusalem! Praise your God, Zion![^9]
שַׁבְּחִ֣י יְ֭רוּשָׁלִַם אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה הַֽלְלִ֖י אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִיּֽוֹן׃
For he has strengthened the bars of your gates; he has blessed your children within you.
כִּֽי־חִ֭זַּק בְּרִיחֵ֣י שְׁעָרָ֑יִךְ בֵּרַ֖ךְ בָּנַ֣יִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּֽךְ׃
He grants peace within your borders; he satisfies you with the finest wheat.[^10]
הַשָּׂם־גְּבוּלֵ֥ךְ שָׁל֑וֹם חֵ֥לֶב חִ֝טִּ֗ים יַשְׂבִּיעֵֽךְ׃
He sends out his word[^11] to the earth; his word runs swiftly.
הַשֹּׁלֵ֣חַ אִמְרָת֣וֹ אָ֑רֶץ עַד־מְ֝הֵרָ֗ה יָר֥וּץ דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
He gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes.
הַנֹּתֵ֣ן שֶׁ֣לֶג כַּצָּ֑מֶר כְּ֝פ֗וֹר כָּאֵ֥פֶר יְפַזֵּֽר׃
He hurls down his hail like crumbs. Who can stand before his cold?
מַשְׁלִ֣יךְ קַֽרְח֣וֹ כְפִתִּ֑ים לִפְנֵ֥י קָ֝רָת֗וֹ מִ֣י יַעֲמֹֽד׃
He sends out his word and melts them; he makes his wind blow, and the waters flow.
יִשְׁלַ֣ח דְּבָר֣וֹ וְיַמְסֵ֑ם יַשֵּׁ֥ב ר֝וּח֗וֹ יִזְּלוּ־מָֽיִם׃
He declares his words[^12] to Jacob, his decrees and his rulings to Israel.
מַגִּ֣יד *דברו **דְּבָרָ֣יו לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב חֻקָּ֥יו וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטָ֗יו לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
He has not done this for any other nation; they do not know his rulings. Praise the LORD!
לֹ֘א עָ֤שָׂה כֵ֨ן ׀ לְכָל־גּ֗וֹי וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֥ים בַּל־יְדָע֗וּם הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 20.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: That is, the exiles who had been scattered (compare Isaiah 11:12; 56:8).
n.4: Literally "he calls names to all of them". Compare Isaiah 40:26.
n.5: Literally "there is no number to his understanding".
n.6: The Septuagint adds "and plants for the service of human beings", as in 104:14.
n.7: Literally "the legs of the man": the strength of a runner or a soldier.
n.8: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.9: The Septuagint begins a new psalm here, so that verses 1–11 and 12–20 are two psalms (see the note on 114:1).
n.10: Literally "the fat of wheat".
n.11: Hebrew *imrah*, "saying, word", translated "promise" in Psalm 119. The second "word" in this verse is Hebrew *davar*.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "his word" but read "his words".

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Praise the LORD[^2] from the heavens; praise him in the heights!
הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ ׀ הַֽלְל֣וּ אֶת־יְ֭הוָה מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֑יִם הֽ͏ַ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בַּמְּרוֹמִֽים׃
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his armies![^3]
הֽ͏ַלְל֥וּהוּ כָל־מַלְאָכָ֑יו הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ כָּל־*צבאו **צְבָאָֽיו׃
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all you shining stars!
הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ שֶׁ֣מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֑חַ הַ֝לְל֗וּהוּ כָּל־כּ֥וֹכְבֵי אֽוֹר׃
Praise him, you highest heavens,[^4] and you waters above the heavens!
הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ שְׁמֵ֣י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ֝הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר ׀ מֵעַ֬ל הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for he commanded, and they were created.
יְֽ֭הַֽלְלוּ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צִוָּ֣ה וְנִבְרָֽאוּ׃
He established them forever and ever; he gave a decree that will not pass away.[^5]
וַיַּעֲמִידֵ֣ם לָעַ֣ד לְעוֹלָ֑ם חָק־נָ֝תַ֗ן וְלֹ֣א יַעֲבֽוֹר׃
Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea monsters[^6] and all the depths,
הַֽלְל֣וּ אֶת־יְ֭הוָה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ תַּ֝נִּינִ֗ים וְכָל־תְּהֹמֽוֹת׃
fire and hail, snow and mist,[^7] stormy wind that carries out his word,
אֵ֣שׁ וּ֭בָרָד שֶׁ֣לֶג וְקִיט֑וֹר ר֥וּחַ סְ֝עָרָ֗ה עֹשָׂ֥ה דְבָרֽוֹ׃
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
הֶהָרִ֥ים וְכָל־גְּבָע֑וֹת עֵ֥ץ פְּ֝רִ֗י וְכָל־אֲרָזִֽים׃
wild animals and all livestock, creatures that move along the ground and winged birds,
הַֽחַיָּ֥ה וְכָל־בְּהֵמָ֑ה רֶ֝֗מֶשׂ וְצִפּ֥וֹר כָּנָֽף׃
kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all who rule the earth,[^8]
מַלְכֵי־אֶ֭רֶץ וְכָל־לְאֻמִּ֑ים שָׂ֝רִ֗ים וְכָל־שֹׁ֥פְטֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
young men and young women alike, old and young together.
בַּחוּרִ֥ים וְגַם־בְּתוּל֑וֹת זְ֝קֵנִ֗ים עִם־נְעָרֽ͏ִים׃
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his splendor is above the earth and the heavens.
יְהַלְל֤וּ ׀ אֶת־שֵׁ֬ם יְהוָ֗ה כִּֽי־נִשְׂגָּ֣ב שְׁמ֣וֹ לְבַדּ֑וֹ ה֝וֹד֗וֹ עַל־אֶ֥רֶץ וְשָׁמָֽיִם׃
He has raised up a horn[^9] for his people, praise for all his faithful ones,[^10] for the Israelites, the people close to him. Praise the LORD!
וַיָּ֤רֶם קֶ֨רֶן ׀ לְעַמּ֡וֹ תְּהִלָּ֤ה לְֽכָל־חֲסִידָ֗יו לִבְנֵ֣י יִ֭שְׂרָאֵל עַֽם־קְרֹב֗וֹ הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 14.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: The heavenly hosts (compare "the LORD of Armies", 24:10). The Hebrew text is written "his army" but read "his armies".
n.4: Literally "heavens of the heavens". *The waters above the heavens*: compare Genesis 1:7.
n.5: Or "a decree that they will not transgress". Compare Jeremiah 31:35–36; 33:25.
n.6: Hebrew *tanninim*, the great creatures of the sea (Genesis 1:21).
n.7: Or "smoke". Hebrew *qitor*.
n.8: Literally "all judges of the earth".
n.9: A symbol of strength. Perhaps a king for his people, or their strength and honor restored (compare 89:18; 89:17 in most English Bibles; 132:17).
n.10: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". *Praise for all his faithful ones*: either a reason for them to praise, or their glory.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Sing to the LORD[^2] a new song, his praise in the assembly of the faithful.[^3]
הַ֥לְלוּיָ֨הּ ׀ שִׁ֣ירוּ לַֽ֭יהוָה שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֑שׁ תְּ֝הִלָּת֗וֹ בִּקְהַ֥ל חֲסִידִֽים׃
Let Israel rejoice in their Maker; let the people of Zion[^4] be glad in their King.
יִשְׂמַ֣ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל בְּעֹשָׂ֑יו בְּנֵֽי־צִ֝יּ֗וֹן יָגִ֥ילוּ בְמַלְכָּֽם׃
Let them praise his name with dancing; let them make music to him with tambourine and lyre.
יְהַֽלְל֣וּ שְׁמ֣וֹ בְמָח֑וֹל בְּתֹ֥ף וְ֝כִנּ֗וֹר יְזַמְּרוּ־לֽוֹ׃
For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he crowns the humble with salvation.[^5]
כִּֽי־רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה בְּעַמּ֑וֹ יְפָאֵ֥ר עֲ֝נָוִ֗ים בִּישׁוּעָֽה׃
Let the faithful exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.[^6]
יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים בְּכָב֑וֹד יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָֽם׃
Let the high praises of God be in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands,
רוֹמְמ֣וֹת אֵ֭ל בִּגְרוֹנָ֑ם וְחֶ֖רֶב פִּֽיפִיּ֣וֹת בְּיָדָֽם׃
to carry out vengeance on the nations, punishment on the peoples,
לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת נְ֭קָמָה בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם תּֽ֝וֹכֵחֹ֗ת בַּל־אֻמִּֽים׃
to bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron,
לֶאְסֹ֣ר מַלְכֵיהֶ֣ם בְּזִקִּ֑ים וְ֝נִכְבְּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּכַבְלֵ֥י בַרְזֶֽל׃
to carry out on them the judgment written.[^7] This is the honor of all his faithful ones. Praise the LORD!
לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת בָּהֶ֨ם ׀ מִשְׁפָּ֬ט כָּת֗וּב הָדָ֣ר ה֭וּא לְכָל־חֲסִידָ֗יו הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 9.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *chasidim*, "the faithful, the loyal", related to *chesed*, "faithful love". Also in verses 5 and 9.
n.4: Literally "the sons of Zion".
n.5: Or "he adorns the humble with victory".
n.6: Perhaps the mats or couches on which they lay down to rest, or reclined at a festival meal.
n.7: Perhaps the judgment on the nations written down in the prophets' oracles, or in God's own decrees.

v: Praise the LORD![^1] Praise God in his sanctuary;[^2] praise him in the mighty dome of the sky![^3]
הַ֥לְלוּיָ֨הּ ׀ הַֽלְלוּ־אֵ֥ל בְּקָדְשׁ֑וֹ הֽ͏ַ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בִּרְקִ֥יעַ עֻזּֽוֹ׃
Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him for his surpassing greatness![^4]
הַֽלְל֥וּהוּ בִגְבוּרֹתָ֑יו הֽ͏ַ֝לְל֗וּהוּ כְּרֹ֣ב גֻּדְלֽוֹ׃
Praise him with the blast of the ram's horn;[^5] praise him with harp and lyre!
הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ בְּתֵ֣קַע שׁוֹפָ֑ר הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בְּנֵ֣בֶל וְכִנּֽוֹר׃
Praise him with tambourine and dancing; praise him with strings and pipe!
הַֽ֭לְלוּהוּ בְּתֹ֣ף וּמָח֑וֹל הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בְּמִנִּ֥ים וְעוּגָֽב׃
Praise him with clashing cymbals; praise him with resounding cymbals![^6]
הַֽלְל֥וּהוּ בְצִלְצְלֵי־שָׁ֑מַע הַֽ֝לְל֗וּהוּ בְּֽצִלְצְלֵ֥י תְרוּעָֽה׃
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD![^7]
כֹּ֣ל הַ֭נְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּ֥ל יָ֗הּ הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *hallelu-yah*, "praise Yah", the source of the word "Hallelujah". *Yah* is a short form of the name YHWH. Also at the end of verse 6.
n.2: Or "in his holiness". Hebrew *qodesh*, "holiness, holy place": the temple on earth, or God's dwelling in heaven.
n.3: Literally "in the dome of his strength". Hebrew *raqia*, the sky pictured as a solid vault (Genesis 1:6–8; see 19:2).
n.4: Literally "according to the abundance of his greatness".
n.5: Hebrew *shofar*.
n.6: Literally "cymbals of sound" and "cymbals of loud shouting": perhaps two kinds of cymbals, or two ways of sounding them.
n.7: Psalm 150 closes Book 5 of the Psalms (Psalms 107–150) and the whole book. Each of the other four books ends with a blessing (41:14; 72:18–19; 89:53; 106:48; 41:13 and 89:52 in most English Bibles); here the whole psalm is the closing call to praise, and the last five psalms (146–150) each begin and end with "Praise Yah". The Septuagint adds a short Psalm 151, spoken by David about his victory over Goliath, and a longer Hebrew form of it is found in a Dead Sea Scroll (11QPs-a).
